I was very skeptical for the future of this game while I was playing it in closed beta, it was always kind of empty and the lack of contents was hitting very hard.
But with the official release of the game, I tried it again and... I was surprised! It was (and is) full of life now and it's incredibly relaxing, peaceful and funny to roam, explore, search and move around with a friendly group of other cute animals.
Everything is so quiet and soothing, the complete lack of real communication is just beautiful as it's beautiful that the game make you communicate with simple adorable emoticons, sounds and body movements. No toxic people, not shiz talking, no offences, no griefing... is like you are not even playing with people! And that is wonderful for me.
Most of the players that I've meet were very helpful, kind and would always wait for the slower animals before breaking an essence stone, call for them for regrouping and even run back if they were momentarily lost.
The graphics are the same of the past Shelter games and that is a good thing for me, cause I really loved their artistic decisions, and everything makes you think you're playing in a living finely painted canvas. There are also many wonderful biomes, climates, night/day cicles and the music is really super sweet and relaxing as well.
It really is an unique game and if you like animals, playing in your own peace and exploring peacefully, then you can buy it, it's worh it for the money they're asking :)
I just have Shelter 2, but I haven't find the game so limitated for who doesn't own all the other Might and Delight games, the other free animals you unlock are incredibly cute aswell: the frog, the rabbit, the goat! Oh I love the goat! But before I'll play her I want to unlock all the skins for my adorable lynx :P
By the way, I really hope they put up some servers where you can play kind of survival where you have to eat and drink to survive, even without pvp, we could only hunt npc animals maybe :P

Firstly, this game isn't an Unturned clone.  They're both zombie survival games.  This game is based of the Crafting Dead MODPACK for Minecraft.
Secondly, I received this game for free in a Twitch giveaway, but that won't affect my opinion on the game.  I think you'll be able to tell I like the game by the fact I have nearly 30 hours on it within 2 weeks of getting the key.
The game is pretty damn good for being an early access title made by one person.  It has a working singleplayer and multiplayer.  Singleplayer is perfect if you want to just relax, chill, and kill zombies without the worry of players.  Multiplayer is obviously perfect for interacting with others, making new friends, and having some fun PvP moments.
Pros:
Game is a cheap $10 (Removes pay2win aspect from the modpack and easy access for annoying kids)
Has singleplayer and multiplayer
Well optimized
Graphics aren't obnoxious
Map is decent size and easy to learn
No VOIP
Cons:
No VOIP
(Can't think of anymore, because any cons I have are just stuff that aren't in the game yet but will be soon)
Please, remember this game is in early access.  Know what you're getting into when you purchase.  Bugs are expected.

Neo Scavenger is one of those rouge-like games that comes off shallow with it's RNG "BS" and makes you feel like a toddler at first, but dont be fooled. After you gain some experiance and live for longer than a couple days you will realize how much depth all these interlocking systems have. The writing+ art + music is charming and at times can even give you one of the deepest feelings of hopelessness and lonesomeness only a realistic post-epoch game can give you. Its simple art style compliments the intense inventory management and crafting systems.
My advice? Go in blind your first couple games until you get one long life. When that game eventually ends, crack open the wiki and start to really take advantage of every gameplay system. Pick the traits you think have the most benefits/crafting recipes, always look up the outcomes of random encounters, exploit the movement system (0.15 moves wont make you another spear, but it will let you move 1 more hex). You will get to see a lot of the game this way but just remember even with some of the best gear in the game, in the wrong conditions, one mistake can end your life.
PSA: The dev is working on a MOBILE port! Very much looking forward to that :)

I don't really recommend this. It was billed as a RTS with an emphasis on the scale of the battles and ships. Of how customizable the ships are, and so on/so forth. Except there isn't any real scale to the battles, or depth to the mechanics, and the customizability is pretty limited(in campaign at least)
AI isn't very intelligent. Your ships will maneuver like idiots and ram eachother if you don't micromanage them, and often times their too slow to be able to catch anything thats gone out of range anyway.
As a whole, the game plays like Rebellion(really really old star wars turn based strategy) and you go into missions with your fleet a certain number of times per turn. The missions are either stupidly easy (protect the data, you just run for 2 minutes and then jump) Or stupidly impossible(prevent planetary bombardment? HA)
the missions themselves take 4-5 minutes usually, and thats if you get them right, there is no quicksave or quickload system, so you have to return to the main menu if♥♥♥♥♥♥is not going well to reload and try again.
There are many upgrades for your ships, however they're slight upgrades and you won't really see a major difference between a ship with an extra shield or one with armor piercing ammo.
Nitpicks everywhere. No fleet formations, no tactics for the ships other than attack or don't and which range. a frigate plays exactly the same as a battlecruiser. not to mention the low as ♥♥♥♥ unit cap the campaign limits you to.
The game also tends to crash on me. Though i've played 7 hours, I've managed to have it crash 4 times completely randomly. Usually in battles, but not consistantly.
Finally, i realize the universe of WH4k is supposed to be 'gothic' and i've even played other games before without a problem, but i can't help but be annoyed by the pompous cliche jackasses who are my characters 'superiors'

Excellent software, I've been using it for slightly over 2 years now, and switched over to steam so I could keep track of the time I spend in it. While there are other 3D programs you can get to use free, like maya, you have to use those under student or learning licenses, and cannot monitize your creations. overall, there is nothing you can do in maya or 3dsmax that you cannot do in blender.
the good, the bad, the ugly:
the good:
•beyond the core of blender, which is c++, the interface and everything is python coded, so those with the desire or ability can quickly learn to add functionality or scripting to automate tedious tasks.
•Being open source there is a large community that can help with any problems or questions, and numerous youtube tutorials exist.
•blender wraps functionality of 3D design/editing, rendering, sculpting, video editing, and even a game engine into itself.
•once you get used to it the left click 3D cursor (little aiming reticle that exists on the screen) is extremely useful for number of tasks.
the bad:
•if your goal is to learn methodology and skills in 3D modeling then the program is great. however if your goal is to indicate on a resume you have experiance with a specific modeling program your going to have a tougher time. blender is not one of the 'industry standard' programs and thus if you join a team or employeer you may find yourself spending a good chunk of time relearning interfaces and retraining muscle memory to work in specific software they want you in.
the ugly:
• the UI is unique to blender. expect a learning curve. everything is designed with shortcuts in mind and it takes time to learn them. however if you take the time to learn and become accostumed to the layout tasks are very streamlined in general.
•if you run blender through steam look up a tutorial on how to migrate settings and customizations between versions. this ones one steam; with no way to prevent automatic updates for specific programs when blender updates it will create a new folder for user preferences when the version number changes. doesn't happen too often, once a year maybe, but be aware this is something you may encounter, but can overcome.

Right, so first things first, if that trailer doesn't make you feel insaaaaaaane then.... well, actually, thats understandable. Zero Gear is probably one of the funniest racing games I have ever played. I have never played a mario kart game in my life, due to the fact I own nothing intendo, but I have always wanted to play one. I found this waaaaaaaay back when they had a free weekend of this to promote their game, and I gave it a go. I will never regret that day.
I had soooo much fun online, back when it worked, and I pooped in my pants every once in a while because I laughed so hard. Now days I don't do that so much, but i still manage a fart whenever I play this game.
The tracks are awesome, some better than others. The racing is the best. The AI is top notch. The vehicle customisation is state-of-the-art. And the PHYSICS in this game is far more advanced than the physics that occupy this world currently. I mean, how many times can you slightly nudge your friend ever-so-lightly on the back of his car, THEN HE FLIPS, AND CRIES, AND ♥♥♥♥♥ ALL IN THE SAME SWIFT MOVEMENT?!?! that's right, you can't, but this game makes it possible.
Now, I dont write a lot of reviews, so, you can trust me on this. Zero Gear is where I have had most of my laughs in gaming. This game does not work correctly with xinput gamepads. The button placement will be mixed up, and it is not possible to fix the controls for xinput gamepads with the in game options.

The developers are very very anti modding. If you're going to buy this game because you think mods will save it wait a few months to see just how far they will go to shut down modders.
The DLC available for this game is ridiculously over priced. There are currently four packs available in the store at the time of me writing this review. Even the cheapest DLC pack will cost you more than the price of the base game, and altogether cost over $200(not including the cost of the base game).
There are features missing from this version that are available in the console versions. I won't go into detail about this since the other reviewers have mentioned it enough.
There has been almost no communication from TK aside from their negative statements about modders.
I can't recommend this game because of the above issues, but if you really must buy it I would suggest waiting for it to go on sale.

So after around 25 hours of playtime I feel I've got a decent grasp of the current EA status of the game. I'm no where near a god at this game so I wont pretend to be, however, I can give a few potential investors a heads up on what to expect..
You will die, it happens, and you're probably going to do it alot but it gets better, the more time you spend harvesting, crafting, building, and all the other little things the game lets you do the easier it gets. I'm currently sitting at level 18 playing with 2 friends. We rolled on a low population US Official Server to avoid griefers and so far we've done well. We set our house up, have tons of chests, weapons, materials, and all kinds of other things set up already. It is fun, but it's also frustrating at times.
It's a Survival Sandbox, one thing I will say is from looking around the web the developers are more vocal than I expected, even though they're slightly cryptic they do see to communicate at least moderately well with the community and they are definitely taking public opinion into consideration when it comes to certain mechanics.
If you're in the US and you're reading this, don't be afraid to buy the game. Don't let the negative reviews get to you, it's definitely worth the price tag and when the product is finished I'd say it will be every bit as popular as Ark as far as Survival Games go. There are bugs, and glitches, just little problems. But nothing I would truly call game breaking.  The majority of the negative reviews (and you can google this) came from Chinese Players that flooded the servers as soon as they opened and then cried when it wasn't the perfect polished game they wanted. It's hard, it's rough, and it takes planning and precision. If thats the kind of game that turns you on this buy it, work at it, and enjoy the hell out of it. Every action you do in game helps with leveling up and as soon as you can craft a Bow and Arrows get out there and start killing anything you think you can take on. You'll get lots of experience far faster than just crafting and harvesting. Which will unlock the ability to unlock the ability to craft more things. Yes there are Level and Skill Requirements, you need to be level 20 to unlock learning the ability, and then you need to perform the corresponding actions to unlock the ability. I enjoy that, because each action feels like progress.
Anyways, disregard the majority of the negative reviews, this game would have gotten a much better start if it weren't for Chinese Flooding, find a low pop server or a private server and come enjoy the ground floor. Beautiful graphics if you've got the machine to run it, a great challenge, and decent customisation. Plus a big bug fix patch coming in the next week or so we'll make it even more attractive.

First of all, about the missing features in the PC version that most of the people are complaining about, like the missing Soft skin Engine or the missing 2 new Stages, I myself have no problem with these missing stuff since it was never promised that we will have them in the PC version. I bought the game because I accepted this.
Short Pro/Con Summary
Pros:
+A good port. Runs even smooth on low end systems.
+Still a rare genre on PC (Fighting games).
+Base game already contains a lot of different costumes compared to other fighting games.
+Decent graphics (even with that missing next gen features it still looks good).
+Decent gameplay (if you like the style of course).
+Sex appeal.
Cons:
-Ridiculous DLC policy. (There are already 4 costume packs that costs 241.- Euro, and more will follow....)
-Missing online support has to be patched in within few months after release.
-No trading cards.
-No archivements.
-The official system requirement informations are far away from the real requirements. (Runs well on far lower systems)
-Clothes are frequently bugged while fighting.
-Critical savefile bug (maybe intended I don't know) that is bound to your Steam username.
Impression:
If you can live with the missing features the next gen consoles have, and also if you can live without being able to play online (at the moment), in that case, I have to say that this game is a decent fighting game.
But be aware, if you are used to the combat style of the Street Fighters series or the King of Fighters, DOA plays totally different, since its more important to press your buttons in the right combination and order to activate combos, instead of pressing like ↓→ + punch button to activate skills in other games. Since this was my first DOA game I played since 2005 or so, I had to get used to it's style once again.
Included are a lot of hot virtual babes.... And I think they look better than girls on any other fighting games avalable on PC at the moment. But yeah I think you knew this already.....
There is also a story mode, that is not to long, but also not to short, and it really helps you to know a bit about the characters of DOA. The story mode works like the one in Mortal Kombat 9, where you switch between characters while playing through it.
So, what else do you get with this game? To be honest, the problem with any fighting game nowadays without online support is, you get bored fast.... So all you can do while waiting for the online patch is playing the solo/tag arcade mode to unlock all those avalable costumes, or practicing in practice mode or tutorials to be ready when online mode is there.
About the DLCs..... I think KT imagines people like this. A horny teenager boy asks his father "Dad, I really need like 250 bucks to change clothes for my half naked virtual girls!" Dad says "Of course my son, just give me a min I need to poop that money fast, brb".....
So at the moment I have to say, if you are a big fan of playing offline games using cute girls, then this might be something for you, but if not, just pass by and wait for a sale or the online patch first.

Dark and Light is the experience that I wanted from ARK but never got, finally being the game that properly merges survival and fantasy genres. The game is tough and forces you to work hard to fight the environment, unlike a lot of survival games that have a negligible PvE experience resulting in rampant KoSing just to have fun. The skill system is much improved over ARK's, with no skill points to spend you can truly master everything if you put the time into it. The map is huge and beautiful, teeming with diverse fantasy wildlife.
There are issues with the game. Namely, many people seem to be having serious performance issues. There is also some lag when harvesting resources which makes the game frustrating at times, like when you just want 1 wood but have to spend minutes waiting for the server to catch up. The game also suffers from the experience gap that ARK had where if you're a high level, you can just easily stomp over everyone lower than you due to having flying mounts, way better armor, and top-tier spells. Luckily, it seems like because of the difficulty of the game compared to other survivals, high level players are more willing to help you than hurt you. Overall, I highly recommend Dark and Light if you enjoy survival or fantasy games; it had a solid launch and is full of content, but still suffers from many of the problems that Early Access games tend to have (server lag, optimization).

Things should be considered for deciding to pick this game :

3/ Lacking of 2 arenas and soft engine. To be fair, there's enough arenas for a solid game and boobs engine is useless as you can't focus on breast while fighting ; and boobs are already insanely defying all gravity even in "natural mode".
Soft engine couldn't be put on PC as it requires motion sensitive pad (boobs are actually moving as you move the pad on PS4).
4/ It is not really a game for pervs only as half of characters are male and the game is fair on that point : they get as oversexualised as females. And again, while playing, impossible to focus on cleavages. It can feed pervs only if they're already pervs.
The game is actually quite good itself : easy to get fun, (very) hard to master. The game will help you though to learn all moves and combos for each characters unlike Street Fighter which learn you either too basic combos or impossible to land ones.
It is a port so technically it can't be perfect but it is still better than Dark Souls'.

I kinda forgot about this game and the previous one as well but i bought it anyway because i needed something to finally test my PS4 controller on.

The graphics seem nice and very polished however the music is generic and unmemorable. The game seems quite taxing on the system - my videocard heats up to 70C even though it rarely goes up above 40C in other games, there are some slowdowns between cut-scenes and lags that make the game unplayable in multiplayer when there's a lot of things on the screen at the same time like enemies and projectiles.
The story is plain and dull - you get thrown into underworld and have to reassemble Osiris. Basically its Age of Mythology all over again.

Same as in Guardian of Light each level offers number of challenges and rewards for completing them - there's an overall score challenge (based damage you receive, amount of gems you collect and enemies killed) and some sub-challenges like collecting items or killing foes in specific ways. There is some replay value in levels but not much of it.

The game gives you dozens of random items outright and even more later on. 99% of them will be completely useless and it would've been better if you could combine, discard or craft them into something more useful. People keep comparing this system to Diablo but in this game items actually hardly matter at all.

There are several issues i see at the moment - companions are missing from all in game cutscenes if you are playing alone but you can still hear their voices which results in weird and awkward feeling. Camera in multiplayer is extremely jittery. Basically it tries to follow every single person which makes it almost unplayable and very confusing. They should've allowed to focus camera on your character only. Also characters appear very small in multiplayer, not as small as in Gauntlet but small enough to get confusing, especially with that jittery camera issue.
Unfortunately "drop-in-drop-out" system isn't that good either - people can't just come and go and level has to be started from the last checkpoint while you are forced to wait on the loading screen. Waiting for 3 players might actually get frustrating and boring.

The game got decent controller support. It keeps rumbling every second, like when you shoot or when bosses walk, when you take damage, when you use light staff or detonate bombs. Overall using controller seems quite pleasurable. It is kinda hard to roll and place bombs at the same time though.
I can recommend this as a decent single player puzzle game i suppose but if you want to play with your friends - you should probably wait for a couple of patches.

Discount purchase review!
I bought this in the bundle with Metro : LL Redux for $25 thanks to a great steam sale.
I'm about half way through the game (I think) right now. I'm just after "Defend/Child".
Short bullets :
REALISM :
- Gas/Nightvison goggles will be damaged (comprimised vison) if you wear them in combat
- No automatic ammo pickups or reloads
- You actually might need your flashlight in this, unlike other shooters
GAMEPLAY (Good):
- Definatly not your traditional "Run-N-Gun" game but far from boring. Two playable modes which can switch the game from it's classic "Scavenege for bullets" and stealth preffered feel, or make it more forgiving on ammo count with "Spartan" mode.
- Heavy scavenging aspect, good if you're into looting every enemy you kill and searching for ammo ect.
- Many different ways to stealth through enemy blockades, or just attempt to gun every enemy down if you have enough bullets
BAD :
- Weak human A.I , Monsters are ok but they generally just swarm you anyways
- Not so good level progession when it requires you to perform a specific action but you receive no instruction or hint from the game on what to do (Read below)
- Forced Night Vision Goggles mode (bug? Read below)
Upon entering that game, I noticed it was FAR different from any other shooter I've played. It does have some focus on realism. Putting on a Gas mask to avoid radiation, a game where you actually need your flashlight, No automatic reload, wiping blood off of said gas mask, no automatic ammo pickups, ect. It has a pretty high scavenging and looting feel to it, if you like searching every body, and looting safes you'll like the scavenging aspect to this. The graphics are super intense I was suprised to find out that I actually couldn't run it at "Very High" setting because it was too much for my graphics card, but It looks amazing in that mode if you have strong enough specs.
This is definatly not a run-n-gun game, but fear not, it's far from boring. You CAN run-n-gun if you choose to play in the new "Spartan" mode, which makes ammo pretty common. But from what I hear in the normal mode ammo is more scarce and stealth is preffered. Speaking of the stealth system, it's pretty nice. Stay in the shadows, don't walk on any broken glass and avoid tripwire traps ect. You can stealthily take out enemies, or blow out the candles and sneak past them. However there is a downfall, the A.I are increadibly horrible at detecting you while you're not shooting at them. I crouched behind one Nazi gaurd and attempted to knock him out only to realize too late that he had full body armor on and I wouldn't be able to. He turned around with his flash light right in my face and shouted "Who goes there?!" I froze, I was practically kissing him but he didn't "notice" me. After a tense staring contest he soon mumbled somthing about seeing shadows and casually pushed me (no really, the game phsyically pushed me out of his way) and continued to walk past me. Now yes, this was in "Spartan/Normal" mode (Easy) but I mean come on, he should have detected me.
Another thing I don't like is how the game just completetly leaves you to figure almost everything out on your own. I (like many others) had NO IDEA what to do when first following Khan and arriving in the train car full of impassable cobwebs. He just stood there and didn't tell me what to do. I thought that the game bugged and failed to load a script and rebooted it several times until finally watching a walkthrough on Youtube and finding out that you had to press M and take out your lighter and burn the cobwebs. The reason this is confusing is because you walk through TONS of other cobwebs throughout the game without needing to burn them, then suddently arrive at some that you MUST burn to pass but receiving no instruction or hint to do so. Litterally, Khan doesn't say ANYTHING when you get to this part. He just stands there and stares through the webs.
Finally, I don't even know if this is a bug or not but, there are times when after you collect the night vision goggles you'll be FORCED to wear them durring some parts of the game. And no, not parts where they're usefull, infact quite the opposite. This is the whole reason I decided to write this review. This is absolutly rediculous. At some specific parts of the game, your character will put his NVG's on and you won't be able to take them off. I first encounted this durring the "Trolly Fight" level in which you use an turret on a moving rail car and shoot at enemies. The NVGs got forced on me and  I couldn't take them off for the whole level. Since the level isn't particually dark it was EXTREAMLY hard to aim at enemies because all I could see was big white blobs everywhere (fires, enemy flashlights, explosions, ect.) The NVGs are definatly NOT NEEDED in this level but the game forces you to wear them. I don't know if this is a bug or not, but I later encountered this when entering a "town/outpost". It once again forces me to wear the NVGs in a well lit environment making it hard to navigate. shop, ect.
All in all, I do enjoy the game for providing me with a different kind of shooter experiance sperate from Call of Duty styled shooters. ....But that NVG thing is really starting to get on my nerves!

So, I've only played a limited amount of this game, but due to the fact that it just came out, people are obviously going to want some impressions. Also, please note that earlier today I played around the first third of Guardian of Light so I would be prepared to compare the progress made on this game.
TL;DR This game improves on GoL in literally every respect, rendering its predecessor almost obsolete in the process. Breathtaking visuals, refined gameplay, larger and more diverse areas/puzzles, more enemies supported on screen at the same time than GoL really ever managed, 4-player drop in/drop out with public matchmaking support, all for the lowly price of twenty dollars. Avoid using SSAA, as it seems to have very little impact on visual fidelity, make sure you plug in your gamepad, and I can almost promise you will enjoy this game.
*REVIEW STARTS HERE*
First, the negative (and trust me, there isn't much).
-Bad keyboard controls return. The scheme is similar to the first game, and for many that will be a bad thing. Keyboard controls just feel unresponsive and awkward, especially since the way Lara gradually turns while running seems to be designed for an analog stick. Get a controller for this game or you will have a suboptimal experience.
-PERFORMANCE. Okay, I've been seeing some initial feedback saying the performance is not very good. I was worried about this (I have an R9 290x Gaming, i5 4670, and 16 GB Ballistix) because nothing frustrates me more than poor optimization when I have a fairly nice rig. After glancing at the video options, I immediately noticed what the issue is. This game offers two types of anti-aliasing: FXAA and SSAA. Most people will be familiar with FXAA. It is very low cost but also tends to blur the image quite a bit. SSAA (commonly confused with the much less performance heavy SMAA), however, is a little bit more uncommon and is an EXTREMELY performance heavy and ham fisted form of anti-aliasing that usually looks great. I don't see much of a difference here other than a distinct performance drop in some areas while having it on. On my rig, I pull an unwavering 60 FPS with FXAA on. SSAA on drops the framerate in only the most demanding cutscenes.
*EDIT*
I feel like I have to add another negative here, if I am to be completely honest. I gave the multiplayer co-op a shot and... let's just say they could have done better. Now, I could see this game TOTALLY being a blast if you and a friend or two get together and communicate. Right now the solo queue is an absolute mess, though. Players drop in and drop out fairly frequently, which halts the action for a few seconds, and if the host leaves then a new one is picked and progress seems to be reset to the last checkpoint, which can be quite a ways away. Adding to the issue is the fact that these puzzles were not designed with four players in mind (it would have been quite an enourmous task to make puzzles that could be completed with one person but challenged four as well). Both Egyptian gods can wield their own respective staves while both explorers have grappling hooks and can use fire (though I've seen an issue where Lara loses fire and only Carter can use it; I don't know if this is intentional). The biggest issue seems to be a lack of communication and ability spam during complex puzzles. The session I was in consisted of one person who seemed to know how to solve the puzzle, myself, who was trying to figure it out but having difficulty communicating with the leader, and two people who seemed to be actively inhibiting progress by messing with switches, dropping mines, and moving the ball of sunlight to places it did not need to go. Fighting enemies with four players is also quite a mess. Fights are chaotic, yes, but not in the good way. Dying seems almost impossible considering the sheer amound of ammunition being simultaneously fired off and mines annoyingly cause friendly fire, which leads to some serious griefing. All in all, with maybe a single friend, this could be fun. Right now solo queue is a nightmare, though.
*END EDIT*
Now, the good.
-This game is breathtakingly gorgeous. I mean, the screenshots look quite nice, but I never expect the same quality in game. This is an exception. From the minute you run out of the temple and outside into the first level, there is an obvious difference in graphical fidelity between this game and the last installment. The smoke effects are some of the best I have ever seen, textures are of above average quality, and the lighting is spot on. Character models look much better than the first game, though not quite as sharp as the environment (which isn't a problem since this game plays from the isometric perspective).
-Gameplay is smoother and more diverse than the first game (based on my limited experience with it). While the first game had the gimmick with the golden spear, which was essentially a one trick pony, this game features a staff that allows you to interact with certain normally static objects in the world so long as they have Osiris's emblem on them. Co-op features two players wielding the staff, which does cause problems (particularly with there only being a need for one staff, so the other player is left twiddling their thumbs). Dodging, jumping, and especially grappling all feel finely tuned. It should also be noted that the UI is cleaned up, and the gear equipment screen is easier to navigate.
-Level design, I feel, deserves its own category. I have only played roughly half an hour of the game and I have already encounterd larger, more open areas than were available in the first game, twice as many more enemies on screen at the same time than there ever were in Guardian of Light, and very well designed platforming sections. I won't spoil anything, but let's just say that the first chase scene in the game is far more compelling and heart pounding than anything that happened in my time with Guardian of Light (and I do enjoy that game, as well).
-The story is so corny and I absolutely love it. Clearly this isn't a narrative driven game, but the writers still seemed to have some fun with the script and nailed the "so bad it is good" tone perfectly. Lara, as usual, is her sassy self, but the new Egyptian additions are just a riot, particularly Set. His voice is so goofy and evil-villain-echo-tastic that one could almost not feel threatened by him, if it weren't for the very menacing and threatening demon chasing you for what seems like it will be throughout the game (a wise choice to include this to contrast Set).
-Miscellaneous: The loot early on seems to possess those classic ARPG modifiers ala "Debilitating Iron Ring of Major Grappling" and so on and so forth, which seems to suggest that there will possibly be LOTS of (perhaps random) loot to collect. There is a nifty matchmaking tool in the main menu for online co-op, which is always welcome. Many of the great features from GoL have returned, such as laying and detonating bombs, carrying four weapons at a time, the ammo meter for secondary weapons, and the collection of gems (though this time they can be used to open chests containing loot; a smart addition).
Overall, I'd say this game is fantastic so far and very much worth the low price tag of twenty dollars. Furthermore, you don't have to have played GoL at all to understand the story. Think of this like a 007 sequel. Sure, if you watch all the movies you will notice a broad timeline and catch on to some of the more prominent tropes, but nothing stopes you from watching them out of order and still knowing exactly what is going on. Keep in mind that co-op with strangers feels disjointed, but great with a friend. I would actually encourage you to buy this game RATHER than GoL, as this improves the gameplay in literally every area, rendering its predecessor almost completely obsolete. Anyway, if you got this far, thanks for sticking with me. Hope you enjoy!

I have enjoyed the sport of cycling since I was a little kid, so when I saw this game I was really excited, but after playing this game for a while, I have come across so many issues i just cant recommend it to anyone. Here is a fairly detailed list of major issues I personaly have with the game.
1. It crashes a lot, I cant click on anyting during the loading screen or it will crash for sure. Nothing I care about much though.
2. This Issue hurts me deep inside the most. When ever you tell a rider to accelerate, if he is stuck behind someone, his energy stats will start going down(like what is suppose to happen if he is free to accelerate), but he wont be going any faster. So you are going the same pace as ther person next to you, but using up all your energy.
3. One small issues is you cant sim the rest of the race once all of your people are done, and many when there is an early mountain there are many stragglers and it takes forever for the stage to end. The worst offender I have found is a rider named Schwarzman.
4. During Sprints for the finish, you can only exactly set up your people the last coupel of K's to go. In real cycling they spend many more K's organizing themselves. This will many times lead to losing some leadout men or wear them out unnessarly. Between this and people blocking themselves in sprinting seems to have a lot of luck to it.
5. Breakaways. if you try to personaly chase a breakaway down at the beginning of the game it is nearly impossible at some points even though its your entire 8 person team hunting down 2 people. I understand It should tire them out a bit, but it doesnt feel right at all. Once your in a break away sometimes its peaceful and everything seems somewhat normal. But other times the riders your with in the break will just keep attacking until your rider (who could even have way better stats then everyone else) gets too tired  to do anything. This is either on or off, they either cooperate (which happens every time if your not in the break) or selfdestruct. The biggest issue i have is teams that have people in the break, chasing the break down by sending riders to the front of the peleton. It doesnt make sense and seems like something easy to code and fix.
6. The game mechanics at time make me want to pull my hair out. I understand you probably dont want to be able to tell exactly where your riders should be at all times, but many times its just impossible to even keep them in the general area. If a rider from another team(or your own team) decides to slow down right in front of you and your unlucky, you could have just lost 30 positions and have just blown the stage. In real life many riders swing off to the side so they dont get in the way of other people, in this game they just screw over 3 or 4 people every time they slow down. Its impossible to follow an attack and draft even a little bit. You just have to spen the same energy they did most of the time no matter what you do. The energy gel is stupid. It is a one time item each of your riders have and after a delay they ride better for a minute or so. It is great fun to roam around the big open world and meet a big group of friendly animals to roam with, and collect treasure, and explore! You can collect colored dodads and flowers, and unlock obelisks together, to unlock new animals to play as, skins for the cutten animal, and emotes for the current animal, and that's relaxing and fun~
That alone is honestly worth the present full purchase price, in my opinion~
HOWEVER~
That is ALL there is to do. Functionally, you can walk, run, jump, and do a variety of emotes, most of which put some kind of picture above your head, which can communicate a small, context sensitive variety of concepts to other players who are close by.
That's as deep as interaction goes. Now, I am not saying there should be a chat or anything, I actually really like the limited communication between animals, it makes a really fun system of communication.
But again, that's ALL there is. There's no form of threat, no failstates, no challenges. There's not much GAME here. You just wander together and collect the same stuff over and over again to unlock things for you.
And really that's my main problem with this game. It comes from a game who's story all that is told almost exclusively through the doing, the things that happen, the interactions between the things you meet, and generally it all makes sense.
Aside from the emotes in this game, there is no player interaction, there is no real interaction at all.
Now, this game does not advertize itself as a Shelter game, so I am trying not to knock it for not being a multiplayer Shelter.
But if I am honest, that is what I would really like from this game. And the only real reason that I bring this up, and think it is at all relevent, aside from the fact that they have the same graphics, is that many of the animals you can play as, and some of the emotes, are unlocked by owning the other content from these developers. Which means, anyone who has the Adult Badger, or Adult Lynx? They had to buy Shelter or Shelter 2 to acquire those. There is no other way to get them, than by having two other games that would translate really well in my opinion to being a multiplayer predator/prey survival type game~
Of course, I understand that what we have here is something totally different. I would be happy to pay significantly more money for a Multiplayer shelter game. This one though I think could do with some kinds of fun, optional challenges or some such. Races? Hide and seek? Collectable easter egg hunts?
Maybe some areas only the smallest animals can go, and have there be something inside that they can bring to the larger characters?
Maybe some areas the baby animals can't jump to, and so need a ride from the larger animals?
These are just a few things that I thought of off the top of my head that I think would do wonders to enhance the interactions and longjevity of this game.
Again, for the present full price, this game is definitely worth it. I just wish that there was more to do, and I would honestly happily pay more for that.

TL:DR;
I cannot recommend it due to few fatal flaws.
This is a flash game of armorgames quality, sale material not worth more than 6$.
Worse it is aimed only at a certain group of people with masochistic tendencies. Read on to find why.
Review:
NEO Scavenger, an odd name for a title that claims to be post-apocalyptic survival game.
It hardly achieves what it promises and unfortunately uses few tricks to hide its flaws from the player for the first few hours.
Graphics: 5/10
No excuses for uninspired graphics. Sure, it's not the most important part of the game, but the choice of tiles, buildings, etc. is waaaaaaaay to poor.
Sounds: 8/10
Actually pretty good. Keeps atmosphere. Ambient, dark elements accompany the game pretty good.
Gameplay: 5/10
Well... good for the first few hours.
Rogue-like random map and loot, random encounters etc.
The problem is that it is yet another game which uses brutal RNG and player's death as an excuse for lack of any in depth mechanics and content.
Once you get a grasp of this title, you will realise that there is nothing to aim at, except for maybe very difficult base infiltration mission which is also an end game.
You see, this game has totally nothing to offer.
- no skill progression
- no character progression
- no camp building
- no real crafting
- no loot variety
- no enemies variety
- no real missions and NPCs
- no factions you can actually join in a meaningful way
- not possible to start a gang of friendly NPCs and roam the land
There is simply nothing in terms of gameplay that after few initial deaths can hold you to this title.
It's all the same - walk around, kill mobs, loot corpses, scavenge, return to camp (now probably ransacked by NPCs.
Fetch wood, boil water, cook meat, repeat till you die of diarrhea or other plagues.
You can't, for example, raid some bunker or a military base and bar the entrance from the inside, thus being shielded from harm. You can't really upgrade it (there is room 17 in starting location, but I got a bug and it vanished, taking all the stuff with it). You can't start a farm or hydroponics at the camp. Can't make bullets.
With crafting limited as it is, with no solar panels to recharge all those laptops and batteries and stuff, you are either forced to buy technology from remaining megacity or live like a tribal.
Only you can't have a tribe because you cannot befriend any of the numberless horde of nameless NPCs.
Therefore this game is only recommended either on sale or to a group of people who enjoy dying and starting over against whatever devilry RNG has conjured against a player this time.

From the moment you wake up, you're fighting for survival. In NEO Scavenger, winning the fight doesn't get you xp or even good loot at times. I've been playing since alpha and have managed to find a skill combo that really helps me get past the basic 3 needs, but there have been countless games where a bad choice has ended my career as a scavenger. If you are looking for a low-end high replayablity game that is tough yet rewarding, this is your game.

Great game for all 40k fans and for fans of tactical space combat. That said its not like Homeworld, but more like Nexus: The Jupiter Incident. No base building, just managing your fleet mission to mission.
graphics: Game is very pretty and ship models are very well done.
Gameplay: While there is a learning curve, anyone can get the hang of it with enough practice. I have found that the auto use feature is a must for skills. Helps out hugely on the mirco so you just have to worry about torpedoes and nova cannons. There is a decent amount of grinding in order to lvl up your admiral and ships, but battles are pretty fast, so you can get to battleships pretty quickly. For now, we can only use 4-6 ships per battle, so we don't get overwhelmed trying to control so many ships and all their abilities and skills.
Campaign: If you played Dawn of War 2 and enjoyed it, you will enjoy this. Similar mission structure with a limited amoutn of deployment per turn, making us choose what benefits we want to keep. I have yet to finish the campaign, but I have been enjoying it immensely.
Skirmish: Here we get to try out all 4 fleets (for now) against the AI. AI is decent to play againts and will provide a decent enough challange on normal.
Multiplayer: Can't say anything here, I generally don't play online.
Overall its a fun game. Some features are still missing, but the devs have been putting out huge patches every single week since the beta started fixing bugs and tweaking the balance. We have 2 new fleets incoming in the next few months, so I see plenty of future support and content from the devs. So give this game a chance. It might be difficult at first, but once you get past the learning curve, its tons of fun.

When I play video games, I really do try to enjoy the game, even when I don't like the game at first. I do not play the first five minutes and decide if I like it or not, sometimes games can pickup the experience mid-way through. I often play the game and complete it before having a finished judgement on the game, quite often I end up enjoying the games after beating them if I hadn't at first. This game on the other hand..
- Interesting story, makes you want to play more to find out your future achievements within the virtual world of Steelport.
- Adding super powers is a good mechanic, can be awkward to use at times in situations.
- Lighting effects are decent.
- Voice acting is decent, can be funny at times.
- Online campaign, get your buddy to play with you.
- Texture quality is poor, yet my graphical and texture quality in the settings are maxed, especially on the clothes that you can apply to your avatar, therefore the bad texture quality is constantly in your view.
- Lazy work-arounds for various mechanics and physics, a perfect
would be skirts in the game, they're just retextured trousers, no effort to implement. This is most obvious in first hour of the game.
- Lazy mission design and objectives, some feel like they where reused with new textures from the previous game.
- Lazy plot, can be predicted easily.
- Lazy design, the city is the same as the previous game with added structures and retextures.
- I felt like I needed ALL the DLC to enjoy the game in its full glory, unlike the previous game.
I felt like this game was a quick money grab for Deep Silver Volition, everything at most is a retexture and a few added bonuses. Within the disclaimer, I said I usually like to complete the game before I make a final judgement on the title, but with Saints Row: IV, I couldn't even force myself to play, I felt like I was just playing the previous game which was much better and had sufficent more purpose to the Saints Row series, I didn't want to play this game because I thought I was wasting my time and I didn't enjoy it after 3 hours in the game. One day I might pickup the game and decide to finish it to the end, but at the moment, I shall not recommend this game to those looking to play the game by themselves.

As it stands right now, I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone that likes to play their fighting games online since this game is lacking that feature at the time of this writing, and according to Team Ninja, it will be patched into the game in about 3 months from now (probably after EVO 2015 maybe?)
That being said, if you don't mind the lack of online mode and just want to play offline or practice, this is a pretty good port of the arcade version of Dead or Alive 5 Last Round with the console modes added in.
The game does a real good job teaching you the basics of DOA with it's in-depth tutorial mode. Everything you need to know about the system mechanics from the different stuns and stagger states, to the power crush system are all explained in this mode that will get you up to speed if you're new to this game, or an old veteran who has missed out on the last couple of games.
As for the graphics, I personally think it looks better than the X1 or PS4 versions since you can supersample from a higher resolution and remove the need for anti-aliasing altogether (if your hardware supports it). The end result is a real clean looking image that you can only find on the PC version of this game.
The game runs at a locked 60 FPS on my system with no issues (i7 2600k, 16GB RAM, GTX 780). You'll only see it drop to 30 FPS during cutscenes and match introductions. This may have been something left in from the PS3/X360 era as those scenes needed to look better than the in-game graphics for that generation with underpowered hardware, so they increased image quality at the expense of the framerate for those specific scenes. It may be jarring for some people, but it's something I can easily brush off since it doesn't affect gameplay at all.
Now for the problems that I've had with this game include the issue of not natively supporting Xinput devices such as Xbox360 controllers and joysticks. The problem is that this game uses the outdated direct input method to detect controllers and that leads to some compatibility issues in getting keyboards and controllers working properly.
I use a MadCatz TE joystick and a Hori RAP V3SA joystick. Both of them have messed up button placements when used with this game. The face buttons are in a weird scrambled order where the A and the B buttons are on the top row and the X and Y buttons are on the bottom, which makes menu navigation odd, but not impossible once you get used to it. In game, you can reconfigure the different attack buttons to match whatever configuration you like, that is not an issue in this game at all. I can set my buttons to the standard 3 buttons and be done with it once I'm in game.
If you're a keyboard warrior, you may have more issues than a controller user in this game as the keys used in-game are all locked to a specific configuration. If they decide to patch the input issues, hopefully this will be fixed as well and let keyboard players reconfigure their controls to their preference.
Ignore the DLC, it's all cosmetic stuff that they won't split up for some reason. Not everyone out there who plays this game wants to pay $120 for extra costumes, especially for characters I rarely use or don't care about. I guess Koei Tecmo would rather make $0 instead of an extra $5 or $10 per user by not offering the costume packs a la carte.
The verdict? buy it in 3 months when it is on sale for 50% or more unless you really want to play a solid 3D fighting game on PC right now and don't mind the lack of online versus mode.

This game has been a surprise to me. Caught it in the Steam sale over Christmas and have to admit I didn't play it straight away. But casually loaded it up last week and have been hooked!
You start with a crew of 3, with a basic loadout of weapons, fuel and the ability to get some drones to assist you with tasks like ship repairs, intruders, among others. Your mission? KEEP MOVING! The rebels are chasing you from one sector to the next. On your journey you'll be encountering events such as pirates chasing down defenceless ships (do you help them? do you accept a pirate bribe to stay out of it?) and you can sell scrap you collect to upgrade your systems (buy additional crew members to help with unmanned systems, buy fuel, rockets, new weapons...). You'll never have enough scrap to outfit your ship completely so it's very important to make the right decision.
The "random" element of the game is perhaps its best feature. No 2 games are the same, you can "jump" once and get an additional crew member, or you can jump and find yourself staring at a rebel ship wanting to shoot you to pieces.
...and if you wanted more than something that was replayable, you've got a truly excellent soundtrack to listen to as you play that's atmospheric and draws you in.
Best indie game I've played personally, and I'd definitely get it... whether you want it right now or whether you can wait til the next sale, at least add it to your wishlist, and look it up on YouTube :)

So even though I never actually played the Battlefleet Gothic Table Top game, I did play Warhammer 40k, and I've always loved the ship design from the franchise. Now, at long last, we finally get to see them come to life in a game that does them justice. So this is a space based, ship to ship battle RTS game. I Played this game during beta and even then I was impressed. So let's go over the pros and cons of this game, because this is one alot of people have been watching closely.
Pros-
Ship design- The models of the ships are 100% faithful to the franchise, and they all look gorgeous.
Factions- Each faction, though they all share certain common features such as upgrades, feel unique in the way they play. Imperials are about up close, powerful broadside barrages. Chaos are fast long range raiders. Orks are tanky, close range brawlers that love to ram other ships. The Eldar are fast and use hit and run tactics. Each playstyle makes perfect sense in the context to their race. And given that this is 40k, you can bet other factions are on the way. Space marines are already confirmed, along with a mystery faction following that.
Voice acting- Although it's pretty apparent this wasn't a big budget title and they did have a huge variety of voices in the game, the ones they DO have are spot on and feel perfect for the 40k universe.
- Very strategic and challenging- I was actually surprised at this. The AI will actually kick your♥♥♥♥♥if your not careful. You actually have to manage and position your ships to prevail. Also remember what I mentioned about ramming? This game has full collision physics, that means you can actually crash your ships into each other if your not careful.
Cons-
Mission Variety- It feels like the mission types really aren't as diverse as they should be. I feel there are several mission types that reward bum rush tactics too much. I also rarely find there's an actual advantage to deploying your ships in different ways.
2d- Although the game is very much visually in 3d, the gameplay is 2d. In many ways this isn't actually that big a deal, as properly doing 3d gameplay in a space rts can be very difficult to do.
Soundtrack- Although the music they DO have is very good and appropriate, there's zero diversity. There's no special theme's for Chaos, orks, or the Eldar, which I think is a bit of a shame.
Bugs- Although the game is in pretty good shape for on launch, I have encountered a couple bugs ingame that WERE present during the beta.
Bottom line is, if you're a 40k fan, absolutely get this game. It more than does the source material justice, and it despite it not being perfect, it more than delivers, especially for only $40. Plus, buying within 2 months of release will get you the next 2 dlc factions for free, so not only did the devs make a good game, they want to reward you for buying it with free stuff. So just go and buy the damn thing already you wretched heretic!

Zero Gear is an indie Racing game, the community is pretty much dead, but if you don't feel like you've had enough kart games, here you go, just for you.
Disclaimer: I'm voting it down *not* because it's a bad game, but because the community is dead, you will play by yourself 9 times out of 10. (Maybe you don't mind that? Maybe you want to play a racing game by yourself? Go ahead and get it, lol)
Instead of a telling the gist of the story (there is none) I'm going to tell my own story. The first time I loaded this game I listen to the soundtrack and though "Woa! This sound really good" I called my brother over and said "doesn't that sound like it has good potential?"
I clicked "quick game" and
all my hopes and dreams were crushed... This was in fact... a racing game.
To provide a back story, I've always strongly disliked racing games and driving games. But Saints Row 3, Mafia 2, and Just Cause 2 have all forced me to learn how to drive in video games.
The first game I played was some type of "Soccer" (or "Football" for those whom aren't in the USA), this is probably the worst game in the batch. There are several game modes: Tag, Race, and Soccer. All of these can be played and learned, however it takes a bit of getting used to the turning style... Much to my frustration when learning the basics of the game.
Soccer/Football/Hockey, your goal is to get the ball/puck into the other team's goal (pun intended).
Race is where you drive in circles for a few laps and try to beat the NPC's, because humans don't play this game anymore.
Tag, for those of you with no childhood; is when you run away from one person because he/she was designated being "it", whatever it is, who knows? In this game it's reversed. You WANT to be it, so you can score points and win.
There are 45 Achievements in Zero Gear, Most of them are easily obtainable, however a number of them are bugged, and still more require the assistance of one friend.
the price for Zero gear, is $4.99 that's pretty fair, if you really want this game just wait for a steal sale, you can probably pick it up for a couple dollars.
AHHH a racing game. *deletes the devil from my computer*
Again, I'm giving it the thumbs down because most people probably won't want to spend time playing this game. The game works, and I could go one way or another, but with my friends interest in mind; probably should just skip this game. You could get a more delightful indie games for the same price.

Saints Row IV is the reason why video games exist in the first place. This game plays much like GTA games except in this world you are a ridiculously overpowered superhero that must defeat an alien race that has taken over the world.
While this game isn't perfect its so close that any flaws that you might have go completely unnoticed as you progress through the game. At the time of this review I've only scratched the surface with close to 5 hours of playtime, but when i get into it I just get lost in the awesomeness that is this game.
If there are any game developers out there that want to know what games should be like? Play this game.
Pros:
- Big Open City that allows you free reign on as much chaos as you can create.
- The graphics are not too shabby. I've seen better but it plays so well you don't even notice. Also while other games run worse on machine and don't look half as good, with this one one the max settings this game played like a champ. I had zero lag or framerate issues, which is craqzy considering the often superspeedy pace of this game.
- The gameplay is insane. You run about destroying this and causing general chaos, and somewhere in that is this game where you have some objective? I don't know yet because I'm having too much fun causing mayhem and destruction.
- It is challenging at times. This can be a pro or a con, depending on your level game play experience. For me I enjoyed the jumping puzzles trying to get as high as possible or run at insane speed and try to get to places.
- It is humorous as hell. Some may not like it, but i loved it.
Cons:
- There is a learning curve with this game. Even when the tutorial explains something, hell if it takes me a while to get it right. The jumping from building to building at superspeed took a lot of practice. The jumping to the top of a tower that you must jump from platform to platform was frustrating as hell as I failed over and over.
Many enemies are way too strong. Again this could be a Pro or Con. For me I like challenges, but when I fight something that is clearly impossible for me to kill, I'd like to know ahead of time.
- The controls were tough to figure out, and this kind of goes with the learning curve. I think after a little bit of chaos i started to get the hang of it.
- Some thing made no sense to me. One quest had me stealing a bike. In the game like GTA you can commit many acts of grand theft, and it never seems too hard, but then this bike had some weird physics. I couldnt steer it at all which made it super difficult to complete the quest. Ultimately I figured it out but it took a while to get the hang of it.
This game is ridiculous in all the right ways, 10/10 BUY THIS GAME!

My next stage was to run off into the woods to escape the carnage and get to grips with crafting some tools and the most important task of not dying of thirst and starvation, which subsequently happened no long after realising those strange noises i could hear was my characters stomach grumbling.
After 4 hours of gameplay, this is definately starting out alot more refined than what Ark initially was, fair enough there is crashes (only once in 4 hours), a couple of lag spikes (about 10 times in 4 hours), but it mostly ran very very fluid.
Mechanics are rather well thought out, animals vary quite alot; some like sheep are plenty to come by and easy to tame, and some you can't get close enough to read what they actually are before they tear your head from your shoulders while you stare at the screen in disbelief.

If you buy this expecting current Ark quality you will suffer (actually probably not tbh, might equal it to fair few people depending on your experience), you have to remember this at time of writing is 10 days into Early Access, however i do believe this is definately worth the purchase, even if its brought now, tried for a bit to get a feel of it, and then kept in the library for a few months before it matures a bit more to save some money as development continues.

But anyway, if you hate those games that offer a good cinematic ending after completing the arcade mode then rejoice for the only reward you get other than some achievements, and a different color of the initial costumes you were given is a rest from the game by being sent back to the menu screen.
You remember super street fighter four, blaz blue and even marvel versus capcom's feature where characters sometime say different lines when fighting specific opponents? It's not in this game. By the end of one arcade mode you'll probably memorize the intro lines and ending lines of your character unless you're too mesmerized by her unbouncing breasts. I don't know if it's different from story mode, but I doubt it since the original team that made the game i ordered probably already wasted all the budget on the breast bouncing physics that's not on this game.
Hmm... what else... the special is amazing... once. Unless you can use it properly to throw or slam your opponent to interactable places on the stage... which are few it gets pretty stale pretty fast. Sure it's always fun to see your character kick her opponent up crashing against a helicopter but to do this not only do you need to position your opponent properly in front of the helicopter but also need to be at relatively low health. So perfectionists who want to end the fight with a finishing move can suck a salty sausage.
The amount of characters is also good. They finally completed all the standard requirements for an eye candy game by adding a loli. We now have a big boobed heroine, an equally large breasted rival, the generic goody goody guy, a hideyoshi, a sadistic woman, an overly serious man, a ninja, some hurly burly man for those sadistic needs and a jailbait; I think we have the complete set.
The soundtrack is okay... Well, no, I personally think the tune in the beginning was too loud. It felt like the developers were conditioning you to get pumped up for some multiplayer battle but with the absence of an online function it's now just some pretentious generic tune. Only Marie Rose had a good character soundtrack. Everyone else felt like they had generic tunes partnered with them just for the sake of them having a tune each.
There are already mods for this game but since other people are working on them and not the hardworking developers who didn't give me the game I ordered I am not giving the game any points for that. Overall maybe in three months this game will look like the game I ordered but I'm not sure I'll still have this in my library by then. For now, I recommend to everyone to look away from this game, no matter how much those breasts in the posters tempt you.

I really wanted to like this game, especially because I enjoyed the previous installments a lot. But as much as I'd like to, I can't recommend the game, simply because it's littered with bugs.
The core concept is really appealing and the story progression and visuals are nice and fitting. I also enjoyed the soundtrack by composer Michael McCann. These aspects might make the game at least somewhat interesting for extremely frustration-resistant players and/or fans.
What I absolutely hated was the overall "wonkiness" of the turn-based system. My squads frequently got spawned mid-air, allies and enemies got bugged on ladders and floated above them, hit-chances felt completely random at times (
), and I regularly had to quit and restart the game for various reasons.
Sometimes I was unable to heal anybody (Medkit spray animation played but recipient didn't receive any HP) and other times I tabbed out of the game - don't tab out of the game. There's a high chance for graphical glitches to appear and a reload or even a full restart is necessary.
And one of the worst issues I have with the game: Half of the time you can't open the menu, mostly during alien activity. You see the aliens move to positions you didn't anticipate or your squad just got fu**ed and you want to load your save and try a different tactic? First you have to wait a minute until all aliens are done with their turns. That's annoying and has no benefit.
All of these problems add up and playing the game got really frustrating. I still want to finish it, however I'm disappointed with what I've seen so far. The concept in itself is great but the execution is just horrible. Thus I can't recommend this game, at least not in its current state.

Before my actual review of the game, I would like to tell you about my background of the Pro Cycling Manager series. I started playing the game in 2004, with the release of Cycling Manager 4, a game that I still often return too. I have played everygame in the series, and have often been dissappointed, by the improvements in the yearly releases.
This year is different though, and i'll tell you why:
Interface:
The interface has been the same in the PCM series ever since I can remember, and even though the main menu in career mode, is basically the same. The prerace loading menu, has improved dramatically. Instead of showing you pointless information, they now give you a great overview of the main riders of every team, together with a list of the biggest favorites for the stage win. So even though I never actually played the Battlefleet Gothic Table Top game, I did play Warhammer 40k, and I've always loved the ship design from the franchise. Now, at long last, we finally get to see them come to life in a game that does them justice. So this is a space based, ship to ship battle RTS game. I Played this game during beta and even then I was impressed. So let's go over the pros and cons of this game, because this is one alot of people have been watching closely.
Pros-
Ship design- The models of the ships are 100% faithful to the franchise, and they all look gorgeous.
Factions- Each faction, though they all share certain common features such as upgrades, feel unique in the way they play. Imperials are about up close, powerful broadside barrages. Chaos are fast long range raiders. Orks are tanky, close range brawlers that love to ram other ships. The Eldar are fast and use hit and run tactics. Each playstyle makes perfect sense in the context to their race. And given that this is 40k, you can bet other factions are on the way. Space marines are already confirmed, along with a mystery faction following that.
Voice acting- Although it's pretty apparent this wasn't a big budget title and they did have a huge variety of voices in the game, the ones they DO have are spot on and feel perfect for the 40k universe.
- Very strategic and challenging- I was actually surprised at this. The AI will actually kick your♥♥♥♥♥if your not careful. You actually have to manage and position your ships to prevail. Also remember what I mentioned about ramming? This game has full collision physics, that means you can actually crash your ships into each other if your not careful.
Cons-
Mission Variety- It feels like the mission types really aren't as diverse as they should be. I feel there are several mission types that reward bum rush tactics too much. I also rarely find there's an actual advantage to deploying your ships in different ways.
2d- Although the game is very much visually in 3d, the gameplay is 2d. In many ways this isn't actually that big a deal, as properly doing 3d gameplay in a space rts can be very difficult to do.
Soundtrack- Although the music they DO have is very good and appropriate, there's zero diversity. There's no special theme's for Chaos, orks, or the Eldar, which I think is a bit of a shame.
Bugs- Although the game is in pretty good shape for on launch, I have encountered a couple bugs ingame that WERE present during the beta.
Bottom line is, if you're a 40k fan, absolutely get this game. It more than does the source material justice, and it despite it not being perfect, it more than delivers, especially for only $40. Plus, buying within 2 months of release will get you the next 2 dlc factions for free, so not only did the devs make a good game, they want to reward you for buying it with free stuff. So just go and buy the damn thing already you wretched heretic!

For less than the price of 2 pieces of bread sandwiching some sort of delicious filling, you will not find a better value racing game. Sure, it's 7 years old now, but that doesn't matter. That means even if your PC isn't crammed with the latest technology, you'll still be able to run it. If you do have a brand new, highlly-specced gaming machine, you'll still be able to make this game look good whilst running perfecly smoothly, even with 30 cars on screen.
Included within are great deal of interesting and varied circuits and a collection of proper racing cars, from saloons to single seaters, prototypes, featherlight caterhams and high performance road cars. The handelling may not be entirely 100% sim-like, but it's close enough and means you can play with a controller just as well as a wheel and pedals. Lotso race options available, from 3 lap sprints to 120 minute endurances, fully tyre wear, fuel depletion, damage modelling, engine and gearbox failures, sliding scale AI so no matter how good or bad you are you'll be challenged. There's still a healthy online community playing and modding this game at the likes of RaceDepartment or ReallyRubbishRacing. And all of this before you even take into account the increibly cheap expansion packs that add even more circuits and cars to play with.
Cannot recommend enough as an entry into sim racing, and a game you'll no doub continue playing into the future. (Or at leats Until Project CARs comes out and Assetto Corsa reaches v1.0 release build.)

Super Powers instead of SMGs! Capes instead of Cadillacs! Saints Row The Third was definitely a wacky ride, but it was still grounded in a Crime setting. Saints Row 4 goes off the deep end, adding Aliens, Super Powers, Pop Culture references, and...Raptors?
The first few hours were a lot of fun. Me and my brother made our characters, and decided to role-play as Super Heroes. Mine was named Captain Blast! Defender of Justice! His was named Deviller, and he was supposed to be my sidekick, until he got addicted to the game and got way too strong faster than I could keep up. The loser even got 100%!
It was stated by the developers that many of the events and powers of Saints Row the Third was originally going to be DLC for Saints Row The Third., and it shows. The old engine, activities, guns, and tools from Third are brought to Saints Row 4, but will alterations and many additions. You can’t be as powerful as you were in Saints Row The Third (and you were so darn untouchable in that game once you started getting perks). Nevertheless, you still feel pretty invincible in 4 outside of Warden Fights even at the start if the game.
The powers are also varied and interesting like the Super Jump, Glide, and Super Sprint. You can also cause shockwaves with the Super Stomp, and freeze, burn, and eviscerate your enemies with the Blast abilities. You also still have a repertoire of guns and rockets under your disposal. Because of this though, it made the use of vehicles and homies rather pointless, as you could pretty much take on the entire city and then some with just your powers. You could get to places faster than any car, so it was especially jarring whenever a mission would force you in a vehicle or find any nonsensical reason to take away your powers during certain missions. Another thing about the powers is that they felt very hard to use with a controller (I played with a PS4 controller with DS4 Windows) my brother played with a mouse and keyboard, and he said he had no problem switching between powers with it, so this complaint is irrelevant if you do not use a controller. Either way though, combat was a bit of a clusterfrick, but honestly, that’s the point.
The mission variety is there, but many of them I felt were a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥and just not worth doing half the time (I’m looking at you hacking minigame! Also you too Rift missions!)
Coming back to the “first few hours were fun” comment I made a few paragraphs ago, the game was really fun the first few several hours, but around the 13 hour mark, in started to wear thin. There was much to do, but many of it felt empty after that mark. Side Missions that your crew mates would say would “stick it to the Zin”, but did frick all. The Insurance Fraud, MOM, and Tank missions were always fun though.
The story is on the back seat, but I wouldn’t really expect anything different. The Writing I felt was much stronger in this game though, compared to the Third, although funny, involved too much toilet humor.
The one major complaint I have, was that the game had bugs up its♥♥♥♥♥during the climax of the game. Random crashes, Quest items not being where they are supposed to be (The Map shows the item is in one place, but you can see it somewhere else far away from the marker). During the transportation of the key item near the climax I had to restart it 3 times until it would proceed normally due to the objectives not activating properly.  Really marked the experience when I was finishing up, and kind of put me off getting all the Data Clusters and other collectibles. Seems strange considering I’m playing nearly 2 years after launch and yet these crashes haven’t been fixed. Maybe it’s because I’m using an Nvidia GPU? ( 970)
Port was good besides that though. It had the options I wanted, no lag on a decent computer, could switch between m+ kb and a controller on the fly, all that jazz. All in all, I enjoyed it, but the bugs and crashes near the end really hurt my experience.
