Game Play   ------->                8.8/10
-Plot
The plot of the game is very basic.  You are being pursued and essentially need to upgrade your ship in order
to prepare for the final battle.  Once you get into the game there are a TON of mini plots and mini missions.
I've played this game a lot and have seen many of these mini quests/missions only once though they follow a
generic formula.  They each have radically different potential outcomes.  Example of these in a generic
sense:
Helping an alien ship to get to location, A ship in need of fuel, or decoding an alien code.  They all have
different outcomes.  You  may get nothing for helping someone, or if you  give someone fuel you might get
reward  with a secret weapon, or you may even get reward with the powerful weapon in the game.
-Controls
Are very simple.  Essentially the controls are moving your characters around your ship and pointing at which
compartment you want to  fire at in an enemy ship and with what type of weapon.
- Playability
The game is different each time you play.  You'll get different missions and you'll find different weapons
even from the stores.  Even when you destroy and enemy, you might get a different weapon/drone.  Even
though  it does have a random component to it, it still follows a generic formula though sometimes they'll
put a  random surprise in there.
Sound        ------->                 7.8/10
The music very much does help with the atmosphere.  Though like Interstellar (the movie) the music can get
annoying and irritating after some extensive game play.
Graphics   ------->                  6.1/10
If you're playing this game for the graphics or hoping for great graphics this game isn't for you.  The
graphics are not amazing but you can easily tell what everything is for it does have detail.
Difficulty    ------->                 9.3/10
This game is very difficult.  I've only played it on normal and have continually gotten destroyed.
Replay       -------->                 10/10
This game has a lot of replayability.  Sometimes, you'll hope for a certain outcome or mission that has a
certain reward, don't bank on getting them.
Game Value (this is the value that I WOULD pay for the game.  This value is not necessarily how much I ACTUALLY paid for the game).
I would pay in the low 20s and no more than 25 for this game.  This game is a gem find if it is less than 10
and or even at 5, you will not be disappointed. If you see it 10 or less, pick it up.
Overall Rating  ------------->   42/50
Issues/Complaints:
If you are looking for a linear game, this game isn't for you.  You can be doing great and get a bunch of
random crapshot one after another and before you know it you've been destroyed.  Example:  You can be
doing well and go to a planet that has solar flares where you always will have to fight someone.  It seems
that these flares ALWAYS impacts you and every rare occasion impacts your opponent.  I have issue with
that.  Since the system has solar flares, you might not have time to fix up your ship, so you'll have to make
a jump.  Then, you might get boarded and be attacked.  Which I'm fine with.  When I get boarded I send
everyone except for the captain to the medic area and open all the doors to kill the intruders.  This helps
to filter them to the medic room but it never kills them.  Which is frustrating because it kills me pretty fast
and not the computer.  Games like this really makes me wish the opponent was held to the same
constraints that I am held to.
Final Thoughts
If you are the type of person who has to win every time (example if you play FIFA/NHL and you have to win ever single game) this game probably isn't for you.  This is a rogue game, which means that random events can kill you (it won't be a mystery though of what killed you) and you'll lose everything when you die.  If you don't like that, then don't purchase this game.  Most of the randomness you can prepare for or you just need to think outside of the box in dealing with the random events.
I have totally enjoyed this game.  Have I gotten frustrated with it? Yes! If you are on the ropes about buying this game, wait and buy  it if goes below 10 and buy it for sure if it is around 5.  Trust me, if you buy it in that price range and are on the fence you won't be disappointed.

Arcade and console games from Japan are often terrible ports and apart from a few exceptions there’s very few fighting games on the PC worth playing.
This port works. It’s graphics are great especially in 4k and very smooth fps. The texture resolution is more than adequate for the stages and the character models have superb detail.
I know some people dislike the removal of the Soft Engine, but if you’re that desperate for realistic jiggly boobs then there’s many other ways to get your fix. Not exactly game breaking is it. “The wobbliness of the boobs are all wrong.. GAAAA~Tableflip”  Get over it.
Controls works perfectly, plug in a good controller and it feels just like the playstation version. what more can you ask?
The menus and graphics are perfectly fine. Some fonts could have been redone a bit higher res but this port is not the broken mess that Dark Souls was.
Dead or Alive 5 plays, and plays well.  And online will arrive soon.  Yes I know it was odd to release without that feature and that is a big turn off for many, but the feature is coming. many other game ports have left those kind of features out all together.  Once it does there’s no reason to knock this game.
The PC needs more games from Japan’s arcades ported across so I will applaud this release for being one of the better efforts, if it just encourages other games to make their way over to the PC.

The single player Ardennes Assault Package is not realistic or fun to play in the long run.
It really is a shame, as I like the overall concept: Instead of fighting separate piecemeal actions, the developers have given us the ability to run a campaign. What you do in each mission will affect the strength of the Company in missions further down the road. However, the execution of the idea falls short because at the start of every mission you need to start from scratch, whereas the enemy gets stronger with every battle. For example: You unlock bazookas for paratroopers in one of the first missions to take on tanks. At every mission thereafter, you have to unlock the bazookas again to access them. But the enemy armor becomes heavier and heavier and they start pounding on you sooner and sooner in each battle as you move through the campaign. But you start from the base having to unlock everything while they start with Panzers. So after a certain point in the game, in every battle you will need to spend the resources to unlock those bazookas in order to put up an effective defense.
Realism says that once you unlock it for that Company, you don't have to recreate the wheel in every mission thereafter. But in this game, you do. This can be overcome in the early matches where resources aren't as contested but as you progress in missions, you have access to fewer and fewer resources and the Germans take the offensive sooner with heavier armor in each sequential match.
Think it doesn't matter? It only takes one bad mismatch in a battle to gut a Company to the point where it gets put on life support. However, as the Germans are defeated in individual matches, their units can retreat and retrench with other German units in unconquered territory on the strategic level. So despite losing battles, their units get progressively stronger and stronger as your units get weaker and weaker through attrition. That's not realistic or historically accurate.
Speaking of getting weaker and weaker, even if you pull an almost perfect battle with no unit losses (but have to use reinforcements) your main Company will still lose almost 10% of its strength. If you lose even a few units, you can easily lose 30% of a Company's strength in one match, and it's very possible to lose 50% or more of your strength in a single battle. Multiply 10 to 12 rounds at 30% losses per round and you can see that you won't have enough manpower in 3 Companies to finish the basic campaign on Normal. Don't forget that you will lose more and more troops in each battle as the Germans get more powerful each round while your troops weaken.
Reinforcement at the strategic level is a joke. You don't get anywhere near enough points to replace the losses suffered in matches and if you choose to reinforce your Companies they are penalized and LOSE BATTLE EXPERIENCE. This defies the essence of this game's logic. In a battle, if just 1 guy is left in a unit and he retreats and is reinforced back to full strength the unit keeps its experience towards veterancy. But if you reinforce the Company as a whole they basically become as green as before the game started and still be at a lower overall strength.
Companies that aren't in battle are supposed to self-reinforce without losing battle experience between turns. I see that's what the game says on the screen, but the manpower gauge doesn't go up enough to be noticeable on Companies not being used in battle to be noticed.
Alternatively, you can choose to bolster your unit's abilities instead of reinforcing the Company itself, but the advantages they provide aren't enough to overcome the losses that are inflicted on each Company in each battle. (And each new ability increases the cost of calling it into play during battle.)
Lastly, the units curse too much and too often. I'm no bible thumper but it gets to the point where you hate clicking on units because they're going to swear at you or make some snide remark. COH was clever and I never tired of hearing the little unit comments as I played the game. I find myself disliking the units the more and more I play this game. There's no good reason for the units to curse to the point where you have to put headphones on to play this game around kids.

Its nightime on the the Meadow and at the beginning, I was a lonely Lynx. After a couple of minutes I found a Badger, then another, then two bunnies and another Lynx - there was also a bear cub. You could see, that we all were made to be friends as we were jumping around and smiling in tandem. Then we got moving, found a stone or two. I was trying to lead the group and let out a big Meow-Howl. It echoed across the meadow - the two bunnies started smiling.
Time went by as we crossed the fields, swam through rivers and took little naps. At some point I noticed that my effort to lead the group was in vain - almost. Everybody was gone and I was looking around - let out a lonely and sad Meow-Howl...and then they came, the two smiling bunnies. They hopped around and we frolicked together before we started running like crazy without a goal in mind through the snowy fields. We saw a waterfall and we were psyched. Happy little animal sounds echoed around me as I was leading my little group towards the giant waterfall. We swam through icy water to get there, but I'll be damned - it was worth it!
We found a long icy tunnel. The light shone bright as we run through the cave. The caves were intertwined and we just followed our instinct until the grass became greener again and once more we were treated to the splashing sound of water. After a little walk, we found a waterfall with a little lake on the bottom surrounded by giant green cliffs. We just stood there and took the scenery in - it was well worth the travel.
Me and my little Bunny-buddies were climbing higher and higher and as we reached the top we stood there in awe - for a moment - then I jumped down the abyss - and they followed. Down at the bottom we were frolicking again and found another Lynx. Together we all relaxed at the lake for a bit - then I had to leave. I didn't want to, but you gotta go while it's good - and it was amazing.
Thanks little Bunny-Buddies - I will find you again!

The Metro games are an incredible addition to an overpopulated and excessively popular genre in which the series nails all odds of the genre's cliches. The Metro franchise initiates in a post-apocolyptic Russia - more specifically Moscow. After being given his first mission to leave his station, young Artyum must face the odds of survival and travel to Polis to meet up with Colonel Miller to seek help for his cause. This involves meeting stranded individuals fighting for their own survival, and passing through stations of which are doomed due to the lack of resources or positioning of their base.
The metro series is based off the active book series, and it really is one of the most immersive first person shooters of this time. I may have a fondness of the genre, but I have watched as this beloved genre has been butchered and disrespected since the original first person shooters were made. This game pays a great deal of respect to the genre, the story and to the PC market in general.
The game caters to any play style, be it stealth, assault, survival or modular. This game is completely completable with spending none of the currency on offer for bullets or weapons. As you progress through the game you'll get better and better weapons but if you need to buy weapons or ammunition you're probably playing it wrong.
It's rich, detailed, scary and beautiful in all respects. It's said that the Russians tell the best repressive stories and this is one shining example of that talent. You'll get to experience the best and the worst in human kind, and every time you play these games you will experience something new - big or little. I've finished this game countless times, in fact I can finish it really quick now, but I will always find something new.
This version of the game was released in order to modernise the game from the original, and to update all the technology behind it. The engine and it's components have evolved from the original, and this arguably comes at a price. I find the modernisation is a good thing in general as there's a consistency among the series now, but some of you may wish to experience the original of which I'm yet to review. The original is much darker, the AI is much better if not too good and takes some adjusting, and I got to confess, I do prefer the textures of the Librarians over the Redux version.
If you enjoy first person shooters, if you enjoy zombies, monsters and scary games, if you love beautiful graphics and a challenge, this is a must own. I've bought the whole series at full price and I've definitely got my moneys worth from it. I have finished each version of the game countless times, and I will finish them all again countless times. In fact the last run of which I've just completed, I completed with more than 1700 military grade points.
One of the few games on Steam with the "Survival" tag that actually is a survival game. You will die.

For me, I thought it would be fun to manage, train, and race my cycling team around the many different circuits.  To outfit the team colors / sponsorship, bike frames, wheels, etc would be nice attributes for a cycling game.
After Purchase:
After downloading nearly 11gigs and doing the install, the game loaded without error and runs fine on my machine using the maximum settings. So, I am not too sure why others had/have crashes, maybe early versions of the game was problematic, I am using 1.3.1, Overall the game is stable and runs fine.
Graphics:
I have no real complaints, the "effects" and rendering are pleasant enough for realism, you have control over the color saturations, and in game special effects.  One thing I did notice is all the duplicate bystanders along the routes, basically you have about 10 different bystander and they repeat which is very obvious, as well as photos of riders.  Not that this matters since each rider is measured by his stats not his photo.  The other minor issue is with vehicles going through riders, mostly at corners.
Camera Angle:
The in game camera allows for a few fixed views, mimicking those angles you would see on TV during a real race. You can step through these using shortcuts or via the side menu.  I do wish they offered a free view, so I could put the camera behind my rider facing the challengers or on the handle bars etc..
Game Play:
Depending on how you approach playing this game will dictate your experience. What I mean by that statement is this game offers a "Career" mode which involves you in every aspect of managing a team; even to the point of scheduling, scouting for new talent, purchasing, salary, picking your team, calendars, answering mail, assigning members to training camps, setting objectives, trying to meet your sponsor objectives for scheduled races. - So, career mode is the long term play mode that involves all the tedious duties necessary to run/manage a racing team. With career mode you will not be immediately racing until you satisfy several pre-season task and for a lot of people this may be too much to do or frustrating.
The game does offers single non-career races that you can participate in. Unlike the career mode nothing in the single race is too overwhelming, You select, go through a few screens and your racing.  So for me this is where I mostly find myself unfortunately due to my aversion of the career mode requirements.  In non-career mode you select your team & riders, set objectives/strategy and show up for the race, then send commands/orders to riders via the riders interface.
What’s wrong for me?
In Non-career; I feel detached from the game and my team. During races, I simply move some sliders around an position riders as the race progresses.
I want to like this game so much, but it does not contain enough substance to keep me drawn in.  I wish there was a simple TEAM mode where you choose team members, have the ability to take your team to training areas within a country/local and build up experience, fitness and other attributes and develop sponsorship as you build up and win races.
Final Thoughts:
CYANIDE founded a great franchise in "cycling”, there is room for improvement in several areas and I hope the game evolves to include more interaction and involvement with actual building of characters dialog with team members and with the inclusion of 3D training routes you can take your team to increase their attributes in real time.  Overall the game does offer cycling fans enough to keep them coming back for races and if you so desire,  a career mode for those who like diving deep into the management aspect.  For me, I would prefer a more streamlined “Team Mode”option.
Is it worth $$, if you like or are a fan of cycling – yes,
If you want to deep dive or have a desire to manage a cycling team – Yes, this is the only game in town.
If you want real-time 3D “character” race simulation and control – probably is not worth spending your $ on.

I have used this software for many hours before I started using the steam version.
Blender, probably the best 3D modelling software out there with common features that other competing software have and especially with its free price tag, it attracts a large amount of people. However due to its somewhat small artist and tutorial community, there are not all the resources that some poeple may need to fully understand the software fully (although recently its getting a larger and larger community). I definetly recommend this software if you are even slightly interested in CG.
Blender, a free and open-source alternative to the often expensive and huge 3D software suites. Blender, although relatively small in size compared to its rivals, definetly can create the same results as other 3D software. The software at first glance seems very intimidating, but is actually very nicely laid out in terms of efficency and definetly increases your workflow speed as a result. One of the huge advantages of Blender, is that its more than just a 3D modelling tool, but multiple tools intergrated into the application. It has modelling, sculpting, material creation, rendering, camera tracking and even a video editor. Blender has a node-based render engine, which may seem also complicated, but is very powerful as it can pull of stunning and realistic renders and effects. Blender has come a long way from its original roots and is definetly on its way to become a industry-standard 3D modelling suite.

So, played this a bunch. Bought it at Beta, been playing it since.. Launch fixed and broke a lot of things..
The Good:
--The critical system is a little less random at high health now. (believe me, this is good.)
--Ships for each race move and feel very unique.
--Chaos got buffed.
--Good art.
--Ships are wonderful to look at, shoot with, and blow up.
--RAMMING.
--Ships have inertia, so turns are almost always MUCH wider than you might expect.
--Story Follows the 12-13th Black Crusades from GW's Eye of Terror World Wide Campaign
(good story)
The Bad:
---EVE-Online AI Move options ('go here then stop and shoot' or 'circle and shoot with broadsides only.')
this doesnt help anyone that has forward firing guns, which is good because...
---Eldar. They got nurfed hard. This isnt totally a bad thing as they were nearly unkillable during beta, but now they are fragile and take significantly more damage from macrobattery ships even with full defence buff, and since they are insanely fragile, they have become insane glass  cannons.
---Truely horrible player-side AI. Some of the AI's pathing choices are down right awful, especially when playing less tanky races like chaos and eldar where stuff needs to be doing the right thing, or its dead.
half the time you will be babying your line ships only to find an escort found a minefield and still decided to fly though it, or, instead of turning AWAY from a closing enemy ship, it will turn towards it while on auto, or worse, toward a near by ally, creating evil micromanagement hell. Thank god for bullet-time, but even that wont save you all the time.
---Strike Craft. these are.. not great. worse, only a few ships carry them and they are kinda dedicated to it.
-Fighters are redundent.
-Boarding Pods are good but iffy.
-Bombers are lackluster against anything other than escorts.
With No counter to keep track of reamining craft so its kind of a crap shoot how many runs they will get before they are out (yes very much like the tabletop, just bombers are way less rewarding).
---Would really have liked to see ships that are assigned a numbered group sticking in formation - moving the same way, changing facing the same way, staying together, while not smashing into each other, and being able to fire similar weapons at the same time..
---They got rid of hotkeying groups?
TL;DR
Its not a bad game, but its not a great game. Its based heavily on awesome movement mechanics but there are very few options that allow you to make use of them effectively, and as you scale into larger and larger fleet battles simply making your fleet do what you want gets compoundingly more brutal.

That said...
This game is harsh, unforgiving, seems to take delight in causing you mental anguish, and has nearly been responsible for the rage-induced destruction of my computer on more than one occasion. Just about everything and everyone seems intent on ruining your day and your ship, and most of them have the weaponry to do so. Mistakes are punished rapidly and severely, and even when everything seems to be going swimmingly, a great big warm cluster♥♥♥♥ may very well be waiting for you at the next Jump Beacon.
To me, FTL is well worth the $10. It's a great way to kill time, and it has a way of drawing you in; on many occasions I've started it to play for a few minutes and found myself there an hour or two later, still immersed. The appreciable variety of ships and the variations thereof that must each be unlocked certain ways keeps the replay value high and gives you something to strive for, and the feeling when you finally beat that motherless Flagship is wonderful; only bested by when you accidentally stumble upon a new ship. 10/10

Game Play   ------->                8.8/10
-Plot
The plot of the game is very basic.  You are being pursued and essentially need to upgrade your ship in order
to prepare for the final battle.  Once you get into the game there are a TON of mini plots and mini missions.
I've played this game a lot and have seen many of these mini quests/missions only once though they follow a
generic formula.  They each have radically different potential outcomes.  Example of these in a generic
sense:
Helping an alien ship to get to location, A ship in need of fuel, or decoding an alien code.  They all have
different outcomes.  You  may get nothing for helping someone, or if you  give someone fuel you might get
reward  with a secret weapon, or you may even get reward with the powerful weapon in the game.
-Controls
Are very simple.  Essentially the controls are moving your characters around your ship and pointing at which
compartment you want to  fire at in an enemy ship and with what type of weapon.
- Playability
The game is different each time you play.  You'll get different missions and you'll find different weapons
even from the stores.  Even when you destroy and enemy, you might get a different weapon/drone.  Even
though  it does have a random component to it, it still follows a generic formula though sometimes they'll
put a  random surprise in there.
Sound        ------->                 7.8/10
The music very much does help with the atmosphere.  Though like Interstellar (the movie) the music can get
annoying and irritating after some extensive game play.
Graphics   ------->                  6.1/10
If you're playing this game for the graphics or hoping for great graphics this game isn't for you.  The
graphics are not amazing but you can easily tell what everything is for it does have detail.
Difficulty    ------->                 9.3/10
This game is very difficult.  I've only played it on normal and have continually gotten destroyed.
Replay       -------->                 10/10
This game has a lot of replayability.  Sometimes, you'll hope for a certain outcome or mission that has a
certain reward, don't bank on getting them.
Game Value (this is the value that I WOULD pay for the game.  This value is not necessarily how much I ACTUALLY paid for the game).
I would pay in the low 20s and no more than 25 for this game.  This game is a gem find if it is less than 10
and or even at 5, you will not be disappointed. If you see it 10 or less, pick it up.
Overall Rating  ------------->   42/50
Issues/Complaints:
If you are looking for a linear game, this game isn't for you.  You can be doing great and get a bunch of
random crapshot one after another and before you know it you've been destroyed.  Example:  You can be
doing well and go to a planet that has solar flares where you always will have to fight someone.  It seems
that these flares ALWAYS impacts you and every rare occasion impacts your opponent.  I have issue with
that.  Since the system has solar flares, you might not have time to fix up your ship, so you'll have to make
a jump.  Then, you might get boarded and be attacked.  Which I'm fine with.  When I get boarded I send
everyone except for the captain to the medic area and open all the doors to kill the intruders.  This helps
to filter them to the medic room but it never kills them.  Which is frustrating because it kills me pretty fast
and not the computer.  Games like this really makes me wish the opponent was held to the same
constraints that I am held to.
Final Thoughts
If you are the type of person who has to win every time (example if you play FIFA/NHL and you have to win ever single game) this game probably isn't for you.  This is a rogue game, which means that random events can kill you (it won't be a mystery though of what killed you) and you'll lose everything when you die. Alright, I originally purchased the game for 60% off (£15.99 ish) and completed it almost entirely within a day (the day of writing this review), so get ready for some fresh opinions. On the whole, I would give Dying Light a minimum of a 7/10 in terms of gameplay. Now, this game has a lot to offer so I will try to break it down in more digestible segments:
STORYLINE
I have not read other reviews for Dying Light, so I am unsure what the general concensus is on the storyline. However, I wholeheartedly enjoyed the storyline, and towards the end I felt genuine investment in the characters. Other open-world games seem to have their storylines take a backseat (Oblivion and Skyrim in particular), however in Dying Light there is lore everywhere. Regardless of whether it is a main or side mission, the story is engaging and well fleshed out, leading to an enjoyable quasi-cinematic experience if you are partial to a game with a solid storyline. My one criticism is the choice for the final boss fight, which comes in the form of a quick time event. Some may argue that this is one way of sticking to the writer's idea of the story while still engaging the player, however it came out of the blue and ruined the immersion of the storyline. A cinematic is far better at conveying the finale of a game than a QTE, which often disjoints the impact of the scene.
MOVEMENT
With the game being presented as a parkour-esque zombie survival game, you would expect that there would be fluidity of movement and good parkour integration, and you would be completely correct. The movement fits very well into the action of the game, and the upgrade system allows more complex movement mechanics to be involved without becoming too clunky. For example, the stamina system for parkour provides little stamina in the beginning of the game, but this raises proportionally with the action of the game such that in chase sequences throughout the game the movement feels good, without giving the impression that you are effortlessly fleeing from your enemies. Night time chases are still absolutely terrifying, by the way. That all being said, the movement is not without issue; some sections of the game (such as the final sequence) heavily rely on it's movement system, and can sometimes fall flat with clipping issues, resulting in premature deaths.
COMBAT
Combat takes a very similar style to that of Dead Island, taking a more melee centric focus with little variation of ranged firearms. To some this may seem like it would detract from the experience, however the game sets up a scenario in which ranged firearms are equally devastating to you and your opponent, quickly dispatching them while at the same time drawing more enemies towards you. That, and the relative rarity of bullets for pistols, rifles and shotguns means that ammunition is often reserved for the more dangerous enemies: the bosses and bandits. Overall I would say that the combat is very solid and contributes well to the experience of the game. One key improvement would be to include an "analog" style weapon system as featured in Dead Island, such that you can control the angle and direction of swing (making decapitations or specific attacks more reliable). Despite this, the currently implemented combat system is on expectation in comparison to similar games.
GAME ISSUES
If you are running on a lower end computer, there are some sections of the game which become quite problematic, especially with heavy particle effects. That seems to be the only issue with the game itself.
It's a fantastic game, and as of writing this it is 66% percent off, and I would easily reccomend this game for all types of gamer.
That being said, I probably won't play the game anymore, but that is just me.

TL;DR - You will highly enjoy it if you like exploration and collecting things to unlock more things. You'll enjoy it even more if you meet up with other players or bring your friends!
Full Review
Meadow is fantastic and refreshing (I can't believe it's only $3). I literally would have paid $29.99 for this game, or at least $19.99.
I have a lot of great things to say about this game. As usual, it is a marvelous illustration of artwork, both in audio and visual, brought to you by some incredibly talented developers. These guys are artists, not big game developers, yet they have brought us multiple games that each have very positive reviews. That says something about the content these guys put out there for us to enjoy. It's incredible and worth spreading the word about.
There is no reason at all that this title should ever receive a negative review. The few negative reviews I have seen are people complaining about not being able to type in a global chat, having to own previous titles by Might and Delight to unlock certain animals, the eagle not having as many emoticons as other animals, and optimization (which isn't a problem unless you have a crappy processor - you need at least 2.6 GHz). These reviews are unfair, in my opinion, and I'll tell you why I feel this way:
First off, not having a chat box in the game is one of the most interesting things about Meadow. The developers have implemented a system of communication using nicely illustrated emoticons (expressive and directional). These emoticons have worked perfectly for players who are patient and willing to learn how they are best used to communicate with other players. Adding a global chat into the game would completely ruin the experience. The emoticons would be pointless and there would be more bickering in chat than there would be gameplay. Not to mention, the entire atmosphere of the game would be different. Everyone is so friendly and helpful in Meadow because they are strongly encouraged to explore together, and they do this without any biasedness. If there was a global chat, players would divide into groups of friends, leaving anyone not apart of that group feeling left out or intrusive. Meaning, ultimately, the atsmophere would feel less welcoming. Also, trying to hunt for runestones and puzzle pieces would be less fun/challenging if people were calling out locations.
Secondly, this is a $3 game. For $3, you get a massive wilderness to explore with other online players, and four different animals (baby badger, rabbit, frog, and goat) with dozens of skins and emotes. That seems like a really good bargain to me. I don't think it's fair that people should complain about having to purchase other titles in order to unlock animals like the adult badger, adult lynx, baby lynx, and baby bear. Each of these animals has their own story, and I think players should experience their stories before being able to play them in Meadow. These animals are meant to be bonuses for people who own their previous games, Shelter, Shelter 2, and Paws: A Shelter 2 Game (seriously, I felt like it was a really nice extra for having already owned their previous games, like the devs were thanking us for supporting them). These games are fantastic, and honestly, they aren't really that expensive on the Steam store. So the fact that people are complaining about having to buy other games if they don't already own them, is kind of petty. Might and Delight are wonderful and talented developers, and if you enjoy this game enough to want to unlock other species, then you should be glad to support them by purchasing their other titles. Hopefully the increase in sales will encourage Might and Delight to add more into Meadow in terms of other playable animals, emoticons, actions, etc.
Finally, the eagle complaints have got to stop! Guys, come on. The eagle is not broken, and it does not need to be "fixed." If the eagles were given the same directional emoticons as other animals, then eagle players would just fly around and look for runestones and then lead other players directly to runestones, which completely defeats the purpose of the game! Also, it wouldn't be fair to let eagles collect essence and puzzle pieces because they would have a completely unfair advantage over other players who are also collecting essence to make it onto the leaderboards.
If anything could be changed or added to the game, I would suggest a quick intro or tutorial for first time players. You really have to explore and learn as you go, but a lot of players seem to get confused because the objective of the game may not be clear to them. Because of this, I thought I would throw in a few tips that I've learned since I started playing Meadow:
1.) You can change animals by going to The Den/Main Menu and actually clicking on the animals sleeping in the background. A lot of people had a hard time figuring this out, so I thought it should be the first tip.
2.) You can view other player's names by pressing the right Alt button on your keyboard. You can change this key in your control settings. I use E because it's easier to press.
3.) You can hit P to open your Puzzle Progress. Pink puzzle pieces reward you with essence and help you unlock new emoticons, blue crystals reward you with new skins for the animal you're currently playing, and yellow crystals help you unlock new playable animals.
4.) You can hit M to look at the map, which is more like a radar. It shows you the center tree, and all of the white icons indicate other online players. Generally it's a good idea to run to a cluster of players. Exploring alone is fun, but exploring with others is a whole new experience!
5.) If you press your middle mouse button, you can use your senses to see nearby players.
6.) Runestones are black obelisks that can be unlocked with two or more players. The symbols indicate what you need in order to open the runestone. Runestones contain blue or yellow crystals. It's worth exploring with a group so that you can unlock runestones.
7.) You can use F to auto walk forward, and R to toggle autorun (pair these together for the best results, imo).
Another suggestion that I think would satiate the community's desire to contact the players they meet within the game is to allow your servers to send info to Steam so that we can Shift+Tab and look at the "View Players" list. We can already see the names of the players we are playing with, but trying to find them on Steam can be a challenge if their name is more common. It would be easier if we could look under "View Players" or our "Recent Players," which derives from the "View Players," list.
This game truly is relaxing and a world of fun. I really hope that Might and Delight continues to add more content. Perhaps they will expand the world into more biomes for us to explore and add new unlockable characters/skins/emotes. My fingers are crossed for foxes and porcupines in the future of Meadow! Thank you so much for such a pleasant experience, Might and Delight! Keep up the incredible work!

it's an improved version of quake 3. it's the best first person shooter overall when you look at all the different modes and maps it has to offer.
almost no other shooter has high quality 1v1, high quality free-for-all, and high quality team modes that work perfectly whether it's 2v2 or 8v8. and some of the modes can even have more strategy than most RTS games.
most FPS games are primarily about aim, but this game rewards many more skills. there are no headshots or things that do tons of damage instantly, so the game has a lot more diversity. every fight is an actual battle with a lot of back-and-forth, not just about getting a lucky shot against someone who was looking the other way.
some other fps games have balance problems. this has none because there are no classes or different sides or different weapons for different players or things to unlock or upgrade or purchase. every player has equal access to everything in the game from the moment they start playing.
this game has extremely responsive controls and great UI customization options, so the only thing that matters is your skill, not how well you adjust to the interface. if there's anything you don't like about the visuals or the controls, just change it. everything can be as clear as you want it to be, so that it's always easy to know what's going on.
everything behaves properly and accurately in this game, as opposed to a lot of modern games where there are lots of calculations that add lag and make it unclear whether your shots are going to hit or miss. the engine is so good that playing against people thousands of miles away in quake feels much better than playing most modern games on LAN.
steam says i've played 2 hours, but i played thousands of hours of the non-steam version and thousands of hours of quake 3 before that. the game never gets old because it's practically flawless.

Meadow is an exploration/social experience from the creators of the Shelter series.
In terms of gameplay, Meadow is rather simple. You enter the world as a small, brown badger cub and your primary objective will be to collect colourful little shapes in order to unlock emotes, skins and utlimately, new characters. To do so, you can either explore the land in search of individual collectables OR you can team up with other players in search of standing stones. These monuments are scattered around the map and require varying combinations of animal calls in order to be pillaged. That's your bread and butter.
Your secondary goal will be to collect essence (score) in order to advance up the leaderboard. You can also earn a few emotes this way. It's worth noting that the devs are adding more unlockables as time goes on, so you can expect there to be more incentive when collecting essence in the future.
Visually, this game is a bit hit or miss. Either you enjoy the patchwork, polygonal style, or you don't. If you're a returning fan of the devs work, you'll probably feel right at home with the art style, however I can see newcomers being turned away by it's simplicity. I will agree that the music and atmosphere are fantastic.
As a social experience, Meadow is quite refreshing. The traditional text chat is replaced by cutesy emotes and adorable squeaks, most of which are implemented already but others are still being added (for free, I might add). You'll need to be quite creative in how you communicate with your pals, which is always fun. It's worth noting that there aren't any real threats in Meadow, so this limited interactivity doesn't exactly hold the same consequences it might have done in Shelter.
Now there is no denying that for everything this game does right, there are a few shortcomings.
The game itself is actually quite poorly optimised, and on top of this players report considerable frame drops when playing on heavily populated servers. Luckily, the devs have been working hard to fix this.
This next point is really the dealbreaker.
Meadow boasts a selection of 9 different playable animals. Sadly, the average player will only have access to 4 of these when paying full price for the game.
This is because the majority of the unlockable animals are tucked away behind paywalls, requiring the player to have purchased previous titles by the devs in order to unlock them (In order to obtain all content included in the game you'd have to pay something in the region of 30 to 40 pounds!). This might have been acceptable if it didn't comprise such a large portion of the game, somewhere around 30% of the content if you consider that the whole premise of the game is to gain new animals, emotes and skins.
Still, I'd have to recommend this game for what it offers, regardless of how much it hides. For what I payed (£1.99, a steal!), I've gotten a good amount of playtime out of it already and I still find myself coming back. I'd certainly recommend that you at least give it a go, and hopefully the developers will be able to iron out some of their optimisation issues in the future.

Well then, battlefleet gothic: Armada, here we go 'sigh'.
to start off i feel like this game does justice to the universe of warhammer 40k, especially the tabletop game it was based on.
but...well...it's just something of a mess at the moment, even though the game itself plays well, has great textures and has a ok campaign, it's very reminisant of that RTS vibe 40k has for games on pc, yet it also fails on alot of points, and it's very sad for a veteran 40k player like me to see that it's kinda going down the pan like alot of other 40k games.
The grinding:
leveling in battlefleet gothic is mind numbingly slow, i'd get it a good 11 hours to get everything for a SINGLE faction in skirmish/multiplayer and the harder you put it on, the longer your going to have to grind, your going to spend WAY to long on each faction, and for just the 4 factions there are at the moment it feeling very pointless, it's almost like they made it that way so you can buy your way to get the best ships. there is also the very silly ship damage system, to put it simply, if you lose a ship in a battle your not getting that ship back for probably 1-3 missions, unless you give the game your well earned ingame money to make it repair quicker or just repair it completely which can be quite hefty if you have lost alot of ships.
the micromanageing:
'sigh' this is a major problems, i have never played a game with so much micromanageing, the put it in a big picture, you HAVE to be the npc to be able to perfectly manage your fleet, when your fleet has almost a dozen ships all with special abilites, turning menouvers, weapon ranges, ship angle or side checking, 'click this button to fire' weapons, and watching the battle aswell, you start to realise that the game is completely over the top for a person to do, and if you mess up you will probably end up ramming your own ships or hitting them with your own torpedos and cannons and never mind the fact that your fleet goes limp when they say destroy an enemy ship that you told them to destroy and then just do nothing (EVEN THOUGH THERE IN THE MIDDLE OF A BATTLE GETTING SHOT AT).
The ability system:
see, in the tabletop game you only got to use 1 ability per turn, but in this you can just spam abilites to your hearts contempt, then just wait a bit and start spaming again, this wouldn't be a problem if the abilites wern't so overpowered, throw a load of stasis bombs and watch the entire enemy fleet just freeze while you shoot the hell out of them then watch all your shots pound into them as they can avoid them and end up totaling there capital ships or escorts, this is even worse when combind with plasma bombs or lance turrets, then there the fact that EVERY faction has the same abliltes which make no sence considering that some of those abilites don't need to be in certain factions.
and finaly!
The ungodly unbalancing:
here's the thing, the beta was meant to sort out the overpowered from the underpowered, for instance, the nova cannon, also known as 'the critical existance failure cannon' which was nerfed into the not very used territory, then there was the fun perk of WMP or micro warp jump, in the beta you could jump a ship literaly into another ships path and smash then into each other like as if it was navel warfare in the greek times, but yet that was nerfed to, now you can only jump at a certain distance near another ship, so no more super warp ramming, but you see, thats just ablities and weapons, the worst part is that the stuff that needed balancing never got balanced.
see, in the multiplayer, lets say you play the imperial navy and your opponent is playing eldar corsairs and the mission is data recovery, which is basicaly nick the important stuff off each other then run away, normally this would be a balanced fun and alos quite tense game, but in reality you will get outrun, out menauvered and in some cases, out gunned, you can micromanage all you want but there is almost no way your going to win, you spend all your time running after their ship and when you finally catch up to it your opponent will just boost his way out and warp to saftey because he is outside of your striking range, or in the case of ork, just ram the crap out of your ships, and if that doesn't kill you then his torpedos or boarding assaults will cripple you to hell, then in the case of chaos, just sit out of your weapons range and send a baggillion bombers the blow up your ships, which is the same as what eldar do. but lets not forget about the imperium, just meh, there good but to be honest you'll be out-everythinged at some point.
look, im not saying the game is bad, it's just....well....not enjoyable, the problems seriously damage the fun aspect, not to mention that the trailers are VERY missleading.
there are no massive space battles, just small scale mini battles.
there is no team or friend joining, it's all random.
and it's very hard to get used to, especially the keybinds.
what i'll say is, the game is ok, it's not anything special, it's not really that enjoyable and it can seriously annoy you at points the multiplayer and skirmish.
but for a game of it's type it does quite well, the campaigns fun, the ships look FANTASTIC and look even better with a special skin which gives you a few extra skills or upgrades and i think this could be the best feeling FPS i've played in a long time.
so...final verdict....what i'd say is, save your money untill they fix the major problems, at the moment it's not good, but keep checking up on it because it will eventually get sorted one way or another...but like i said, save your money for now, or get homeworld 2 remastered for roughly the same price.
i'll give battlefleet gothic: armada at it's current state 5/10.

This is one of the few games that the enemy is actually trying to defeat you and not lay idle in order for you to win, which means, many people will get angry about how difficult it is. The point is, its not difficult, you just need to learn it.
I do not play multiplayer so  i will talk about the campaign.
Generally
It is played in turns. In each turn you get deployment phases, where you choose which battles you will play. The battles are real in time. You get to upgrade your ships, your crew, your systems, pretty much everything. After some time, you even get to give "favour" to your ships, which means you ordain it under an imperium organization. You can have an adeptus mechanicus, or an inquisition ship. Each favour has some certain percs. By the way, all of the ships are there. From the escorts, light cruisers, to the huge battleships (and of course all their sub types).
Every upgrade you will do, you will do it with renown.
Dynamic
The game in general is partially dynamic. Which means that the main missions are scripted (although if you choose to replay them it will be on a different map) but the side missions are totally dynamic. The orc raids, the eldar raids, the exterminatus missions where you have to win in order to save the planet, the chaos champions vessels, all dynamic. If you loose on a main mission (or any mission) the game continues. Its not like you have to win everything.
Ships
If you loose a ship, it stays dead for two rounds unless you pay to fix it.
Length
Thing of the campaign as a funnel. It is narrow at the beginning, and broadens slowly. At first you will think it is easy. After some turns it get bigger and then, you have a full invasion. Your mission is to stop the chaos crusade. If you play it on easy, its an average campaing. Play it on a more difficult level and you will never forget it.
Difficulty
If you grasp the basics of the game, you can win in easy. There will be some times that you will lose of course. Yep, you can loose in this game and move forward. You can always save before a fight in order to win everywhere. My personal opinion is to play it on easy, defeat it, and then play it in a more difficult level under iron man (where you are not able to save the game wherever you want, and every ship you'll loose, you loose it for good), in order to feel how a real warhammer game is
Overall
If you want a game with a good strategy, fair difficulty (if you are willing to learn) and epic battles, buy it.

Many members of the community insist on referring to FTL as a "roguelike" however we shall forgive this error and judge this pixel-art, trendy, indie puzzle game slash strategy sim for what it is--alright it's a ♥♥♥♥ing roguelike, fine!
FTL: Faster Than Light, the sole offering to date by Subset Games offers a selection of roguelike-worthy challenges well beyond other indie offerings despite eschewing the traditional form of the genre. The game forces strategic foresight and consistency from the macroscopic, character building (in this case ship-building) level down to hyper-tight management during combat encounters. Randomness is similarly introduced into playthroughs on myriad levels. Each game requires pathing through a selection of sectors--think dungeon floors--whose distinct challenges and rewards must be balanced against the particular strengths of the ship. Within each sector the captain meanders her ship as slowly as possible to the exit, staying ahead of the advancing rebel fleet whose ominous advance serves well as an anti-grinding mechanic.
Individual combat encounters are the meat of this game and designers Justin Ma and Matthew Davis have married tactical play and tense timing superbly well. These encounters play out in real time, though the player can (and should) pause as often as is wanted. Though pausing shifts the primary skills from action-oriented to tactical, precise timing remains critical. It is exhilarating to destroy critical systems on an enemy ship with a synchronized volley seconds before they are able to attack. A subtler triumph of the game's combat is each encounter's long-term import. You cannot afford to take a beating every fight: the cost of repairs will hamper the development of a ship capable of tackling the mounting challenges of later sectors.
I judge FTL by the higher standards imposed by its classification as a roguelike and it defiantly impresses on most fronts. However, there are a few relatively minor failings. My most critical criterion for a successful roguelike is that performing the optimal strategy must not be boring. Playing FTL well is mostly just as enjoyable as learning how the game works, but there is some potential for grinding your crew's skills during non-threatening encounters. Employing this strategy provides a small enough advantage that it ought to be ignored but that it is possible irks me. Unlocking the secondary layouts for each ship requires the player to perform two out of three prescribed achievements. Some of these tasks are fairly uninteresting and I would prefer not to have to undertake them.
FTL will stand as an exemplar of indie development for years to come. Players willing to learn the game's unique mechanics will be rewarded with a balanced, intense, and altogether thrilling flight through the galaxy.

There are so few bad things I can say about this game. One is that it's pretty hard to beat, two is... nevermind, it's just that one. But when it gets right down to it, beating the game isn't that important.  This game is immensely fun at every part, and your decisions will greatly affect your fate. There will be sectors you don't like, choices you wish you hadn't made, and many other parts that you will probably dislike a lot. Despite that, the fun persists always, even while your ship is being blown to smithereens. And then you'll click the new game button. Again. And again. And again.
And at some point, you'll have finally defeated the rebel flagship, earned new achievements, and... unlocked a new ship? Every ship is a new angle on the same game, requiring quite different strategies. This is why it is again so much fun to be destroyed once more. And once more you'll click new game. Again. And again. And again.
Perhaps the fact that you don't beat the flagship every time improves the game even further. It requires you to play more decisively and carefully, keeping you wondering if you'll win this time around. If you beat the flagship everytime, you probably wouldn't start a new game. Instead, your mouse is drawn towards the button. Again. And again. And again.
One of these days you'll enable Advanced Edition. New weapons, new events, new race, even more fun. And you'll be even more excited to click that darned, time-wasting new game button. Again. And again. And again.
Why do you continue to play again? Because the possibilities are literally endless.
If you choose to buy the game: Play on easy. And try the Captain's Edition mod once you beat the flagship at least once.

Braid is really tough. The writting and level design are really worth bearing through it though. Itts a puzzle playformer that involves worlds with different rules. Note - If you are visually impared you can still play this game. The story is told mostly through writting, but it isn't too tiny, and there aren't that many lines to read. At worst case you can screenshot the bits of story. Another difficulty you might come accross involves identifying things that glow in a particular color. This is related to the physics of each world you encounter, so you may need to pay extra attention, especially with yellow glows cos the enemies in the game are mainly that color.

As a puzzle designer, Braid has possibly the best puzzle design I've ever seen in a game.
All the rules of game design are followed here. The mechanics are introduced well. But what really struck me is that the puzzles in this game are prime examples of what I call parsimony. This means that every piece is essential: nothing could be removed without fundamentally changing the puzzle. This limits the scope of the puzzles, so you can keep all the parts in your head. But parsimoniously made puzzles also leave you with a sense of satisfaction at how well they work.
Other than that, the visuals are great. The story is good, but I wasn't *that* enraptured by the philosophical presentation of it all. The ending is particularly brilliant, though. The gameplay is not 100% mental: you'll need some hand-eye coordination here and there. It's pretty forgiving, though.
If you appreciate precision design that's clever like clockwork, I highly recommend Braid.

I was very "on the fence" about this game when I first heard about the, supposedly, numerous problems that plague this "terrible" pc port. I'd pretty much decided to give it a swerve instead of effectively "doubling down" on it (I also have DOA 5 on xbox) but when I actually played it I changed my mind. I also changed my mind for a couple of other reasons that I shall detail below.
First out I think it's important to address the "soft engine" debacle. This is basically an option for tv tanned virgins to enable which, apparently, makes the "boobies" (as they're childishly being referred to online in the myriad of "DOA5LR Y U ASSHURT ME?" videos on youtube) look more "real". Seriously ? Go outside. Failing that, maybe consider ending your own existence ?
For people to whine about the fact that the most miniscule, unimportant facet of the game isn't identical to the next gen console versions (soft engine isn't on the xbox 360/ps3 versions, either) is just laughable. Grow up, maybe ?
It does seem somewhat pathetic that team ninja even include this as a "bonus" (along with the "OMG" 'boobie' physics model that is unlockable) but, then, considering the extra curricular activities of the head of team ninja it is, perhaps, hardly surprising (master sex criminal/sexual supervillain). However, to rally against the community and threaten to make no more pc conversions if the mod scene produce nude patches for the characters (which they already have. Sigh....) is a little "rich" in my book. You can't have your sex offending cake AND eat it.
Anyway, 'boobies' and 'nekkid' stuff aside, once I actually played this game I was more than happy to fork out the money for it for a fair few reasons. Here are some bullet points....
- Anti Aliasing: The game looks amazing with this. Way sweeter than even the next gen versions, imo (which don't have it). Everything goes from jaggy looking, last gen style to smooth, silky, modern and cool. The AA is applied to everything, not just the characters, so the (somewhat jaded) backdrops also look much better with this applied
- 4K !!! PS4 and XBOX ONE games actually run this in 1080p, which is a big change for these systems as usually everything is run in a resolution below this. Presumably they can cope as there's "not much going on". Anyway, PC can run it at 4K and it looks genuinely awesome. It also runs very well on this resolution, compared to a lot of other current games which seem to require titans/dual 980's to do so. Also, at 4K you don't need anti-aliasing as everything is so, so fine without it.
- Sweet FX. Okay, this is an external modification BUT it makes the game look even more awesome. I've had a problem with team ninjas choice of colour for a long time and this basically gives you the chance to fix it. The main problem I have with their colourschemes is their apparent lack of ability to use BLACK. They just use charcoal/washed out dark grey and it always looks crappy. Ninja Gaiden could have looked so much sweeter if they'd blasted the contrast and upped the black significantly. He's meant to be a ninja, I believe they semi rely on the dark, no ? The same is true of DOA5LR, everything has a slightly "washed out" look to it. I'm really not sure why, aside from making the deduction that they like things like this. Perhaps their penchant for "the grey area" is a throwback to their boss citing it as his defence in his multiple and frequent deflections of the sexual harrassment suits that are levelled against him ? Who knows. Anyway, installing Sweet FX (a tiny and simple program) gives the game a look that really "pops" (there are multiple colourschemes/filters so you don't have to 'go radioactive' straight away, just find one you like)
- FAST !! The game loads REALLY fast, even on a standard HD, though I have now moved it over to my SSD where it, pretty much, does everything instantly. Really good. I played DOA a lot in its various incarnations on the console and it's never been as rapid as this. #PCMASTERRACE
- Mod scene. Aside from the obligatory "I'm a virgin/I am so dumb that I can't find pron on the internet" naked patches I forsee a great future for this game in terms of things being patched in by the modding community. There's already numerous Sweet FX presets to make the game look substantially better and it's been out less than a week. It seems that it is indeed, as far as the community suggest, fully mod-able so I look forward to seeing what people come up with in future. I hope it's not too much to expect perhaps some older stages decompiled from console versions and patched in.
That's pretty much the "pros" for now, so here are a few "cons" just to balance things out
- Front end is a little ugly. Doesn't really matter, tbh, the game looks great but still, it looks very played out/last gen and could have looked a lot nicer.
- No online (so far). I don't really care about this as I find fighters are usually pretty crappy online what with having to learn lag breaks and all that (there's even an option to simulate online lag in offline play included, though, lol, so you can get used to this "wonderful phenomenon"). However, I'm sure the lack of opportunity for getting absolutely hammered by Japanese players with the gaming equivalent of severe autism will upset some players. Cry me a river and drown yourselves. Just WAIT - it's apparently coming in 3 months or less. Maybe.
- No keyboard control rebinding. Let's be honest, though, what kind of cretin wants to play a fighting game on a keyboard. Get a controller or an arcade stick. Failling that, tie yourself to the front of a large vehicle and have a friend drive it into a wall. Repeatedly.
- DLC. I thought I was dreaming when I saw the price of it. WTF ? Seriously, folks ? the price is absolutely ridiculous for what amounts to, basically, aesthetic changes and nothing more. Still, if LOL and DOTA can get away with it..... I hope they bring some stage DLC and don't charge a ridiculous amount for it. That would be much more welcome than this soft-porn masturbatory material which is clearly pumped out (pun not intended) for those driven myopic by acts of furious DOA based onanism...
- Streaming. So far I've been unable to get the game to stream onto my other computer, which is odd as the "less legit" version I tested before buying the steam version streamed fine from steam as a non-steam game added to my list. This is nonsense and there seems to be no reason for this to happen. It also locks up/freezes my host computer so I need to shut down and restart steam each time to play it again otherwise it doesn't accept inputs. A small issue to some but I do like to stream to my laptop so this is bugging for me.
Right, so, in conclusion, there is nothing much against recommending this game as far as I can say, the only major gripe I have is with the streaming as mentioned above. Ignore the haters and complainers online and enjoy what is, in my opinion, the finest fighting game ever made (which has the potential to get soooo much better thanks to community interaction)

This game has so much potential to be great, unfortunately it has just a few flaws that do enough damage to ruin the game.
You'll see a lot of people give positive reviews without actually playing the game often. I don't know the origin behind this, maybe they got the game really cheap or free and decided it was worth it and that's all that matters. I bought the four pack for $2, but I won't let that impact my review at all because I see the bigger picture that I'm probably not going to play the game a whole lot, no matter how much I want to try and play the game.
The game's positives are many. You have a variety of levels that all have their unique game modes associated to it. Think of it like Mario Kart but much more variety.
You have this unique take of Tag where sometimes the person it loses points rather than gains, which is closer to the traditional sense of tag (the person "it" would want to tag someone) and then sometimes it gets "flipped" where the person it gets points, thus wanting to run away from the other players. If the player reaches zero points, the ability to become it is then in the middle of the map. Additionally, there is weapons in the middle of the map you can gather as well. First player to get a full bar of points wins.
You also have this cool soccer ball mode where you obviously got to get the sockerball into the goal using either your own vehicle or a boxing glove to act like a kick. You have racing and probably numerous more. They're all great ideas and were well thought out.
The game has a garage menu option where you customize your character and vehicle. Not only do you get to select the stuff your character wears or your vehicle style and its wheels, but you also get to customize everything's color with all colors possible using this box and its slider that adjusts brightness (color grid or something, forgot what it's called). The vehicle styles range from your typical vehicle to a tank, my favorite is the skull vehicle. The wheel options are good as well, some are goofy and some are less goofy. I picked the tires with spikes on them to match my skull car. I have the skeleton character and I made him wear the bugging out eyes and a top hat. Yes, you can even customize the color of your character.
The game has an alright soundtrack. It isn't good, it isn't bad. It's just fine. No complaints from me. The graphics style is cartoony, but it's enjoyable for all ages despite it.
Now for some of the negatives that absolutely ruins the game, thus its low price and obscurity. The items the game has does have a healthy variety, not to the scale of Mario Kart or even Jak X: Combat Racing, but the variety is fine. I would have liked to have seen more variety however.The items, however, can also ruin the game for the player using them.
In the game mode, Flipped, you gotta tag people, remember? Well, with the force shield, nobody can touch you and you cannot touch anyone, so how do you tag people when you need to? Flawed design. The force shield also doesn't protect you from everything but rather the players actual vehicle, so bombs and stuff appear to still hit you... unless that's a bug.
Additionally, some weapons help the player you're using them against more than yourself. Bombs, for example, can blow the player forward and they have a fast enough recovery where you still wont catch up to them. Mario Kart did it right where you, despite it being unrealistic, fly upwards more to slow you down. This, I imagine, can be even more frustrating in a racing game where you push a player ahead of you rather than help you. The items could use a bit of a revamp, perhaps even a filter for specific maps. For example, the Kickit map only has punching bags, perhaps flipped should only give the shield to players that can use it for their best interests or not have it at all.
The second worst thing about the game is the camera. I use a controller because mouse and keyboard just doesn't make sense for some games, racing being one of them (wheel>controller>mouse and keyboard). However, both mouse and keyboard have this same issue, the camera is just too frustrating. You could reverse and it IMMEDIATELY snaps backwards but sluggishly continues forward. It should be a bit faster snapping towards the direction you're driving. You could try to turn and the camera feels a bit off, it's hard to see where you're going, especially when chasing someone on an open map. You can use the mouse to move the camera, which is actually good. The controller, however, is painfully useless. It's a ♥♥♥♥ing racing game and they somehow made the camera horrible for controller players.
The absolute worse of the game that just ruins it entirely, no matter how many positives, is the controls. The controls make the game so unplayable that you'll have to relearn everything you have ever gotten from driving games. The turning specifically. The turn isn't imemdiate, there is input lag. This input lag is frustrating. It makes timing really hard. You know what's worse? The way the turns work. You LUNGE left or right. There isn't a good system of turning because there isn't an easy way to turn slightly left or right, you'll probably zig zag around stuff you're trying to get because of it. There is jumping and *kinda* drifting that *kinda* makes things easier, but not by enough. You'll have to invest a lot of time to get used to the game and even then I don't think you'll fluently be able to drive to what you are targeting.
Online community doesn't exist. No players online. That's probably because of the turning controls and what not.
When hosting your own game, I notice that, even as host, I lag with my friend. I only had problems with him, so that suggests that maybe there is some type of connection similar to Super Smash Brothers Brawl. That's not a good thing, especially since it causes not just me but my friend to teleport, reset all over the place, or go under the map. That's not something the host should go through.
If the developer would invest the time to, at least, fix the camera and controls to be less frustrating, the game would be able to get sales, easily, without having to sell a 4 pack for $2. However, the game seems to be dead both online and the developer side. I really like the idea, but I refuse to say it's worth buying no matter how many laughs I had with my friends because I was more frustrated with the controls than I was having fun. Not to mention the laughs my friends and I were making were more related to how bad and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t the game is.
If you're adventureous, you might wanna try buying the game on sale to experience it yourself. If you're looking for a good PC Mario Kart or something, look elsewhere because this is not it.
edit: to update, this game is still♥♥♥♥♥♥ However, my friends and I never touch it because other games, like Rocket League, are better. Don't bother with this.

In addition, it has replayability as it is not just limited to racing, there's other game modes that will provide entertainment, such as tag, soccer, basketball, hockey, pachinko, etc. There's also unique "power-ups" which you can pick up and use to give you a slight boost in the game, making it hilariously fun when you're playing with your friends !
Graphics-wise, it is pretty decent, with lots of vibrant colors and even a unique pixel-slider function, giving the game a retro-esque look.
However, there's some minor downsides, whereby the controls are slightly clunky, physics are a little off at times and some achievements are broken.
The player population is also minimal, so you usually end up playing with bots, which are boring and repetitive.
I suggest only getting this if you have friends to play with.

I'm not going to tell you that you should get this game. Whether you like this game or not really depends on how you want to interact with the game world and other players. I'm going to share my experience with it and why I like it, and hopefully this review/personal experience will help you with your decision.
I have played Shelter 1 and 2, plus the Mountains expansion for Shelter 2. They're an emotional rollercoaster that I couldn't stop playing. Let it be said that I am a big fan of the series. But I wanted to be among others in this game world in a way that would not break the immersion too much. I wondered how a multiplayer Shelter game would work.
Then came Meadow. Might & Delight delivered. I went into the game blind save for the trailer and I discovered that it lived up to my expectations. The thing I liked the most? Nonverbal communication. I am a very, very shy person when it comes to verbally interacting with other players in video games, whether typing via chat or speaking via microphone. I normally keep to myself in MMOs and other multiplayer games because grouping up with other players and aiming for a common goal usually requires continuous verbal interaction. So I find that I isolate myself. For the most part, it's alright. But I can't help but want more. A primal desire for connection trying to break through my apprehension.
I joined a world that had 9 people (there were worlds with more people, but I went for a less crowded one, knowing that it would fill up to a comfortable level). I spawned as a badger. A very basic brown badger. I knew I had to collect things to get more skins, emotes, and animals. I clicked a few emotes to get a feel for them. There's one depicting a happy badger with its paw raised (I did not know that this was a greeting until my bunny guide, mentioned below, used the bunny version multiple times when we met other animals). There's a smiling badger too, and a crying badger, and several action emotes meaning "cross the body of water", "go this way/follow me", "bark/growl/make noise" (barking or the equivalent for your species is used to activate totems and break them open to get at the goodies inside - a task that requires multiple players), and various other requests, explanations, and responses.
Feeling that I had the hang of this, I sought out other players. This is the first time in a long time I had done this. I, a new badger dropped into a foreign world, found a little red bunny and a goat(or was it a deer?). We travelled together until the goat logged off. Since the goat had no name or any sort of identification, I may never see them again. If I did, I would not recognize them. Such is this world of anonymity. The bunny must have sensed my unfamiliarity with the game because they were showing me around. They showed me how to use totems, helped me find other players and collectable items, guided me the quickest and easiest ways up mountains. In no time, I was a natural. I unlocked many emotes, a few skins, and another animal (a frog - I had seen only one in my playtime but I haven't tried playing as one yet).
I did not know who was controlling the little red bunny. It was not necessary to put a name to the bunny. They were just a bunny. But that bunny made my day: somebody somewhere in the world reached me in the language I feel most comfortable speaking. So thank you, Little Red Bunny, whoever you are.

This game is all about atmosphere and tension. It's impressive visuals and highly-detailed world really make you feel like you are in a post-apocalyptic world. Think Fallout, but with less humour and a lot more dire circumstances for everyone who is still alive.
The game plays as a first-person shooter, but the emphasis is on the narrative experience, and keeping you feeling afraid. Enemies are tough, monsters pop out at any time, and even the air you breathe works against you.
To help keep immersion, the HUD is minimal. In fact, it's completely hidden until you hold down the appropriate buttons/keys in order to access certain functions (such as switching gear).

The game usually let's you choose the way you play (action or stealth), but sometimes it funnels you into a way where you don't really have a choice. It often takes some trial and error to see if your way of playing is actually viable in those segments. This often ends up breaking immersion momentarily, but not for long as you will quickly go back to feeling tense again.

Making an update to the review since I've been able to play the game more and see more details.
Below are my general feelings about the game.
Positive:
* Graphics are improved and quite good.
* Gameplay is nice.
* Different skill levels to make it easier for casual gamers.
Negative:
* Game crashes alot (Like around every second race - this is also reported by others)
* Major bug at August 2015 which makes the game crash. According to developer this means you have to start a new career once the bug fix is implemented in order to proceed. The bug fix has not been implemented yet( Ref:
* The loading of races are really slow, even on quite decent computers.
* The sorting of players lacks several options to find the correct riders. For example tring to find the best riders without a contract at a certain age is from what I see really difficult to do.
* A bit difficult to find things like training, training progress etc until you are used to the game.
* For the games current state and in general, 39.99 EUR is very expensive.
Minor negative things:
* If you change screen resolution you have to manually exit the game, and then start up. Quite annoying when trying to find the correct resolution as this takes alot of time.
* The change of volume from minimum to maximum is done by holding down a minus button for a long long long time. This must be done for each of the 3 volume options from 100-0. It does not speed up while holding down the button. Instead of adding a slider and a mute button, it's only possible by holding down these buttons 1 by 1.
Conclusion:
I'de recommend the game if you are a hardcore cycling fan and can survive crashes and some annoyence. However if you haven't played any of the games before it might be worthwhile first to buy an earlier patched up version. In it's current state the game now is not in my opinion all completed. Still it's great fun to play the game when it's working. It might be worthwhile to buy an older cheaper version first to see if you like the game before you pay 39.99 EUR.
