This is a hard game to review because it has so many issues and yet isn't horrible and I'd recommend it if you're a very big fan of this genre (only from a sale though).
This game is horrendously designed. It was clearly made by amateur indie developers and the only thing remotely polished about it is the artstyle, which is fairly polarizing as it is. The game is essentially a tasteless grindhouse that involves as much gore and blood as possible, but I suppose that's apart of the genre that it's trying to be in so I can't fault it for that. However, what I can fault it for is it's terribly unresponsive controls, repetitive gameplay that's only real progress is gained from achieving arbitrary weapons at times that most of the time are worse than the first few weapons you unlock anyway. The enemies are created to essentially annoy you and juggle you, which in a beat em' up is essentially to be expected but this goes in this game where you've got guys shooting you while guys from off screen tackle you while dogs jump on you and guys hit you with machetes from a much longer range than makes any sense. This would be alright if enemies weren't damage sponges and couldn't attack you when they're barely on screen but it seems to just devolve into button mashing and luck, especially if you're playing on hard mode which means you only have one life. To add to this, the game is artifically created exponentially harder than it needs to be in hard mode because of the horrible platforming in the game that only serves to irritate you further. The developers seem to think irritation is good game design.
On top of all of this they censored the game and removed a ton of cutscenes which thus made the story make even less sense than it already did and gives you little motivation to be invested in the game unless you really just like mass murder. There is a steam guide that explains how to put the censorship back in but I just find it amazing that one implied♥♥♥♥♥♥scene was considered innapropriate in a game where the player commits brutal mass murder to countless people. Doesn't sound like the developers have their priorities right.
With that being said, there is some charm to the game that kept me playing and is the reason I am recommending it if you don't have better games to play. Also because I don't like beat em' ups to begin with or grindhouse I'm giving it the benefit of the doubt.

With all due respect to Dawn of War 2, which was a great game in its own right, Dawn of War 1 (and its sequels, even the woefully uneven Soulstorm) managed to capture the sense of scale in the lore of 40k. Relic has managed to capture the essence of what the tabletop missed, which was the massive battles in the stories.
Visually engaging even after all these years. While the models would look out of place in this generation, at the time they were one of the best. Gameplay is standard RTS base-building fare, but the resource gathering had been simplified to open up the action sequences. Basically you throw people in the grinder of war, but mobbing isn't the only viable strategy. Melee units that tie up the range attackers (which can fire on the move, unlike most RTS), unit abilities that close the gap, cover system etc... the game also rewards strategic placing of units. It isn't perfect (reinforcement should have had the option to be made automatic especially in the heat of battle), but respectable enough.
Audio is great, voice-acting has the right balance of hammy and lore-friendly.
If you are a big fan of Warhammer 40k, whether the tabletop or the lore, this game is for you.

An excellent example of how single-player shooters should be designed, I'd recommend Metro Redux to those who find post-apocalyptic action and stealth appealing. Do not jump into the game expecting an easy shooter, however, as even the "Action" mode is difficult without stealth, and more casual players might find the game frustrating.
To those of you who are interested, you're in for a treat. This game has some of the most unique game mechanics in the genre, which really pulls you into the game's atmosphere. A gas mask is required when above ground or other specific radiation zones, and a watch is synced up to the amount of time your mask can filter air. Taking damage while wearing your mask will cause it to crack and eventually break, making combat difficult until you can find a replacement. You are equipped with a flashlight early on, but it has to be charged to stay at full brightness. The charge will slowly decline, making your flashlight less and less useful.
On top of mechanics, a few of which are listed above, the game also offers a bit more exploration than typical games of the same genre. Exploration is often rewarding, offering secret paths around dangerous enemies, or stockpiles of valuables left in lockers or on bodies. Keys and safes are hidden in many of the levels, which, in combination, yield some extremely valuable contents to thorough players.
I came into this game on a sale, as I encourage you to do, but would have bought it at full price at release had I known about it. I had a wonderful experience, as short as it was (it felt wayyy longer than 11 hours!), and I encourage you to give it a shot if you're on the fence about it. If you like it, you might even end up playing Last Light as well!

Dino Run DX is a two-dimensional 'racing' game created by Pixeljam. You control a raptor that must escape a giant pyroclastic wall of doom (thanks to the giant meteor) by navigating through all sorts of randomly generated obstacles and landscapes in order to reach safe shelter.
Originally released in 2008, Dino Run was given a new coat of paint in Dino Run SE (Slightly Evolved) released in 2011 and given another in Dino Run DX (no clue what it stands for) released in 2015.
Dino Run is a very simple side-scroller that provides an atmospheric and enjoyable experience with a lot of replay value.
Controls are very simple, involving only the wasd/arrow keys to control all aspects of movement and shift to activate a temporary boost. The mouse is not used during gameplay.
There are two modes: Challenge and Speedrun. Challenge is the 'campaign' mode where there are set levels and failed attempts can be reverted with a limited number of 'time shifts'. Speedrun is a simple run of a single level which may have unique modifiers applied to it.
Each level starts off with the dino to the left of the level and the wall of doom following not too far behind. The dino runs into a variety of obstacles, environments, critters, other dinos of different species, dino eggs and powerups. Some dinos are helpful and some get in the way. How the level is laid out can either be randomly generated or created from a unique code that guarantees the same layout when used in the same run.
Game modifiers can be used to further enhance gameplay. Try changing the sky into a nightly setting.
Through experience, the dino can be upgraded with DNA, which is earned via saving eggs, eating critters and obtaining milestones.
The dino can be customised with skin colours and patterns and hats. Some hats are unlocked via completing runs at higher difficulties.
I haven't tried multiplayer so I cannot comment on that feature.

I also own the PS4 copy of this game, I can vouch for its graphical comparisons. There seems to be a misunderstanding with the ports of the game. The Playstation 4 version of the game renders the internal resolution in 1080p and the PS3 version in 720p, if you set your graphical setting to that resolution the game will be equal in graphics for the most part to the PS4 version. The PS4 version of the game has the Soft Engine, which makes the characters boobs bounce even more than it already does (boobs bounce enough with just the DOA setting imo) and it adds a bright glow to characters skin. The Soft Engine does not add any significant new textures to the game.
For those already familiar with the Dead or Alive series, its combat system is known for its holding system. This entry to the series adds an extra layer to those mechanics with the new and improved stunning system. The game runs at a smooth 60 FPS depending on your machine and, there are new and improved movesets as well. New mechanics such as critical burst, power launchers, power blow, and environmental features such as the cliffhanger gives DOA a new fresh look.
This seems to be the controversal topic of the game. As I stated earlier this port is lays very close to the PS4 version, but it does not include the Soft Engine. This uses the same textures and graphics of the PS4 version with the exception of the Soft Engine's glow on characters skin. There are MSAA options , and 4k shadows in this port which would make it potentially better than the console versions. DOA5 offers very detailed environments, as well as character models. The dirt, and sweat are nice touches to character detail.

Dying Light is a great open word-ish zombie shooter, best played with some friends in Co-Op. Tho it has it’s flaws and shortcomings, overall it is quite fun and rewarding.
The game features the zombie infested Harran city where a mysterious zombie infestation spread wide and evil bandits use the opportunity to gain power. You, Kyle Crane dropped into this Citi to find a cure. The scenery is beautiful and detailed, both graphics and sound design is excellent as well as the voice over. The game does suffer technical difficulties and bugs, like crashes. Depending on your system it may be severe or just rare occasions.
Melee combat is very fun, especially with the later unlocked skills and combos. However ranged weapons (guns) are very limited, not upgradable and just few in type compared to melee, where in reality, guns would be likely to be used more. Needless to say, killing zombies and their mutations (like Volatiles) are fun either way and works perfectly. (The following DLC adds more weapons to the game)
Unfortunately, the Story aspect and the tagged-on Co-Op experience is where the game lack the most. The writing is a rollercoaster, sometimes shines (Tolga sand Fatin twins, Gazi) and delivers a funny or amusingly bizarre missions and sometimes outright bad, like most of the Main story missions. Both the Main and Following DLC campaign end bosses/fight are really underwhelming and the main plot is disappointing.
Tho the game does feel good in Single Player, I would say you will get the most fun out of it when playing with friends. The game world, story unfortunately cannot recognize that you are a party (instead of just Kyle Crane himself, alone) and several missions, quests and areas does not give your friends the “party experience”. Even though several challenges available, to ease this fact, still the game feels that it was primarily designed for Single Player.

The Bad:

I played for some time now. At the beginning I tried some characters and used only button mashing to beat the opponents. This worked quite well for the weaker AI difficulties. The moves which this method unleashed were still impressive. But with increasing difficulty you have to understand the fighting mechanics of the game. There are many tutorials to get to know the rock/paper/scissor like system of the game totally unique in the fighting genre and learn the characters in various training modes. In most combat situations you can do something, even when you get stuned. Usually you have a wide variety of options. Fore someone new to this game like me it is not easy to make the right decisions. But if you manager to counter a challenging opponent the resulting punishment for the enemy will be terrible and looks amazing. Sometimes I was able to turn the tide of the fight right before I was going too loose badly. That's really fun.
Every character has its own moves and combos. Some character share the same martial art but they are all unique. Characters are also specialized on a field of the rock/paper/scissor system. Some fighters have special mechanics and stances making them totally distinguishable from the other fighters. I find the character roster multifaceted and it is fun playing different ones. As a result there variety of constellations for a fight. There is also a tag mode for doing a two on two where marvellous tag combos can be done.
There are plenty of stages to fight in. Two stages are missing from the PS4/X1 version of the game, but this has no real impact. There is a desert, a jungle, a temple, a castle stage, some fighting rings and so on. Most important the stages are part of the fight and not just simple background. You can smash your opponent against obstacles and walls making special combos possible. So even the positioning is important in this fighter. There is nothing worse to have one's back to the wall, especially when it's some kind of electric fence. Also some stages can even break down so an opponent will be thrown down a level. Sometime there are also some cool short cutscenes when a fighter was thrown off the stage with some interactivity for both fighters deciding in which favour they land on the ground. The stage interactivity is outstanding in this game.
Altogether I really enjoyed the game right from the beginning. Some people say it is easy to learn, but difficult to master. I can fully agree with that. The game runs stable and has an impressive graphic and high quality animations. Plus the fighting mechanics are deep and well-thought-out. If you want to smash down your opponents with awesome moves or want to dig deeper in the game and do the really eye-catching combos, then you should not miss this great 3D fighter :-)
A few last words in regard to the negative reviews. Don't take them too seriously. The game may have some issues, but there is nothing crucial. Most of them complain about missing features which the publisher announced and stated in the store page round about two weeks before release of the game. They still bought the game despite knowing of the missing features. There are two possible conclusions. They wanted to waste their money for a negative review or they still wanted to play this game for whatever reasons. So, what do you think?

NEO Scavenger is a kind of game where you need to keep an eye on everything, your wounds, your diseases, your equipment, hunger, thirst. It might give you a feeling the game is just another boring survival, but this is something that is worth checking out. This is a failed try-hard copy of WoW with lots of Pay2Win aspects. Cash shop is brings insane advantage in PvP, new mounts and vanity items ruin the immersion. Leveling is ultra linear with very little exploration. Build customisation might seem quite broad on paper, but in reality it's narrowed down by "aspects". The endgame is pure grind and can indeed get boring, burning you out fast. For some, endgame is the PvP, but as I mentioned, Pay2Wing ruins it. PvP while leveling is either non-existant or you get smacked down by ocasional paying veteran.
Playerbase isn't big, but not dead. People are really friendly and from all over the world. Everyone is mainly on "New frontier" server, "Equilibrium" being nearly dead and "Smuggler's paradise" having low population.
HOWEVER this game somehow manages to be my 3rd best free MMORPG (1st being Guild wars 2, 2nd Blade and soul). The concept of the world and it's lore is unique in few aspects, that bring the game it's charm:
1) It's a planet, shattered by cataclsysm and now there are pieces of land floating in space. Later in-game you have a possibility to build a ship that can sail n the mentioned space. The sad part is that devs abandoned this concept and after a few fun flights, it gets boring...
2) The two factions are based on russian culture. The League is bayor Russia - wooden houses, castles, a big presence of nature, traditional clothes and lifestyle. The Empire on the other hand is a reflection of Russia when it was the soviet union. Lots of similar, ugly concrete houses, to reflect the poverty brought by heavy industialisation and need of work/fighting force as the faction's main focus is war. There are lots of statues representing faction's heroes. Even leader's tower has an enormous statue on top of it representing the individual who established the faction.
I keep telling myself: "It's a bad game, but I keep coming back to it for once in a while for some reason.
All in all, if you decide to give it a try, play it for story and it's enviroment, but don't invest any money.

F2P system implementation is why I do not recommend this game. If You can live with things I have written in negatives below my recommendation changes to yes.
Most important advice: do not bother with Allods Online if You do not have big wallet or plenty of time (~18h/day for several years).
I'm experienced Allods player (several years long, with breaks) and for others like me I'm saying steam versions doesn't allow playing on old account (period), which is why I tried it in the 1st place.
Positives:
1. Graphics
2. Story line
3. Character customization (custumes, mounts etc).
4. New content usualy twice per year.
5. Free items You get at start (sufficient for 1 month of playtime).
6. Possibility to exchange ingame gold for currency used to pay in item shop.
7. PvE and PvP system.
Negatives:
1. No regard for time spent by players for developing their characters (mainly gear resets but build resetsapply too)
2. VERY unstable environment (due to upredictable changes u can't actualy plan for more than 3 monts in this game).
3. Old community, usualy hostile vs new poorly geared players in raids/pvp but there are some minor exceptions.
4. VERY expensive item shop (game is pay to win atm)- a perfect example of how F2P should not be implemented. I'll explain more at the end.
5. Nearly impossible to reach top within reasonable time without paying like 100EUR/month.
6. Nearly non-existing crafting (only alchemy is usefull now).
7. Plunder like economy, no control over exchange rate of ingame gold for currency in item shop, which allows manipulation of exchange rate for richest players in game.
8. Endgame content available only for elites.
To summarize:
Feel free to try it, explore classes, story line, find out how pvp and pve works (that was real fun for me).
If answer is pvp better look for well paid job so You can afford to pay for equipment upgrades (resets every 3 months all real money invested for gearing up to be competetive in pvp will be lost) and also for necessary and permanent items like runes, extra rubbies, combat mounts, talents, patronage lvl 5 and other item shop skills. Otherwise be prepared to be cannon fodder in pvp:)
If answer is pve game can be enjoyable even for someone not paying at all for game. Just keep in mind that if f2p players are starting to earn too much gold nerf to that gold source is guaranted to be implemented in incoming patches soon:)
In regards of the F2P system game is using really bad model which imho optimized only in (sry for the word) sucking out as much cash as possible from paying players:
1. Boutique hammers for equipment upgrades (that alone is about 20 EUR/month).
2. Expensive and temporary items (like holy weapons vanishing after 180days of real time, they can be reactivated... for a price ofc).
3. Many expensive items which F2P won't be able to get unless sitting in game like 18h/day for several years- which is why I said before it is more efficient and healthy to get RL job. For example getting patronage level from 4 (200% dmg bonus) to 5 (250% dmg bonus) requires 10000 crystals (100EUR) and You are not guaranteed to get it since it is lottery involved.
In short total cost of playing comfortably is like several times higher than average sub for other MMO while F2P system should allow comfortable playing for money comparable to other MMO sub.

When his boss leaves him for dead, Shank must kill everyone who stands in his way to get revenge.  With his trusty chainsaw, pistols, and shank, he sets out on a bloody journey.
This sidescrolling beat-em-up is exactly what fans of the genre expect.  Tight controls with numerous and varied weapons that have their own strengths and weaknesses, dozens of enemy types, beautiful comic-style graphics, and a storyline even Quentin Tarantino could appreciate make this a game to pay attention to.
Shank’s bloodthirsty rampage will take him across about a half-dozen vaguely Latin-inspired stages, each with their own visual flair and memorable boss battles.  New weapons are gifted frequently, and you’ll enjoy learning how to string them together into absurdly long combo attacks against the seemingly never-ending waves of enemies.  Given the quality of the art and design, it isn’t too much of a negative to say this game is quite short: I beat the whole thing in under three hours.
There is a co-op campaign that details the backstory of Shank’s initial betrayal and how he ended up in this mess in the first place.  Yes, a co-op campaign that is actually separate from the main story, but still impacts it!  More games should take that approach.  It is only available in local mode, so you’ll need a real life in-person friend to play it.
The graphics are absolutely gorgeous.  Crisp, clean and excellently drawn characters make every boss fight memorable.  The waves and waves of enemies in between them also look good, and every single enemy is animated in their own unique way.  The music is likewise extremely well done, adding another welcome layer of drama to the mix.
Klei Entertainment nailed it with this one.  I have a few minor quibbles with it, like the fact that some enemies attacks are telegraphed way too late for you to be able to react to them, but overall it is excellently made.  This is a great way to spend an afternoon or two, getting revenge for lost love by way of chainsaw and shotgun.

TL;DR “It’s Ark: Survival Evolved, stapled over a map made a decade ago, with a lot of Early Access problems, but you can use magic and tame unicorns so if that’s your thing then go for it, otherwise don’t waste your money.”
Typical "Early access" issues aside it is pretty blatantly an ARK ripoff, reskin, whatever you want to call it. Yes … SnailGames did buy Studio Wildcard and so they’ve sort of got a right to do this, but everything from the character model, to the hud,  to crafting system, to the creature mechanics are so reminiscent of it’s ‘parent game’ that I kind of feel like it would have been better served as ARK: Middle Earth DLC or something, instead of a whole new game.
The map itself has a layout painfully reminiscent of it’s 2006 release and it’s fairly obvious where the ‘questing zones’ once were. The “Starting Cities” have a lot of empty space to them wasted on grandeur with a smattering of NPCs from whom you can buy/sell things, however the textures, modeling, and AI all pretty clearly show just how old those assets and the AI really are.
I guess the ‘quests’ you might have once done in this game are now ‘tasks’ purveyed to you in a ‘flash game reminiscent’ tool tip on the left hand side of your screen. These serve as your tutorial as well as a mechanic to introduce you to the game's Lore, which in itself is kind of watery and unfulfilling. “Magic is bad because it blew up the moon” or something.
A lot of the things you’re supposed to do are often garbled by the poor english skills of the development crew, where tooltips are often times misleading or just hard to understand. I realize the original game was in chinese but personally expected more effort than ‘running it through google translate’ to be applied to the english version even at this stage of development.
All in all it just feels like a shameless money grab, where the better parts of two games were mashed together to create another and instead of paying 9.99 a month to be able to use a hang glider for it they’re charging a flat 22$.
Save your money for something else, or if you already have ARK you can just mod it to the same effect. This could, someday, metamorphosize into a new, unique, fun game but it is not any of those right now.

At 17 hours I am still a happy clam and the game makes me, get a bit salty.
After 32 hours of gameplay. We have some bugs/issues/features that need to be handled. The "Not able to invite someone" as a teammate or 1v1 (at least) should be a major issue, that SHOULD of been ready at launch. This is what almost every player is going to want asap, and if it is not addressed, it will cripple multiplayer.
Speaking of multiplayer, The matchmaking is not dialed in yet, also the point to spend per match needs to get a boost or some solution like roles like BS/BC role and the support role CA/LCA. but 2v2 is weird point wise. Multiplayer needs a fix/punishment for warp out/retreat churn "matches" to fix ships while @#$%ing the other teammate in 2v2.
I have had some crashes, ie; when gaining a faction for a ship and the look changes.
I have had about 5 crash to desktop, 2 looked graphical(?), 2 were in a solo game, and 1 in matchmaker. With over 30 hours of gameplay that makes me have about one crash every 6 hours of app. up time.
They still have done a great port of the classic game IMO for solo gameplay. If you like the lore and the paradox of 8 issues and 3 actions so it is more about picking the 5 places you want to lose, and then fighting like hell to gain the three victories you can/could win, you will love it.
I recommend this game if you love the 40k universe to buy it now. If you don't care about the lore, and you just want an RTS fix you should still buy it AFTER they resolve these issues.

So this game was originally a browser game from 2008. I used to play it a lot when I was younger, I remember seeing these lobbies full of people from across the globe. I may like this game from nostalgia, but when I take a deeper look at it I think that this game really is a good party game if you will, one to play with friends. This game is also still available in the browser even if it has less functions. As of now the browser version seems to have a bug that doesn't allow new users or guests to join the lobby, but hopefully it won't be that long before it's fixed. If you paid for this game on steam you will get some extra features aswell as being able to play it offline obviously. In online mode there are two lobbies, one for those who bought DX on steam and one lobby where browser users and DX users can play together! Sadly this game's multiplayer isn't very active at all and you'll be lucky if you find a random person to play with, it's really best to play this with friends. The gameplay is fun, chaotic and intense. You are some sort of bipedal raptor like dino that you can dress up in different hats. Your goal is to escape the ever closing wall of doom that heads toward the same goal as you. While you try and get away from your extinction things such as meteors or herds of triceratops will be in your way. If you eat critters and collect eggs your speed will increase slightly as long as you keep it up, you can also gather power up flowers that give you abilities such as an extended jump, increased speed+/acceleration or one that allows you to destroy large obstacles in your path for a short while. In singleplayer you can also upgrade your dino as you gather points. I don't think I recommend this game for full price, wait until the slightest sale is taking place.
Tl;Dr
Very fun with friends, can be partially f2p, has a semi dead multiplayer. Buy it during a sale.

NEO Scavenger is mean. It's unfair. It's cruel. It's grisly. The odds are stacked against you and odds are you won't make it a week. It's also one of the most fun procedural RPGs I've ever played.
It's certainly not perfect. The UI is clunky at best and deeply confusing at worst (remind me to tell you about the time I accidentally ate spoiled human flesh) and the story, while it starts strong, peters out to an ending that hints at a design cycle that ended with exhaustion rather than completion.
Still, NEO Scavenger is otherwise a remarkable and very well thought-out foray into a mythical, post-collapse Michigan with tons of interesting worldbuilding details and enough entertainment value to last you for a long, long time.

Two eyes flickered open and heavy breaths followed as she awoke from the nightmare. Her body shot upward from the sleeping bag. She felt her grip on it loosen as she began to calm down. Her eyes adjusted to the dim lighting of the shed.  She listened to her racing heart and the rain on the shed’s metal roof.
For a moment, a mere moment, the girl felt relaxed by the noise. Rain was soothing. The unbroken rhythm of each drop.
But the ease was lost when she heard a grumbling noise from the pit of her stomach. Her eyes traveled to her stomach. She placed her hands on her stomach, and tried to remember a time where she felt full. As proof, she wore a protruding ribcage.
Her attention was then drawn to the door of the shed. She could go out and search for food, risk death for food. Or stay here safe from the outside world and risk starvation.
Another grumble from her stomach made up her mind. The young girl found the dagger behind her dirty pillow. She gazed at it’s worn appearance for a moment. A dagger was not much but she had not much else.
With as must courage as she could muster, she slid out of the sleeping bag and crept slowly out of the shed. With one last look at the place she considered home, a dusty area with only one hole for light to penetrate through and a small space, she turned away from the shed.
Her eyes looked around the forest and felt goosebumps as rain tickled her skin.
The air was coated in a thick fog and the air was stale. What little left of trees stood, but various scraps decorated the ground.
At the age of fifteen, she had been on her own since she was five. Well that what she could remember at least. Whatever happened to the world, she could not recall. The only thing she could recall was her name, or what she had been called at the time. Merida.
Merida shivered feeling the rain soak into her clothes, or what little there was of her clothes.
The scrawny young girl moved away from the shed. She crept through the forest, feeling her muscles tense. A few snarls, growls and footsteps reminded her that she was not alone in the woods. It was dangerous here.
A few moments of walking and she heard something. A bush rustled. Her eyes darted to the bush and she stopped suddenly. She moved quickly behind a log across from the bush. A small rabbit wandered out of the bush. It's ears twitched for a moment. Luckily, it seemed to not have noticed Merida's presence. The rabbit sniffed at the ground for a moment and turned it's back to the log.
Hunger outranked patience, and Merida suddenly leaped forward towards the rabbit. She aimed her dagger for the creature, but missed. The rabbit, startled, begin to ran. Merida eagerly chased the rabbit farther. Her legs ached as she forced herself to continue.
It wasn't until a while, when Merida managed to chase it to the outskirts of the forest. Caught up in the chase, she had not noticed where she was until she tripped on a tin can. She fell down the hill and into the heaps of scraps.
The dagger in her hand had slipped from her grasp. It fell along with her.
With a sudden stop downward, she caught a glimpse of the rabbit running through the scrapyard. Her eyes wandered around, and she felt fear gnaw at her. She had never been here before. She had never left the forest before.
Merida tried to catch her breath. Her small body was not strong enough for the run. Pain engulfed her right leg. She noticed a red liquid spilling from her leg. A large cut rested on her knee. Various scratches decorated her body as well.
She guessed the fall into the scraps had managed to give her the mark, along with the blade of the dagger. Tears threatened to seep out her eyes but she dare not cry.
The girl struggled to stand. But her leg was badly injured and the weight of body was too much.
So she crawled forward. After a few attempts, the girl gave up. The pain in her leg was unbearable.
There she lay, amongst the scraps, with a still empty belly, a damaged body and lost hopes.
'There's no one, no one here to help me..', she thought to herself in despair.
With that, she shut her eyes, and awaited death. She knew she was not dying at the moment; but without shelter, food, and with her wound, she didn't think she'd last a night.
***
Night was present when she heard the noise of the beasts. Creatures of all variety were known to come out at night time. Her eyes tried to make out her surroundings in the darkness.
The night brought cold air to her. She shivered, and wished for her shed. At least it was shelter there.
Merida heard something rustle near the scraps. She shook in a terrified motion as the sound came closer. Clomp. Clomp. It almost sounded like footsteps. Merida tried to move her legs, but they felt numb.
She struggled to move, anything to avoid what ever it was.
The noise drew closer. All she could manage to do was hold her breath. A light as well, a red glow, was now close to her. She tried to avoid looking towards whatever it was, in fear that it would see her glancing.
The noise was now there near her. And the glow surrounded her. She close her eyes in fear. Suddenly, something cold and metallic touched her. She opened her eyes slowly, and saw two glowing eyes looking at her. The glow showed a mechanical being made of metal, gears and scraps.
And that was when she drifted into darkness.

When I started playing Shank I'd been already familiar with Klei Entertainment - their game, Mark of The Ninja, is one of my favourites and it is among those where I have 100% achievement completion. Of course, MoTN only came out 2 years later, therefore, I expected Shank would have its shortcomings.
Now, Shank is a fast-paced, action-packed side-scroller that reminds us of the good-old beat 'em up games from the arcade era. We proceed from one screen to the other while getting rid of dozens of enemies and eventually coming to a boss battle. At our disposal we have melee weapons (chainsaw!) and some firearms. While nothing fancy, making combos with all of our available items is pretty cool in the heat of battle especially when enemies are pouring in from every which way!
The game has cutscenes between the levels and a great accompanying soundtrack. While short (can be completed in a couple of hours), for hardcore gamers the hard mode is available offering an extra challenge by completely removing the checkpoints.
There are 2 things that make Shank stand out. First, we immediately notice that the game has a comic book art style - this was later used to make MoTN happen and Shank also has a sequel with similar graphics style. Now, the 2nd and perhaps most interesting is the excessive gore / violence the game uses.
I found it a bit too much at times - I admit this is the game's style but even the cutscenes have some pretty gory scenes for no apparent reason. I understand the game later on underwent an upgrade and as a result of that some of the more violent scenes were removed / edited including some nudity.
Don't go looking for a story here as you do not really have one. This is Shank's tale of revenge against his previous employer but it really is just a basis for killing a whole bunch of enemies (they never really elaborate on the story). This is not necessarily a problem as you are here for the chainsaw! :)
To summarise: Shank is a decent beat 'em up from Klei Entertainment which offers a couple of hours of entertainment if you do not really have any other game at your disposal. I look forward to completing its sequel! This is an easy pick-up - especially when discounted - just remember to use a controller!

If anyone ever asked me the kind of game a mathematician would play, it would be FTL:
After a few runs on easy, you'll have seen every mechanic, not counting a few more options in the advanced edition which don't add much variance on initial strategies.
The game then turns into:
1. pick a strategy
2. try to make it work
3. try to scrape around the nonsense the RNG throws at you to make you suffer
Each battle is self contained, so it can be pretty clear right from the beginning whether or not you can win. Overall the game has very little skill, in that you get what you get and good luck making it work. If you like picking apart the logic and probabilities of certain outcomes, then this game would be good for you, If you're looking for a game where there's an interesting interplay of mechanics, a story, an overall motif more than window dressing, then this is not for you. It is a grind, over and over, through the same situations, hoping the RNG smiles on you before and after.

Lots of games set in space make you feel like a soldier or a pilot, but FTL is the ideal simulator for playing the part of the captain. The tough choices, the glory of victory, and the price of failure are all on your shoulders. Since it's randomly generated, FTL alternates between fun and frustrating. A long string of defeats (and there will be MANY of them) can be discouraging, and the game has many circumstances where these defeats seem inevitable. But it's also extremely satisfying to score multiple victories, narrowly defeat powerful enemies, and try out the various weapons and ships you unlock over the course of the game. It takes a while to learn how to play, and the many deaths can be infuriating, but FTL is so much fun that you'll keep coming back to see how much farther you can go. Just make sure to play through the tutorial before you do ANYTHING ELSE! It's near impossible to play otherwise.

Civ V is pretty much an entirely different game from Civ VI. Its worth owning both, but I would recommend Civ V over Civ VI.
Since I don't want to write a 20 page report, I'll leave it to you to find out how the game works (civ's wikipedia page and yotube are your friends)
Pros:
-The most replayability in a game I've ever played ( see hours on record)
-The most enjoyable multiplayer experience of any game I've ever played (you need friends who play it with you, ignore random rooms)
-An indepth strategy game experience (pretty easy to learn, difficult to master)
-The complete edition bundle is often on sale for something like 12~16$, which is pretty damn good for a game like this
-AI can be relatively interesting at times
-Very active community both with technical help and gaming
Cons:
-AI becomes pretty easy once you learn their tricks (garbage at naval warfare, easily manipulated, etc.)
-Some glitches with large multiplayer games. (seems to be related to network issues with individual hosts)
Overall, if you like long but interesting and immersive strategy games this is the game for you. However, Civ V has a distinct gameplay style that you should probably lookup via youtube so that you can see if this is the game for you.

Dawn of War is a very special game to me, not only beacause it served as my entry point into the WH40k universe, but also as it cemented my love for strategy games along with its expansions, Warcraft 3, Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars and The Battle for Middle-Earth II back in the day.
There may not be ample reasons to play it today, but the campaign delivers an interesting, character driven story with stellar voice acting and writing, and serves as a good entry point for anyone unfamiliar with the series and the universe.
The multiplayer is dead, but its very much alive in its Dark Crusade expansion, which I recommend getting as well. You'll just need the original game first to play as four out of the seven races that are playable in Dark Crusade. The fifth race, The Imperial Guard, is obtainable through the Winter Assault expansion, while the last two come with Dark Crusade.
Last thing I'd like to mention is the sneaky price increase that happened  somewhere near the end of last year. The price went up from 9.99€ to 12,99€, in what I assume is an attempt to cash in on the still growing popularity of the series now that Dawn of War III is coming out at the end of this month. It still gets heavily discounted during sales so you'll be able to get it for just 3.75€, as opposed to 2.50€, which is how much I paid for it.  Nothing major, but nothing fair either.
All in all, Dawn of War is a good game that hasn't aged too badly. There's fun to be had in the game's singleplayer campaign, but other than that there isn't much else to do if you're not planning on getting the expansions  so you could play multiplayer.

Battle fleet gothica is set in the warhammer universe and many fans of the inverse includeing myself are thrilled to see it.
Good:
Graphics
Graphics look awesome. I love the detail on the ships. However on the same token. Most of the ships within a faction look the same. This is a result of the 40k universe, but it is something to note. The spaces for the battles look good enough but appear distance which disppoints me because some enviroments would be really cool to actually interact with.
Multiplayer
The multiplayer fleet management is well done. You earn experience and customize your fleet. Ships can be destroyed in battled and will be removed from your fleet for the next two battles. This give the multiplayer almost a sorta campaign like feel where it can actually hurt a lot to loose a critical ship.  Often you will see player retreat from battles to save their vessles.
Game Modes
The game offers a variety of game modes and while I do not find most of them highly thrilling, I was expecting only one destroy the enemy fleet mode. So the variety is welcome and hopefully will prolong my interest a bit.
Tactical Slow Mo
There is strategy in this game. Maneuvering and choices do matter. However it is often a difficult management challenge to actually pay attention to more than 1 or 2 ships. Therefore, I am very happy with the slow mo mode. Which I do not think I was expecting
The Campaign
The campaign is a set a randomly generated threats combined with a few special missions. It reminds me of the campaign from XCOM. You pick a crisis to react to, pick your fleet and fly off to a tactical battle. It has a good feel to it.
It is worth noting that the campaign is imperial only. If you want to play the other factions you are stuck with skirmish mode
Factions
In the spirit of warhammer the factions each have a different play style and feel very unique which games often fall short with. The factions are not clones of each other. The factions are also balanced very well thank to the beta.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Bad
RT Management
The game provides you with a lot of options of things to do in battle. And the game takes place in real time. Unfortunatly , it is very very difficult to provide any kind of cordination with your forces. There are no tactical formations in this game and the AI is rather bad at possitioning when set on auto attack.
For example, the eldar ships need to keep moving to keep sheilds up. The auto attack on your ships caused them to sit still, thus dropping sheild.
Part of the strategy is using escorts to screen the capital ships. This is very difficult to do because the ships cannot be groupped and the ships move at different speeds.
This management issue is by far the largest problem with this game. I almost game the game a negative review on this point alone. It becomes difficult for the game to be tactical.
Grindyness
The multiplayer mode has a low level cap. The max is 8. This is good because it allows new fleets to quickly become competitive and encourages players to have a variety of fleet. However the game still holds the weakness that a level 1 fleet is no match for a level 4 fleet. And they game has no option for a truely custom match
Map
Space is empty. I understand that. The game has a number of objects which can appear all over the map . However, I do not feel they often have much of an effect on the battle. I wish the effects were more pronounced.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Other Stuff
2D not 3D
The game is true to the table top and in 2D, not 3D. I do not feel that being in 3D would add any great tactical option. 3D would only increase the management problem in the game.
Stealth
The game has a nice system of stealth and ship detection.  Perhaps I do not understand the strategy, but I have not found it that meaningful.
Naming
I find it odd that you name ships and not captians. But its not really important.
Intro
I have not yet found if there is a way to skip the intro mission in the campaign.
Zooming
I wish I was able to zoom out further when viewing the map.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Conclusion
I reccommend this game to those who understand what it is. Players will not control massive fleets of ships. The game is a grindy, click-fest, but not without tactics.
The game itself walks a line between being a deep tactics and being one of those games we are addicted to and are not sure why. However the game walks that line very well. The game does retains its tactical depth, while still having that odd addictive trait which I associate with cell phone games.
If none of the things I described are a deal-breaker, then you should buy this game. As for myself I want more tactics and just cannot committe myself to the grind. I do not think the game is bad. It just is not exactly what I hoped. I think I would have been happier with a turn based game

Dark and Light is one of the games I have been anticipating on playing since one of their first trailers. I got it day one and have played any time I could. With that in mind, this review will have nothing to do with it's relativity to ARK or other sandbox games, and will purely be insightful based off of my opinion having played for the amount of time I have thus far, and will possibly change as new updates roll out. And with that, here we go.
Dark and Light is a mythical Sandbox-Survival game in a land of spells, wyverns, and undead.
Pros:
•Not a very stressful beginning.
•Progression isn't a hair-puller.
•Most communities are (so far) very nice.
•Dieing isn't super tragic until around level 27.
•For an Early Access game, it's very well polished.
•Lag isn't that big of an issue, and if you do lag, it doesn't make the game unplayable.
Now, the cons are all going to come from the perspective of someone around the level of 27.
Cons:
•The Goblins hit your home for about 4. With houses having ~5000-20000 health, that's not so bad. However, REAPERS AND SKELETONS hit your house (multiple walls) for 2000+ each, leaving no sence of protection.
•Starting over at this point feels more like a bad repeat movie.
•Armor doesn't have enough durability.
•Because of these two factors, finding a spot where you and your home will be safe requires far too much time and effort.
•There is very spotty lag, however it is manageable and doesn't effect the game too much.
I don't think that any review comparing this to ARK is sound in the slightest. It's very fun in its own way and it hasn't been uniniteresting in the entire time that I've played. Not to mention it being the one game that could pull me away from my main game.

How they created D&L:
Look at ark
Take away the Prehistoric theme of ark
Keep the HUD, UI, Crafting system as similar as possible
Add Fantasy theme to everything
Add Mythical Creatures instead of dinos
Add Quests giving that RPG feel
Keep taming but, change the method in which you tame.
Add Character Races/Classes  = Elves, Dwarfs, and Humans
Add Magic Attacks / Spells
Add Dragon (If you dont consider modded Dragons being "Ark" creatures)
Add NPC's (If you dont consider Ark modded NPC's as being Ark NPCs.)
Add Shops/Money (If you dont consider Ark Modded Shops/Money  being Ark stuff)
Overhall the Engram system and make unlocking items based on doing things in the game VS Arks level up route.

All the rumors about it bring ark reskinned is 100% true! From the Hud Design to the Inventory/Crafting system to the way Characters look. The entire purpose behind playing this game is similar to ark as well. You Build a base, get gear, raid players, tame creatures, raid caves, defeat bosses, kill other players. Other downfalls with this game are mechanical. I wish the point of view was different when using magic attacks. The angle is so weird, that I have difficulty hitting things after my first spell attack, I cant see what im trying to attack.
Its hard to know what will kill you and what wont. A lvl 1 creature could demolish you or you will demonish it, really depends on the creature your fighting. For example a lvl 1 goblin you can kill but a lvl 1 reaper will destory you.
Currently would i recommond this to my friends? Im on the fence. These two games are so much alike its hard for me to give a good recommendation.
After 1,500 hours in ark, its just left a bad taste in my mouth. The only things i like is the creature design, world design, RPG element and base building items detail/style. Ill recommend this, simply for the fact they have plenty of time to make it unique and tweak things to make it feel less ark like.

Shame that in Steam there are only buttons "Yes" and "No", but there is no such button as "Meh...". When I was buying this game, the only thing I cared about was campaign, not multiplayer, not skirmishes, just interesting single-player game with good story. Unfortunately, game failed to give me this essential (in my opinion) part of every self-respecting game. Yes, there is story, but for now (I am on 2nd chapter out of 5, according to achievements) its mediocre: no interesting characters, no interesting missions, just chain of battles with briefings and occasional cutscenes (quite good looking, actually) between them. Also, I don't understand people, who claim campaign in this game has replayability - really? where is it? can someone help me to find it, because for me replayability is possible, when you can complete game in really different interesting ways. When in this game you can defend only 1 system out of 2 and you have to choose what you don't want to loose more - more expensive upgades or less renown earned - its not replayability in my book. Ok, what parts of these game are mediocre aside from campaign... Gameplay, to be precise - battles, because there is nothing else, aside from battles, upgrading of ships and choosing of where to have next battle. Missions are interesting first several hours, but now I have 9 hours played (after release + beta) and I already feel boredom while playing missions and honestly, the only thing that keeps me from dropping this game is desire to see all ships. By the way, ships - there are lots of ships, but technically there are 5 ships in each faction (correct me if I am wrong) - battleship, battle cruiser, cruiser, light cruiser and escort ship. Yes there are different variations, but they don't look differently, the only thing that changes is weapons - different ships have different weapons, which makes them useful for different strategies, but doesn't make them different ships, which is also a shame.Every battle starts with deployment phase and, after it, flying to your enemy and I have 1 very little question - Why, the hell, there is no "speed up" button? Every battle I have to watch for minute or two after my ships lazily flying forward and god forbid me from using acceleration, because, oh no, the enemy will somehow will see my ship from his side of field. Ok, I'm already tired of typing so time for conclusion, but, before it, one last minus for the game, but its not for everyone: price of the game. Yes, the game is 40$, which is less than other games, but in my region (Russia) game is quite expensive - 1999p. (Total War Warhammer or Fallout 4 prices). I've already asked on Steam forums why is that and already got the answer - Developers are not rich enough to lower price for my country (because of bad economy of my country) like other developers do. I suppose its fair, but by making such expensive price developers raised the bar so high, that game just cannot reach it. Sadly, another wasted opportunity to make really good game in Warhammer 40k series.
P.S. And, because of the time in beta, I can't even refund it and buy it later with 50%-66% sale.

Dead or Alive... Oh how I love this game. Since DOA2U all the way up to DOA5U, I have enjoyed this series thoroughly and when I heard they were porting it to PC I was ecstatic. Oh and before you judge my playtime as credibilty, I have over 300 hours playtime on DOA5 and DOA5U, I've played enough to form an opinion of Last Round. Now that you know my background with the series and how much I enjoy it hopefully you will trust me when I say not to buy this game unless it's on sale. Why you may ask? Well lets get right down to that.
Dead or Alive 5 Last Round is the third and final installment of the orignal Dead or Alive 5. The second installment DOA5U added many features such as the ability to change the soundtrack and even the breast physics. There were new game modes such as Team Battle and the training mode was enhanced even more, making it easier to master your favourite characters. New stages, costumes and characters were also implemented. DOA5LR was meant to be the next gen version of DOA5U; whilst they were only adding 2 new stages and some new characters, the graphical improvement alone was worth the upgrade. Except the steam version isn't getting half of this.
Wanted those new next-gen graphics? Haha nope.
Wanted the remasters of 2 great stages in DOA? Haha nahhh.
How about even being able to run a PS3 game on max settings with a smooth 60fps? Better have a rig that costs £1000.
Oh you want a simple cloud saving system so you don't have to back up saves? Nope, too complicated.
Fancy a steam name change? Well prepare to lose all your save data.
Want to play online with a friend? Not for the next 3 months you can't.
Might as well rename it to Dead or Alive 5 Ultimate 2.0.

I'm sorry if this was long but Team Ninja has really ♥♥♥♥ed up with this. "...solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short."
Such is life in the "state of nature" described in
by Thomas Hobbes. NEO Scavenger illustrates this state more accurately than most single-player survival games. Here you are not completely alone with wildlife in a sandbox like in The Long Dark; but you're also not stranded on an island with mutant cannibals like in The Forest. Instead, you find yourself competing for resources with other survivors, some of them in desperate conditions like you are at first, and others thriving in the desolation and lawlessness. Once you manage to grasp the basics of survival, after several "nasty, brutish, short" attempts resulting in horrible deaths, you will also thrive in this chaos.
This is a game built upon brutal trial and error, and the errors will often cost you all the progress you've made, with all the cool loot you've scavenged. But each death makes you stronger, smarter, more adapted: you live, you die, you live again. And it's this very brutality that makes it so rewarding. Even when you are several days in, thriving in the chaos like a badass, you can still get seriously sick and die abruptly, no matter how much you try to avoid the inevitable. But you soldier on. I did, and somehow I made it to the ending, which, according to this
, is very hard to reach even after several tries.
(MASSIVE SPOILERS) is my ending log, just in case anyone wants to check or compare.
It also stands apart as an RPG as much as a survival game. Openly influenced by classic tabletop RPGs with creative problem solving through skills, it feels somewhat like playing the original Fallout for the first time once again (and that also means dealing with clunky UI and mechanics). The encounters with characters and factions often have branching storylines and different, sometimes irreversible outcomes. The writing is a bit too purple sometimes, but that's a genre thing, and considering that it's a one-man development team, it's still better than the writing in many AAA games.
The UI can be irritating, and I can only advise that you pick up on the hotkeys ASAP and get used to them, it'll make life easier and counterbalance the addictivity of the scavenging mechanic, the real rough core of the game, which manages to keep you busy for hours and hours while you search for that one left boot in good condition or whatever. Realism isn't a defining factor exactly, but it's well-balanced so that it plays like a challenge, but also not complete scarcity. There is loot aplenty once you learn how to optimise the scavenging.
I've put 110 hours into it according to Steam, but since it is a game that you can just leave in the background while you browse, I didn't spend every hour playing it in a frenzy. This is a game that walks the fine line between casual and hardcore in a fascinating way. It's a background game that can hook your attention for hours in between other things that might hook your attention. And I believe it has immense replay value beyond the seemingly endless cycle of scavenging and dying. I intend to try another character build at some point and see how the story will develop.
The worldbuilding has potential to develop into a franchise and evolve into bigger, more complex gameplay mechanics, and I don't mean necessarily in first-person, though that could be interesting. As a launching effort, NEO Scav is a brilliant little game, a real diamond in the rough of clunky UI.

If anyone ever asked me the kind of game a mathematician would play, it would be FTL:
After a few runs on easy, you'll have seen every mechanic, not counting a few more options in the advanced edition which don't add much variance on initial strategies.
The game then turns into:
1. pick a strategy
2. try to make it work
3. try to scrape around the nonsense the RNG throws at you to make you suffer
Each battle is self contained, so it can be pretty clear right from the beginning whether or not you can win. Overall the game has very little skill, in that you get what you get and good luck making it work. If you like picking apart the logic and probabilities of certain outcomes, then this game would be good for you, If you're looking for a game where there's an interesting interplay of mechanics, a story, an overall motif more than window dressing, then this is not for you. It is a grind, over and over, through the same situations, hoping the RNG smiles on you before and after.
I suppose it lasted me 22 hours, so if you go by gametime it might be worth it, but the game just keeps going with ships focusing on the few mechanics, which lead you to vibrate through the RNG slightly differently. There's plenty of unlocks if you want to grind through them. The heavy use of time in this game is what throws it off for me, it IS novel, but it's a bit of a gimmick in that you can't really use it to your advantage other than microing slightly better than realtime.
Note: The reason I bring up mathematician, is literally I know a collegiate mathematician fascinated with the game. As an engineer however, I can see why but can't recommend it to anyone else.

Lots of games set in space make you feel like a soldier or a pilot, but FTL is the ideal simulator for playing the part of the captain. The tough choices, the glory of victory, and the price of failure are all on your shoulders. Since it's randomly generated, FTL alternates between fun and frustrating. A long string of defeats (and there will be MANY of them) can be discouraging, and the game has many circumstances where these defeats seem inevitable. But it's also extremely satisfying to score multiple victories, narrowly defeat powerful enemies, and try out the various weapons and ships you unlock over the course of the game. It takes a while to learn how to play, and the many deaths can be infuriating, but FTL is so much fun that you'll keep coming back to see how much farther you can go. Just make sure to play through the tutorial before you do ANYTHING ELSE! It's near impossible to play otherwise.

In this genre of games, I think the masterpiece still stands as Final Fight. So I will mostly compare this with Final Fight.
- The art greatly surpasses Final Fight, but it's not a direct result of 20 odd years that passed between these two games. Shank tries to establish its own style that has been a good mix of Metal Slug, Western and Tarantino movies and executes it near flawlessly. The game's greatest merit is its art to be honest.
- Lack of ridiculous♥♥♥♥♥♥to do or secret locations. There aren't any of them unlike Final Fight where you beat a car for no good reason but still a good amount of fun and something to achieve and try to set a record on. Compared to Guacamalee, lack of secret locations also can be more noteworthy.
- Comparing stories, Shank and Final Fight both follow a cliche story about a woman but Shank does it a lot better and the story has a good amount of Robert Rodriguez vibe, which I found incredibly done. Also the characters are fleshed out a lot more, unlike Final Fight's bosses.
- When it comes to gameplay, Final Fight was much more superior. All of your combos made sense and were devoid of button mashing. Also Final Fight tried to keep combos and attack moves a lot simpler but timing of them and the strategy used to defeat a number of enemies in an area mattered much more than button mashing.
- Final Fight allowed you to trap your enemies to a corner of the screen and beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of them, which made the game a lot easier than it could have been if you couldn't exploit this. Shank carries this trope to some extent, you will mostly be able to corner your enemies and beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of them except for bosses and some enemy types.
- Some fights consists of throwing multiple waves of heavy enemies at you without having a chance to rest or save and it's pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Yes, the game scenario makes sense for you to fight them, but having a 8-10 minutes of constant fighting and starting all over when beaten just feels unfair to me.
- Responsiveness of the controls are sometimes ♥♥♥♥ed, which was purely perfect for Final Fight. I often wondered why my fighter insisted on shooting at the opposite direction or failed to grab one item in multiple tries. When it comes to dodging, controls ♥♥♥♥ up more and you find yourself standing in the middle of 5 large enemies.
- I won't be able to compare this with Final Fight due to era's technical limitations but compared to Guacamalee the amount of gore in the game is just lovely and it is very satisfying to violently strangle someone with chains or how you behead bosses.
All in all, if you're interested in the genre or want something interesting, Shank can be a good choice when on sale and fortunately it goes on sale very frequently.

Shank is a very violent hand drawn 2D sideways scrolling beat/shoot 'em up.
The presentation is excellent - badass gory comic book style cutscenes, great sound effects, and a really fitting gritty soundtrack. The story itself is a very shallow revenge plot, but I couldn't care less - it sets the mood perfectly.
Good combat mechanics - 4 weapon categories: The mandatory melee weapon (Two knives), heavy melee weapon (machete, chain saw etc), ranged weapon (guns etc), and grenades (frag, mines, molotovs).  I did find the gravity a bit too weak though - it all felt a wee bit too floaty for my taste.
There's a good variation in enemy types and a boss in the end of each level, so even though you could argue the combat is fairly simple, I still found it varied, challenging and rewarding enough to keep me entertained for the 3 hours of gameplay the campaign provides. There's also a co-op campaign.
The gameplay using an xbox360 controller didn't feel quite as tight as I had hoped for. While the analouge stick is good for aiming the ranged weapon, it felt a bit too indirect/unresponsive for character control.
Generally it's pretty evident that it's a console port, as e.g. the devs didn't even bother hiding the mouse cursor during gameplay.
I bought Shank1+2 at 75% off, and at that price it's just ridiculously high value for money, but even at full price it's a recommended purchase for fans of the genre.

A visually beautiful game with many interesting units and exciting gameplay, but multiplayer has some serious balance issues that don't seem to be addressed.
Almost all of the heavy tanks are on the German side, and the couple of heavy tanks available for allies are doctrinal only and easily defeated by even medium armor. What it means is a much higher level of skill needed to play as allies, while Germans need only to survive into the late game in order to obtain tanks and faceroll everything.
When matchmaking, Relic shows the percentage of players waiting in line for each side. I rarely see over 40% allies, and it is often even 5% allies and 95% Germans. It makes for frustrating gameplay and ultimately let to me uninstalling this game.
I'll give it a shot again once the next patch is released, but with how long this game has been released for I would expect such a basic issue to be resolved.
And I didn't even get into the pay to win issues around buying commanders...

For those who don't know what Quake 3 is, Quake 3 is a fast-paced arena multiplayer FPS that defined Rocket-Jumping and Strafe-Jumping. Quake will test your twitch skills. It requires full focus, speed, accuracy, and knowledge of the maps to win.
Shy playing with others online? You can practice offline with bots that are very challenging. Also there are tutorials available in the game that teach you the basics of Quake Live, how to rocket jump, and how to strafe-jump.
Only problem with this version of the game is loadouts... Really? In a Quake game... WHY?! What is the point of exploring the level when you can just spawn with a rocket launcher or rail gun? Remove this feature now please! It's not the worst change ever, but it does NOT work here!
One feature that I would love to see integrated with this game is Steam Workshop. Add this and remove the loadouts and I think this game would be perfect.
Now do I recommend this game? Yes. It is a great game. I recommend you give this game a go if you are at all interested in an arena multiplayer FPS since it is free.
There are features that are absent from this game that are in Quake III Arena like mod support, blood, gibs, ability to play against bots in multiplayer, no recurring fees for hosting own server, and, most importantly, NO LOADOUTS. Also, with IOQuake3 mod (
) along with the hi res texture pack, you can make Quake III Arena better looking than Quake Live.
I am not an expert at this game, but here are a few tips that I found helpful when playing this game.
1.) Be quick. Bunny hop to gain speed and momentum.
2.) Be accurate. Don't spam rockets unsurely.
3.) Shoot where the player will be, not where the player is.
4.) Know the maps, the flow, doorways, passages, and portals. Where will the player be if they go through that door or portal?
5.) DON'T CAMP!! Keep moving! The more you move, the less chance you will get fragged.
6.) Know the weapons, how they work and their damage.
7.) Don't stick with just one gun. Use the array of weapons to your advantage.
8.) Learn how to rocket-jump.
9.) Learn how to strafe-jump.
10.) Most importantly, HAVE FUN! :)

Having now played through this game, I am very much looking forward to reading the book.  This was one of the most compelling, beautiful, haunting, terrifying, well-written and exciting games I have ever played.  This deserves a full 10/10. The story is intriguing if not a bit beguiling. It is unclear why the main character seems to have a psychic connection with these "Dark Ones," creatures that seem to attack the minds of the citizens of Metro and it was not entirely clear if the "Dark Ones" were the keepers of the hordes of mutated creatures that roam topside and underground. While I have theories and I believe they are correct, I will not divulge them here for fear of spoiling the story for you.  Suffice it to say, not everything is as it first appears ;).
I cannot recommend this game highly enough to anyone that enjoys a complex and entertaining story.  NOTE: This is a first-person-shooter, but ammo is scarce.  In fact, by the last act of the game, I had 5 bullets, some pipe bombs and a few throwing knives. I didn't know if I was going to make it to the end. But that is part of the beauty of this game. Most of the time, wild gunning will not get you through it.  Sneaking or running like hell may be your best option. For instance, in an earlier section of the game, you must plant an explosive to collapse some tunnels. Creatures are running after you left and right. You can shoot them and waste your ammo or you can lead them to your comrades who will shoot at them, or, you can do what I pretty much did, run like hell until you set the explosive and then run like hell again.
Anyway, that is all I'm going to give away regarding gameplay.  But that is part of the joy of playing this game - you can play it the way you wish.
Oh, I did find out that there are 2 different endings. I do not yet know how to get the 2nd ending, but I enjoyed this game so much, I may go and replay it to see if I can uncover the 2nd ending.
Anyway, before I replay it, I'm going to go read the book.

Civilization V was my first experience with the game series.
I was a little overwhelmed, at first, but much of it is intuitive and there are great guides out there for any questions you may have.
I prefer the single player, to the multiplayer, because people frequently leave and it’s rare that you’ll finish a game with all the players you started with.
You can set the win parameters by time, as in whoever has the most points by turn ___ wins the game, but I usually remove that type of win as it’s easy to points and win with little effort this way.  However, it’s a nice option if you have little time to play.
Otherwise, there are wins by; science, culture, diplomacy or domination.  There are also many difficulty levels to choose from, and countless parameters to choose from in order to set up your perfect game.  You can choose; map type, map size, map layout, number of city-states, number of civilizations, number and type of barbarians, auto selecting pieces, auto attacks, auto moves, map terrain, time period to start in etc… etc…
With so much customization, it would be impossible not to find a set-up you enjoy.
At the lower difficulties, the A.I. will make poor choices and a win is rather easy to achieve.  At the highest difficulty, the A.I. gets good at blocking your wins.  They also start with more advantages depending on how high you set the difficulty.  There is a challenge level here for anyone.  It could be that veterans of the series, who are good at memorizing patters, could find a way to exploit the A.I. but my guess is that this is rare, and not, what the average player is looking for.
As a newcomer, I experienced the game as a multi-layer chess match, yet far less dry.
There is great ambiance and music and the music changes for each civilization and for each city-state.  You also get to meet and see the pictures of the leaders you are playing against, as well as see their expressions change from friendly to guarded to warlike, depending on your relationships.  You will hear the music created in your civilization, see the art, and get a quotation for any writing works.
One thing to note is that games can take a long time if you start at the beginning of time. At the start, my games would take several days, usually ending after 12 hours.  Even after hundreds of hours of playtime my games can take up to 6 hours.  You don’t have to play it all at once, of course, there are both auto saves and manual saves to continue games.
The only con I found is that the mid-game can be slow, and at high difficulty, you can find yourself without a way to a win midway after taking much time to set up.
Regardless, I absolutely love this game.

Look at ark

All the rumors about it bring ark reskinned is 100% true! From the Hud Design to the Inventory/Crafting system to the way Characters look. The only differences in the purpose of playing this game is, Quests, Character Races, and Magic Spells. Everything else you can experience from juse using Ark Mods. Also I've heard Races can have massive wars against other races.. I havent figure out this yet or even seen any videos of it.

Last Round finally hits Steam and it manages to be a solid port, despite lacking a few features.
Gameplay:
If you've played any of the previous DOA games or dabbled with Virtua Fighter, you should feel right at home. This iteration features over 30 characters to choose from with 19 stages in this specific port (Danger Zone and Crimson are missing). The Three Button system allows the game to be highly accesible, with a key feature being able to parry an attack during combos and strings.  There's a lot more mechanics for those looking to take their game to the next level such as new types of stuns, Power Launchers, Critical Bursts and more.  Like the other Versions it features modes such as Story, Challenge, Training, Versus (1v1/Tag), Survival(1v1/Tag), Time Attack(1v1/Tag), and Team Battle. The PC port doesn't have Online out the gate, but it is coming eventually. Even if you plan on playing solo there are tons of modes and unlocks to you busy, of course nothing beats playing against other people.
Graphics:
While this version doesn't feature the Soft Engine or particle effects from the current gen consoles, it still manages to actually look better than the other two in some ways thanks to AA, better shadows and resolutions. So yeah if your worried about this not being a looker, then you can put your mind at ease.
Sound:
This game features both an English and Japanese dub, and an OST that includes music from DOA1 all the way to it current incarnation that your allowed to customize no less!
Overall:
If your looking for a really good 3D fighter o PC seriously look no further. Yes it's missing some features but they are minor at best. No online is gonna hurt for a bit but it is coming and honestly that should be the only deal breaker here. If you decide to take the plunge despite all the cons you'll be rewarded with a really awesome 3D fighting game with great sound, visuals, and most importantly gameplay!
+3D Fighter on Steam
+Accesible with challenge for those looking for it.
+Lots of characters
+Lots of Stages
+Lots of Modes
+Tons of Costumes
+Awesome OST
+Dual audio voice tracks
+Pretty Visuals
-Config Launcher
-Missing two Stages
-No Soft Engine (though I could care less)
-No Online (yet)

If you like driving games, then get this. The game and its DLC sets are great value now. I play via keyboard, and its main cars work fine via that. Some of the more complex cars in DLC may need a wheel or controller to work well, but don't let that stop you. The graphics are good enough, because its the cars handling and the gameplay that really matter. The bulk of the cars can be changed to handle how you like, and frankly I've played a lot of PC car games where the handling is rubbish. In this game the cars handling, the physics, and the game play are at another level.
You'll find that practice is required, and playing online against good drivers is an eye opener for sure. Its a fabulous game - at this price? A steal.

It's terrible. One of the things people praise the game for is "storytelling", yet there is none of that in this game. Gordon gets thrown back into the action within minutes of playing the game. You walk for a little while, meet an old friend, then you're being chased by the Combine. Wow, great storytelling right there. After Gordon gets his♥♥♥♥♥kicked by two cops, a girl comes out of nowhere and saves him. Uh, okay? You walk with her, and she takes you to a safehouse where you meet up with some old friends. One of Gordon's friends tries to teleport him to Black Mesa, but his stupid alien pet ruins everything and pretty much almost gets Gordon killed and alerts the entire city. His friend is a scientist, so you would think he'd be smart enough to keep the damn animal locked up when doing stuff like that. Fast forward through all the boring and repetitive shooting galleries and driving sections... that's it, you beat the game.
I would go in depth about Episode 1 and 2, but they're equally as bad, if not WORSE. The main game and the episodes are a snooze fest. When you're not shooting things in the countless action sequences, you spend it listening to boring dialogue that puts you to sleep. And this is coming from someone who LOVES the Metal Gear Solid series, and those are notorious for their long cutscenes and Codec calls.
The characters in this game are so boring, it is pretty pathetic at times. Nobody has any emotion, and you don't care for any of the characters except for Alyx and Barney. You get more emotion out of dying in Metal Slug than you will ever get with any of the main and side characters in Half Life 2.
I would be able to look past all of these issues if the gameplay was good, but it isn't. It is just as bad as the story.
The shooting is awkward, the movement is clunky, the weapons feel weak, the human enemies rarely miss a shot, and bullets do jack♥♥♥♥♥♥to them unless it's a headshot. The zombie-like enemies are just as you'd expect. Slow, tanky, boring to look at. When you encounter these enemies, the game goes from shooting gallery to a "horror" section. The only thing horrific is how slow, boring, and pointless the sections are. The driving sections in the game are way too long, boring, and the vehicles drive like♥♥♥♥♥♥ They throw the occasional puzzle at you, but they're hilariously easy and almost pointless.
It's like someone made a list and they had to add everything that was in it. Over-the-top, overused shooting galleries? Check. Mind numbingly boring driving sections? Check. Hilariously easy puzzles? Check.
The game essentially boils down to this: kill everything in the area, move forward. Kill everything, move forward. Stop! Solve our puzzle. Okay, now go kill more stuff and rinse and repeat until the driving section. Oh, you beat the driving part? Now sit here and listen to these characters talk for a little while until you die of boredom. Oh♥♥♥♥♥♥ you're still alive?
Now go shoot more stuff. Rinse. And. Repeat. It really baffles me how people HATE Call of Duty for linear gameplay, but then they proceed to praise HL2 for having an "amazing" story and "revolutionary gameplay". What a sick joke.

Half Life 2 brought nothing to the table in terms of game mechanics or storytelling. MGS, Tenchu, and Thief changed and made the stealth genre popular due to their gameplay and story, which were both way ahead of their time. GTA made open world games popular, with the MASSIVE world to explore, and the gritty, dark, and sometimes even depressive storyline just made things even better.
