The good:
- It's atmospheric as sh*t.  You feel like you're in a city full of scary dead things.  It's scary when they swarm you for quite a while and nighttime also feels meaningful (if you get sloppy).
- Zombie combat is pretty satisfying.  And that's what we're all here for, I think.
Middle ground:
- Parkour'ing around is fun, but I wound up disabling fall damage because it doens't feel right to continually die to a missed click if you can all-but-fly around otherwise (once you get the grappling hook).  And since this came from console-land, I feel it's not quite as easy as it should be to do certain things.  Also, the grappling hook desperately needs its own keybinding, since it's shared with some other things you really want to use and you wind up constantly doing things like throwing a molotov cocktail at the point on a wall that you wanted to grapple to.
- The UI comes from console-land.  It's workable but mildly annoying.
Oh, come ON!:
- You have to solo the start of the game, so if you're just interested in co-op, like I was, prepare to do something else for a while.  This wasn't the end of the world, but at the END of the game, they did it again!  The final fight area is solo, so even though you were playing for tens of hours with your buddy, you won't get to finish it together.  Even worse, the finish is made up of a lot of "interactive cut-scenes," where you have to hit the right key at the right time as it flashes on the screen, for example.  You wind up dying a few times as you memorize it.  It's just so out-of-place from the rest of the game.
- The story and voice-acting are BAD.  I didn't believe my own character for a minute.  Certain things that I knew were going to happen at the start took painfully long to unfold.  I'll mention that the story is fairly bleak (lol), but I know a lot of you emo f*ckers are into that :p

Quake Live is in essence Quake III Arena with some changes (not necesarily improvements) but for the most part makes a great experience and a worthy update on a classic.
Maps
Can't complain on the number of maps to play, unfortunately there is no support for custom maps, if there was a system introduced for these that would make this game an even more incredible experience. Although some of the more hardcore maps from Q3 have been made a little more forgiving in the form of removing some obsticlles or adding small ledges to land on, although a lot of the new maps contain areas where I almost always plummet to my death.
Weapons
Yeah, they're all there as you remember (mostly) with the Team Arena weapons and the inclusion of a heavy machine gun, the usefulness of the standard machine gun seems to be improved although the railgun has been horribly nerfed so it is more of a support weapon than one for a quick and dirty takedown. I do like the damage boost for getting a direct hit with a rocket or a grenade which does help to make them more shoot to kill weapons than just for senselessly spamming. The nailgun from team arena also seems to suffer from a lack of usefulness as it seems to be very difficult to use in the few free for all maps it is on.
Features
There are a lot of little bells and whistles added like menu options for features in Q3 that are only availible via the console. Very few actually affect gameplay, mostly optional extra sounds for confirming frags and health-dependant hitsounds as well as damage indicators when you hit someone. You also have respawn indicators for super powerups like the quad damage and mega health. This does help make the game more accessible for newbies and does seperate the men from the boys as a lot of unskilled players will rush the quad damage whereas pros will hang back and cover the spot with a few rockets or grenades, make sure the are is clear then make a grab. The inclusion of choosing an additional weapon when you spawn is handy as well as it means you are only ever caught short if you've run out of ammo, rather than getting blown up upon spawning, I am also glad that the system where you can choose 2 weapons to spawn with in addition to the gauntlet has been changed. The only thing I don't like is that forcing bright skins and enemy models is on by default, this makes the game not initially look as good as it actually as, especially when you choose a player skin and only see everyone as Tank Jr.. There is also no blood in this game as it is marketed for teens, there isn't even a way to add gibs in, even if you could pay a minimum fee for gore rather than having sparks to represent blood that would make the game more aesthetically pleasing, although I do kind of prefer the spark effect to the blood in Q3 as I thought it looked too over-the-top and unrealistic. This also has full widescreen support wheres in Q3 you have t use the console and it stretches the HUD and vertically crops your FOV (the rocket launcher and lightning gun are barely visible when you're carrying them).
The only thing which makes this difficult for me to reccomend is the high system requirement considering the age of the original game and the fact that any graphics enhancements added into QL can be disabled, but it doesn't stop you being able to reduce the game's graphics below acceptable settings and still getting immense lag on most maps, even the ones that shipped with Q3. The devs seem to refuse to accept that the game is poorly optimised, or just tell you to disable post processing and you'll have the same performance (which is a big fat lie by the way). just google "Quake Live low FPS" and you'll see what I mean, although these posts are quite old by now they are still largely true unless you have an at least fairly current (at the time of writing) or high-end rig.
All in all a fantastic multiplayer experience, even if you are fairly casual, although I would recommend having a look at the training modes and tutorials to adapt your winning strategies.

Metro 2033 was definitely showing its age by the time the redux came out. I don't have the original on steam, just on console. It most likely looks much better on pc.
The Redux isn't just another "HD Retexture" of  2033; it is a complete rebuild of it on the Metro:LL engine. The enhancements made are obvious when you first boot up the game, but I'll do my best to break it down.
Graphics:
Compared to the orignal's graphics, this is a no contest. The skyboxes are better, the lighting is better, and the textures are better. I think there were a few textures that looked a bit low resolution, but it wasn't a bother. Overall, they more than hold their own against other recent games. 8.5/10
Sound:
The sounds in Metro Redux are excellent. Everything from ambient noise to the combat sounds were spot on. The ambient noise constantly kept me on edge, and did a great job in adding to the immersion. Personally, I think this is the strongest aspect of the game. 10/10
Story:
To avoid giving away spoilers, I'm going to keep this brief. It doesn't exactly follow the book, but it is still good, and believable in the context of the game. 8.5/10
AI:
Probably the worst part of the game. The AI is pretty bad, especially the friendly AI. It will not see enemies even when they are right in front of it, The enemy AI is also disappointing. It seems to ignore obvious signs of the player's presence, and has poor detection capabilities. Once combat starts, it still appears to have trouble finding good ways to engage the player. It blindly runs out of cover, straight into your line of fire, or ends up getting stuck in a neat single-file line as it approaches from a distance. However, it does have its moments, and can put up a serious challenge, especially at higher difficulties. 6.5/10
Overall, this game is solid, and well worth the money. If you enjoyed the original, I think you will enjoy this.

Another beautifully presented game about stabbing people from Klei Entertainment.
Unfortunately, the game heavily falls victim to default optimal strategy, or the "Hadouken Effect," or whatever you want to call it. There are some beautiful and fantastic combos you can pull off if you're willing to experiment and become actually good at the game, but there is one move that will carry you through the entire game with almost zero effort that is quite easy to discover within the first ten minutes of play. Fast-forward through two hours of spamming this move over and over and you have the casual experience of Shank. If you have a friend willing to join you in your jump-slashing spam spree, you can get another two hours out of the local co-op campaign, which was actually quite surprisingly long (about as long as single-player) and to put that much effort into a co-op campaign and make it local-only is somewhat baffling to me.
Also baffling is how the hard mode was handled. There are no checkpoints. Even the people who are really into this game admit that the hard mode is quite tedious and unfun. I'm all for arcade difficulty, and I would have expected a limited-lives system to come into play on hard mode, but you have literally one health bar to complete an entire stage. Ten minutes of gameplay in, and an enemy with a minigun can blow you to pieces with a stunlock-instadeath combo before you even know what happened. Hope you're good with the combat, otherwise you're going to repeat ten minutes of spamming again. This isn't even a pure beat-em-up, either. There are platforming sections, and the non-intuitive "hold right or left to advance, no matter what direction you're actually going" controls can easily send you plummetting to your inevitable instant death.
This is a hard game to recommend, but after watching a walkthrough done by someone familiar with the game's combat engine, I think it has a lot of potential for the diehard beat-em-up fans. If you liked other Klei games, particularly Shank 2, try out the demo and see what you think. Unless you're willing to keep replaying it, however, I'd wait for a sale if I were you.

Great game, can replay it several times and can have different experiances everytime. Vanilla (no dlc) XCOM: EU is worth the buy but getting the Enemy Within dlc really makes the game so much better, and often goes on sale. Adds a ton of options, customizable soldier options, new story mission, new rewards, more ways to deal with aliens (new useable items like flashbangs for example). Really opens up the game to have a lot more variety.
BUT ABOVE ALL ELSE, getting the Enemy Within content allows you to play with the Long War mod. Long War is free, and basically installs itself. It can be so brutal and fun, can make the game take much longer to complete, makes it much more possible to lose (like if you lose some of your best troops over and over, the aliens will just stomp you). It really makes the game what I think it should be imo. Revamps air battle, makes money and building your base much more important, mistakes you make really impact you.
So if you just get the vanilla XCOM: Enemy Unknown it is a good buy and can be a ton of fun learning and replaying. If you can get the Enemy Within DLC content it really makes the game much less rigid than vanilla. And if you choose, can play Long War if you have the DLC (pretty sure there is a non dlc long war, but it has much less features than the Enemy Within version). This is the story of my latest adventure
Day 1: I woke up in a strange facility, I have no clue who am I and why am I here.. Suddenly! Surprise Dogman appeared! I beat the living s**t out of it like there was no tomorrow until it stopped twitching.
It was a good work out I don't remember when was the last time I had a work out or if I even work out at all. My stomach made a rumbling noise so I went to search the place for food but only found a green bag with a white cross sign inside it was just a bunch of dumb pills.. I stared at the dead dog like creature feeling somewhat regretful for killing.. perhaps it was just trying to help me.. So I chopped his body into pieces and brought some wood from the nearby forest to make fire to cook it.
"This is what it would've wanted me to do" I thought to myself silently thanking it for becoming a meal and a coat but also silently hating it at the same time for not bringing any condiments with it.
After satisfying my stomach I went to stroll into the nearest town looking for any sign of civilization but nobody was here the streets were empty and ocassionally I'd see a few skeletons laying around, perhaps it's halloween and they're having a huge hide and seek event.. YES! that could only be the most logical reason!
I looked around inside buildings ocassionally taking items with me "I'm just gonna borrow this stuff I'm sure they wouldn't mind" I thought to myself as I grabbed as much stuff as I could carry.
It was starting to get dark and I was afraid if a stranger would walk up to me and offer me a sugar free candy, so I went back to the facility I woke up in and decided to call it home.
I saw a faint glow of light in the distance and I knew it.. they were hiding from me.. nobody hides from me.. nobo.. *falls asleep* zzzZZZzzzZZZzz...
Day 2: I had a good sleep last night but my stomach was beginning to complain again.. I went out and made myself a hardened spear before heading out any further.. just in case I encounter any stranger danger..
As I headed out toward where I last saw the glow of light I spotted more Town! as I sprinted toward the town I came across a friendly stranger.
He was carrying a revolver he must be dressing up as a cowboy and he was also wearing a pair of croc so I asked him to give me all of his stuff because my stuff sucks, but he refused and start to charge at me, The nerve of some people I tell you! So I poked him on the head with my sharp stick, he fell and was crawling away from me as he beg for mercy so I gave him what he wanted and kept poking him with my sharp stick until he was no longer in pain.
I was pretty happy that I could borrow his croc I saw that cool kids wear these kind of sho- err sandals..? what ever it is.. the cool kids on the old worn out poster wear it so I'm a cool kid now.
OH! and he also had an expired cracker and some ketchup! So I hack him and whack him and chop him since there's no point to let him go to waste no siree! he would've want me to eat him or else he would've told me stories about starving childrens in some distant foreign land! So being the civilized human being I am, I cooked him as best as I could with the few ingridients he had on him that I'm sure would've made Gordon Ramsay proud.
Today was a good day I said to myself as I went to sleep.
Day 3: A noise woke me up today.. it was a guy! He tried to take my precious empty bottle in the corner! “My Precious!!!” I shouted as I charge toward him and knocked some debris toward him, the debris made him vulnerable and as he tries to recover I stabbed him with my sharp pointy stick and carved a hole in his right arm.
I kept stabbing him with my pointy stick as I hissed at him aggressively, nobody touches my precious! Nobody but me!
I lacerated, gashed and carved him into pieces there was no mercy.. it was the sacrifice my precious neede- Oohh!! He had a crowbar! Now I can dress up as Gordon Freemsay the Angry crazy canibalistic chef with a Phd!
And so I ventured out as Gordon Freemsay! Suddenly 3 Dog appeared! I knew it.. I should’ve double tapped him when I last met him at Galaxy News Radio.. now he reappeared before me as an actual 3 Dog!
So I demolished one of the closest dog’s head using my crowbar! That really got the attention of the other 2 Dog and again I demolished the other dog head, it seem that knocked some sense to the last dog as it tries to fall back from me but it knew.. it knew it was too late.. it knew that it had done f**ked up and “WHACK!!” that was the last thing it heard.. “nobody.. mess with Gordon Freemsay..” I said to it in a silent hiss.
As I went on my way I was again approached by more meanies.. they just don’t know when to quit..
After slaughtering about 2 more Dog and 2 Stranger with an angry mother issue, I went off to go shopping for a sauce pan and back pack and found a cool sled and since I’m not a thief I left my plastic shopping bag with some rotting left over cooked human meat as a trade in case the owner came back.
It was another great day, I cooked some water from a nearby lake so I can wash my boo-boo away and bottle some more in case I made some more boo-boo.
I also did an art and craft project by stringing small can with a handful of strings and pebbles it made music if people step or trip on them! It will be a great addition to my house!
Day 4: My art and craft project ringed in the middle of the night.. *sigh* I guess it’s time for a midnight snack, it was a dogie! “Chinese food it is then” I lured it into a trap but it still managed to scratch my coat before I stabbed a new nose into it’s lung and bled all over the floor.
Great.. now I’m gonna have to clean that up.. *sigh* why do they have to make things difficult I grumble to myself as I enjoy my midnight snack and went back to sleep but as soon as I closed my eyes another stranger ringed my welcome bell.. I got up and quickly took cover.. I couldn’t see where or who this stranger was so I lashed out and swinged my sharp pointy stick wildly to where I think he’s at but this stranger managed to shred my upper left leg, I fell to the ground and just then I knew.. I done goofed.. and all the horrible things I’ve done.. I’ve become a monster.. and I didn’t want to acknowledge that.. I was in denial all this time.. this is it.. my time has finally come.. I am ready.. do your worst Karma.. and just like that I passed out..
...
Everything was silent.. I woke up.. there was a bright light as if the sun was shining upon me..
...
Wait a minute.. it actually is the sun! And sure enough! there he was.. The f**ker that tried to kill me! Laying on the ground with a hole in his chest.. Boy~! I sure didn’t learn a single thing from that experience so I cut that f**ker up and ate him. It sure was a glorious day in this man army! And it was pretty nice of him to bring me a hunting rifle with a scope, strap and there's even a bullet in it aww that's so sweet of him.
I enjoyed the rest of the day munching on the left over while reading the outdated newspaper man.. I wish I had some fava beans and a nice chianti to go with this live- shh!! There were noises outside.. and sure it was another stranger waiting in the nearby outskirt of the forest.. and so Gordon Freemsay continues his rampage in this post-apocalyptic world..

The game did have it's delays and is off to a bumpy start; thats usually what happens to some ports no?  It does suck however, that multiplayer will be delayed for a while (approx. 3 months...I never do research because why not go with the flow instead of waiting for a day then get angry if it needs to be delayed again?) so you can only play offline with other keyboards/gamepads (do your research lol; this is based off of 30 minutes of playing the game).
The controls at the beginning caught me off guard (mouse and keyboard wtffff) but was easily adjustable once I plugged in my Xbox 360's controller (I recommend you exit the game, plug your controller in and then reboot the game...otherwise plugging the controller in will trigger as a 2nd player and be confusing as fuhhh).
Reading some of the comments, there are still a lot of issues with the game (something about user names...saves...I don't know; too much hassle to worry/think about no?) so it's obvious that this game is on a bumpy start.
Gamers...life is often not (for me usually never) in our favors and we face hardships (y u 2 hard 2 contollz /y u s0 fuhke ugli...etc) time from time. Some games port excellently while others are poor. Some games we never heard of are easy and fun to play while some games we loved on other consoles are broken and unplayble at times.
For 36 bucks, you get a game full of pretty women (and I think 2 cute young girls....no pervert.....just a little) and several Mr. Universes (macho men to me.....besides Elliot....pretty boy hey-o!) and you beef it out with AIs or friends (and soon to be online). Personally, it doesn't matter if this game is on PC or Xbox or Playstation...its still a game, and games are meant to be played and enjoyed...never forget that.
I would recommend this if you are patient for updates that come (hopefully yeah?).
If you wanted the perfect game on launch; then this is probably not for you... Actually, just get a friend to buy it then crash his house and play on his/her PC... :) save 36 bucks...he-he.

dying light is one of those games where you start playing and you cant stop because its so fun. you are crane, an
american that knows what's he doing and helping everyone in need. the game features a day-night cycle which is a pretty crucial part of the game as in night time the gameplay changes drasticly. in the day you are searching for crafting parts for weapons, the weapons itself, people to help and zombies to kill obviously. but in the night you are the hunted (usually) and you need to watch out for the volatiles that look like monsters from my nightmares and if you are brave, hunt bolters and get the expensive and wonderfull tissue they have. :)
the game also has parkour which is famous for, very creative brutality for (humans and zombies alike) and pretty nice graphics.
though in the start of the game it can be really difficult to get better weps and kill zombies easily but when you do, its worth it because you can play surgeon simulator in dying light. the gore in this game is very nice, you can rip off zombie limbs, legs, heads or simply blow them to oblivion. my favorite weapon in dying light is the baseball bat with the purple neon glow on it with an impact modifier because it like a skull-splitter you hit them in the head and the head is gone nothing more nothing less the weapons in this game can range from simple oars to massive hammers that look more like spikes that you step on and die (legos???) the weapons aren't only diverse, they are smexy af. as i mentioned before there is a neon glowing baseball bat but there are also glowing machettes, swords, axes, sickles and even sexier weapons.
the weapon part of the game and the gore are probably the best in my opinion.
the parkour part of the game is also a good part of the game because its PARKOUR how can you not have fun climbing with your super-man-like-hands buildings and running on rooftops, though there is an annoying part of parkour and that is the tic-tac ability. for those who dont know tic-tac allows you to climb on wall without using ledges and then you can jump of the wall/building to escape zombies or perform and ariel move like drop attack or ground pound (which is fun af)
sounds good right?
WRONG
the keys to use tic-tac are very similar to climbing on walls using ledges like you always do so you can be climbing a building having a good time and then you exectue the move and you are stuck on the wall in the animation.
if you are like me then you will instantly press space to climb the next ledge but you will jump to your death and unless you have a grapple hook you are ♥♥♥♥ed and there is almost nothing you can do. other than that the parkour aspect of the game is really good. ( when you choose to apply this ability or any ability to your agility/power/survivor skill tree you CAN'T rewind and use that skill point to an other perk/ability)
the graphics: the graphics in this game are really good though the game can get pretty laggy pretty quickly especially when you go on a mass killing spree but thats probably my PC specs that i need to change a bit.
the storyline: you are an american that landed in harran, a zombie infested quarantined city with 2 main factions rulling it: rais' guys and the tower. when you are in harran you are bitten and you are forced to stay with the tower. you are dropped in harran to find a missing flie of the globabl relief effort that's suppose to cure the harran virus (aka zombie virus) but as you proggress through the game you will find out that they are evil but you still save the world and the end of the main storyline is unkown as it ends after you killed the main evil bad guy and then you are supose to bring something he stole to someone but there is no quest for that afterwards so i think it ended after that scene.
overall the story isnt bad but. i do think that you are the bad guy as you kill 2 good guys and because of you another 3rd dude in the start dies and you destroyed a full crate of the medicine for the zombie virus
something that i dont like exepct for tic-tac: you are forced to play the good guy (though you did pretty terrible stuff to the people of the tower) and you are forced to play with the tower guys and do EVERYTHING they ask you do and you cant say NO to them you are forced to do what they want.

Metro 2033 was definitely showing its age by the time the redux came out. I don't have the original on steam, just on console. It most likely looks much better on pc.
The Redux isn't just another "HD Retexture" of  2033; it is a complete rebuild of it on the Metro:LL engine. The enhancements made are obvious when you first boot up the game, but I'll do my best to break it down.
Graphics:
Compared to the orignal's graphics, this is a no contest. The skyboxes are better, the lighting is better, and the textures are better. I think there were a few textures that looked a bit low resolution, but it wasn't a bother. Overall, they more than hold their own against other recent games. 8.5/10
Sound:
The sounds in Metro Redux are excellent. Everything from ambient noise to the combat sounds were spot on. The ambient noise constantly kept me on edge, and did a great job in adding to the immersion. Personally, I think this is the strongest aspect of the game. 10/10
Story:
To avoid giving away spoilers, I'm going to keep this brief. It doesn't exactly follow the book, but it is still good, and believable in the context of the game. 8.5/10
AI:
Probably the worst part of the game. The AI is pretty bad, especially the friendly AI. It will not see enemies even when they are right in front of it, The enemy AI is also disappointing. It seems to ignore obvious signs of the player's presence, and has poor detection capabilities. Once combat starts, it still appears to have trouble finding good ways to engage the player. It blindly runs out of cover, straight into your line of fire, or ends up getting stuck in a neat single-file line as it approaches from a distance. However, it does have its moments, and can put up a serious challenge, especially at higher difficulties. 6.5/10
Overall, this game is solid, and well worth the money. If you enjoyed the original, I think you will enjoy this.

THE GOOD
Shank controls nicely on the gamepad (Which is what the devs want you to play this on) and feel better than the PC controls, although Shank is a spam fest either way. Button-mashing is inevitable and gameplay is repetative as the same enemies will attack you in the same ways. I never said that it wasn't fun though, as Shank pulls it off with such style that I really cannot find the gameplay boring. Sure the enemies will take a long time to kill and you will take some damage in the process but it's fair and will drop you health and extra weapons for your troubles.
THE GREAT
Graphically I cannot find fault with Shank's aesthetic. The character animations are smooth, the character models are functional, the backgrounds (Silhouettes) do thier job and the scenery looks pleasing at the very least. Shank seems to break up the fighting from time to time by adding in puzzle sections which flows nicely and gives players hands a rest from the constant button-mashing. Mechanics of Shank are fairly simple with not too much getting in the way of redecorating the walls with enemies intestines, and on the topic of intestines it feels like the devolpers wanted this to be more violent in parts. I expected some gruesome deaths from enemies once I got a high enough combo which makes you feel that this game is censored. We'll get to that later.
THE UGLY
It's later. The story is absolutely terrible and it seems that the main character, appropriately named Shank is just out to kill the Big Bad because he doesn't lke him. I played the Steam version through to the second boss fight and then downloaded the Humble Bundle 4 version (Which I got a while ago) and noticed that the cutscenes had been changed to the point where the story makes no sense. I cannot understand why Steam would censor an M rated game, but I'm not complaining. The only other real issue is the fact that this game was made for the gamepad. It says so on the intro screen and shows it by having the default controls worse than my home country's rating system. These are two seemingly petty gripes but they really ruin the experince.
THE VERDICT
Do you see how I've recommended this game? I've recommended it on two conditions. These follow:
1- You own a gamepad as the default and customizable controls are terrible
2- You don't care about the story/you watch the cutscenes through YouTube to grasp the story/you'll played this game on console and know the story
These are the only conditions I would recommend Shank and that's a real shame because I like Shank, I possibly even love Shank, but if I'm being honest then that's my recommendation to you.

FTL is one of those gems that makes its way through a mist of what is fast becoming a fairly bland state of affairs for indie titles. On the surface, it is a space adventure rogue-like, and as such you can expect death at any time, but like any good rogue-like, failure is almost always your own doing. The goal is simple enough - Pick your ship, name your crew (or don't) and hope that each sector you visit gets you the weapons and tools necessary to survive and warn the Federation of the incoming Rebel armada bearing down on them. Along the way you will encounter hostile ships, inncocent folk in distress, random events and new ships to unlock.
The primary gameplay is centered around combat. FTL features a real-time with pause combat system that has you managing systems and the state of your ship and crew along with targeting your own weapons on enemy hardpoints. Want to have an easier time of things? Target the weapons. But I can't get through the shields! Then you ought to weaken it with an ion weapon, missile blast or even send crewmembers to attack the enemey ship from within. Be careful, though - The enemy can do the same. When not in combat, you will be assissting anyone you come across, or taking advantage of their misfortune and gaining some scrap, which is the primary currency in this game. The more scrap you obtain, the more system upgrades and shop items you can by. But you'd better make sure your hull plating is up to scratch, particularly in a Mantis controlled sector.
Speaking of which, FTL features many species all with their own strengths and weaknesses. Want strong fighters onboard? Make it an effort to acquire as many Rockmen and Mantis on your ship. Or maybe you want to concetrate on maintaining your ship and its systems. Engi and Zoltans lack fighting strength but more than make up for that with excellent repair and power management capabilities. Interraction with these species is perhaps the other major half of the game. Having the right system upgrade or species onboard can reveal a special blue option in certain scenarios, often reaping greater rewards for you.
The only aspect of the game I can understand people not liking is the difficulty spike when reaching the final sector. The Rebel flagship is downright unfair at times, but after a few encounters with it, you will learn of its weaknesses and can plan accordingly, which is the core of most of the enjoyment you will find with this game. It's simple, yet engrossing, challenging, yet rewarding. FTL is an easily recommended game for anyone remotely interested in the space and rogue-like genre, especially with the advent of the free advanced edition content. Buy it with the soundtrack.

Yesterday was my first day playing this game in EA. I'll start off with saying that I can understand the mixed reviews.
It indeed does look and feel like ark. Same engine with more or less the same controls. I'm not really complaining however. I always look up some video's first anyway before I buy something, so I knew this from forehand.
The reason why I still wanted to buy this is because this game brings in or will bring in some extra features I felt were lacking in Ark. I played Ark for a few 100 hours and really missed the pvp aspect. Even when I played on PVP servers.. You just get to know the other people on the server and well that's where pvp stops I guess. You just know you'll get screwed over if you raid your neighbours.. The factions with an elected king and cross server PVP in Dark & Light will hopefully counter this (we'll see).. Another thing for me was the lack of a community feeling, safe trading posts (cities), quests, and so on. With ark you kept on hearing "what's the purpose", "what can we do other then taming and building".  Many ARK mods tried to counter this such as the "NPC mod" which were just dino's with a humanoid look or "trading and economy" mods out of which none really worked well.
In short Ark is solely a survival game nothing more, Dark & light (will) implement(s) more MMO features.

What I hope for the future to improve the game is although an already big map, a larger map which can host more players (wow style).
- A banking system to store items (or just money) and an auction system to sell or buy goods.
- more craftable items including rare and legendary items
- I would like them to revise the skill leveling mechanics so that you can concentrate on leveling certain things instead of just leveling everything.
- Being able to build closer to other players in certain areas to create townships even though they're not of the same house (tribe).
- Better optimization (ofcourse).
- NPC stables where you can house your animals if need be.
- Some kind of lore
- Siege weapons such as huge catapults or rams (maybe only as a mod or something ^^)
If you want to buy this game, please consider it's still in early EA. So it's buggy and not yet optimized.
If you're however doubting whether to buy this or ARK. I'd say buy this because ARK is kinda overpriced right now and this game albeit some bugs offers more and still needs to grow.
All in all this game is a COULD BE awesome game. We'll just have to wait and see.

Metro 2033 Redux is a post-apocalyptic fps that puts alot of emphasis on survival. With ammunition, grenades, medical items, and gasmask filters coming in a somewhat limited supply. The currency of the game is a certain type of bullets, "Military Grade Rounds", that are more powerful than the "Makeshift Counterparts" but using these is basically "shooting money" so the player should be wary when using them.
When it comes to gameplay, Metro 2033 Redux, has a fantastic stealth and detection system combining both sound and vision. The player can turn off, or shoot out, lights and can crouch for added stealth.
From the famous AK-47 to throwing knives, Metro offers a wide assortment of weapons and hefty
customization. It lets the player choose what best suits their needs from supressors and weapon stocks to laser sights and scopes. There are several different weapon types to choose from aswell, including assault rifles, revolvers, shotguns, and many more.
When playing the game and walking around in the tunnels you get this empty feeling, and that really improves the gameplay. But one thing, that I thought was outstanding, was that when you for the first time exit the tunnels and lay eyes upon Moscow, this massive, desolate city. It's a breathtaking view.
The games story is absolutely fantastic and it sucks you right in. Metro 2033 Redux is a game worth playing and is truly an excellent game.

It's only been out for like 4 or 5 days as I write this.  Now the negative reviews call it an ARK clone, loading screen simulator, too buggy to function, not optimized, etc.  Now If you think ARK ran perfectly when it first came out then you're living under a rock.  That game is now 60 bucks and there's still things broken about it they haven't fixed.
I don't have much time in it yet, but it's been fairly enjoyable so far even with the bugs.  I think the whole design is a cooler concept than ARK because I'm more interested in fantasy with magic over guns and rockets and explosives.  I'll just kind of point out some things I think are good an bad so far and maybe they'll positively or negatively influence depending on how you view your games.
PROS:
- Starting towns.  You don't have to just spawn somewhere in the wild without protection.  There's 3 starting towns so far at least.
- Skills system.  I think its pretty cool that you can master everything over time, but should probably focus in several aspects first and team up with people to divide and conquer.
- Magic.  Nuff said.  Really though the magic is pretty cool for quite a few of the spells.  Someday I'll get telekinesis and be a human catapult launching rocks.
- Taming.  It's an "ARK clone" afterall.  Taming is done a bit different though
- No engrams.  As you master skills you learn the crafting items that way.  It might seem odd at first to try and earn a campfire, but you can get apples til then to stave off hunger.
BUGS:
WARNING: A lot of these will probably be fixed at a later as they figure everything out.
- Going uphill.  So there's times where you can't walk up a simple hill.  It's apparently slightly too steep so you gotta try jumping (about a 50/50 chance) or find a way around even if it looks like you could easily walk up it.
- Wraiths.  Not sure if its a bug, but legit they just spawn at night to specifically screw me over lol.  I spent a few in game days making my first epic straw house only to get it instantly destroyed by a wraith that spawned on me while I was getting the wall torches.  RIP goals for the day, but it was ok.  They also keep spawning outside the spawn town and without NPCs to help it can be off putting at times.  I gotta lead them into other people to be free.
- Destroyed house items.  Demolishing home items can spawn in boulder-like untextured blocks that are rather big, but they fade away shortly after so don't worry.
- Melee hit boxes.  I can swing a sheep forever and only land a few swings.  I guess that's what fireball is for, but sometimes you just wanna smack things up.
CONS:  (Wanted to point out some bugs first before this)
- Choosing a town isn't really like choosing a faction. Metro 2033 Redux is by and far one of the most immersive shooters I have played since Bioshock.  The game starts out as you playing a silent protagonist named Artyom.  In this world, Moscow has been severely bombed and the surface world is no longer suitable for human habitation, the only reason you are alive is due to being underground in the Metro at the time of the bombing.  Artyom since he was a young boy, all he’s known is living underground and protecting his home from the various trials and tribulations that this new stark world throws at them daily.
The main plot is that Artyom is tasked with trekking through the Metro system to contact the Rangers to warn them of the oncoming Dark Ones threat rapidly approaching his home station, Exhibition.  The main focus of the game is survival horror/shooter but has an amazing narrative and plenty of colorful npcs and situations that really flesh out the story.  Right from the get go, you learn that life in the Metro is very different from what the surface world once was.  Most things are scarce in the story, food consists mostly of what little livestock that had before the bombing, supplemented with the strange glowing mushrooms that grow within the tunnels.  In addition to this harsh and downtrodden life people hardly eek out, the currency in the Metro is military grade ammunition and is used for all purchases the player will make.  These purchases consist of guns, customizable attachments, bombs, knives, med-packs and air filters.
The main obstacle Artyom has to overcome is the mutated wild life in and outside of the tunnels, but the game sprinkles in bandits, Communists and Nazis factions to mix things up.  To get the full ride from this game, I highly recommend you play on survival mode, which will limit all materials you find and make your decisions have all the more impact on your continued living.  You’ll quickly appreciate the stealth kills when your ammo, bombs and med-packs are running low.  Survival mode keeps the game challenging and making you want to keep pushing through these harsh environments with a relative haste and not waste attitude.
One of the few discrepancies I had with that game is that they never explain the watch that is on Artyoms’ left wrist.  It is an indicator of several things all at once, the blue light on the side tells you if you are completely in darkness and if anything can see you.  The most vital of the functions is it will start beeping when you are standing in a radiation hot zone and you need to rush out of there.  And finally if you pay attention to the hands, it will let you know how much time you have left on your gas mask filter but the game usually prompts you with a message and an easily identifiable set of sounds when it’s time regardless.  I just wish that would have been in the initial tutorial, but as far as complaints go that’s pretty minor.
Bottom line, this is truly a great game, I enjoyed all 10 hours of it and plan on doing multiple play-throughs.  Quality-wise I would rank it right up there with Farcry, Bioshock and Borderlands.  Hopefully that is an indication if you would like it.

I just finished Metro 2033 Redux a while ago, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. One of the best things is that the game is COMPLETELY in a first person perspective, including the cutscenes. Reminded me of Bioshock Infinite a bit in that respect. You are fully immersed in your world. Except for the ending though..for some reason they chose to do a zoomed out pre-rendered cutscene there.
I played on Survival mode (normal difficulty) and the challenge was decent. At one or two points in the game, it wasn't clear to me what to do (probably wasn't paying attention to the dialogues), but I like the no-hand-holding thing. At the last level as well, I ended up running out of filters (pretty sure I scoured all around for supplies and hit the limit many times) so that kinda took away from the experience a bit.
But otherwise, the story was good. Decent enemy variation. Stealth is possible against humans as well (game doesn't explicitly tell you this IIRC). Just make sure you crouch all the time and turn off your flashlight!
Combat was great as well. The weapon handling felt really good. I found a quad-barrel shotgun and that was massive. Killed all Watchmen in a single shot!
Atmosphere was realistic and well done. Performance was great as well on my humble GTX 750 (with medium settings).
It's hard for me to find fault with the game. I went in with little expectation, but then again I also don't play much FPS games. This is definitely better gameplay wise than Bioshock Infinite and Spec Ops: The Line though.

This game should've been a shoo-in for a recommendation. A classic side-scrolling beat 'em up with a graphic novel feel set in the Mexican underworld featuring machetes, chainsaws and epic wrestlers? What could go wrong?
Firstly, the good. The game is pretty gorgeous, nicely stylised backdrops and beautiful graphics generally. Over-the-top gory action is par for the course, with you cutting through legions of troops with guns, blades and grenades. Whilst the game warns that it plays better with a gamepad, it's still perfectly playable on a keyboard, with enough move combinations and enemies to keep the game interesting. There's even a passable storyline!
Yet something went awry with the game testing. There are only two difficulty modes. The easier one is so straightforward that the game only lasts just over an hour. Although the learning curve is pretty well planned, there aren't many tricky sections, the boss fights feel like choreographed cutscenes, and you're more likely to die from learning where the pitfalls are or being hit by a random projectile. You'd think the hard mode would fix these issues, making the game more challenging, but whilst the bad guys have indeed been beefed up and the fights become much more tense as a result, more importantly each level has to be completed without checkpoints! Since some of the levels are over 10 minutes long (one even includes a mini-boss fight halfway through), there's just oodles of frustration waiting to be had here attempting the missions over and over, only to fall down a hole you didn't even know was there after 10 minutes of playing and have to restart.
Overall a decent little game for the price, especially if you can pick it up on offer. The graphics are gorgeous, the gameplay entertaining, and there's even a little local co-op which I haven't yet tried. But the fact that this game only comes with game modes for children and masochists and nothing in between makes it difficult to give more than a borderline recommendation.

By the time of this late review, you've probably have already made your mind about this nearly 3 year old game. I'm simply reviewing to state my interpretation. Shank is a revenge tale played in a 2D platforming brawler. Gameplay is somewhat comparble to the Devil May Cry series, with a standard attack, a secondary weapon attack and guns that can be switched on the fly, grapple and pounce moves, and a grenade to cause heavy damage. The combat is pretty simplistic, and often spammy, as mashing the standard attacks is sometimes the best way to deal with single enemies and small groups. That isn't to say there isn't some complexity with the fact that some enemies can shoot from afar, block or dodge your attacks, or perform unblockable power attacks. The majority of the combat boils down to managing gun shooters and grenade throwers while a handful of standard grunts and a "big guy" or two that require you to dodge or block their attacks. Platform segments are simple and are nearly automatic, but   can become a little annoying when you miss a grab point or are hit by a projectile mid-jump.
The game's simplicity is both it's main pro and con - it's a simple, very short story with easy to grasp controls and enjoyable "mindless bloodshed". It also means the game becomes fairly predictable and leaves most the game easily beat by "spamming main attack" or "spamming pistols" until you win (this will not always work though, and it pays to mix it up on tougher enemies and large groups). I beat it in less than 3 hours, which is crazy short, but I'm also perfectly fine with that because any longer probably would have outstayed it's welcome for me. (another backlogged title defeated!).
You won't find the new revolution in brawlers here, but you have a solid action title that's enjoyably mindless.

HOARD is a short, birds eye perspective, simple board style game where your sole purpose is to be a loot hungry colorful dragon that flies around, uses firebreath to burn down farms, mills, towns, trade carts and towers. With each thing you burn, you collect gold which you carry back to your lair to gain points. Not only that, but you get to kill knights and kidnap princesses. How awesome is that?
The aim of the game is to get as many points as possible in the ten minutes time that is allowed. That's it. Every game is ten minutes, and there is a variety of maps to choose from. With your treasure points, you can level up in each ten minute game, and choose different stats to boost. You can improve flying speed, flame power, gold carrying capacity, or your defence. You can't max all of them during a mission, so you level according to your playstyle. Do you like being a glass cannon that flies fast? Do you like being able to carry a lot of loot and tank everything? It's up to you.
It can be frustrating to play against friends as well since you can damage them and force them to drop their treasure if their health drops to zero. In Co-Op you can't damage each other. You can choose to play with your friends or against them, but in against, prepare for a little rage to happen.
It can be played as a singleplayer or multiplayer game, so you can play all with friends, or with one or two against the computer. It's actually pretty good as the computer AI isn't easy to compete against. This makes it just as fun alone as with friends, and because the games are always so short, it leaves you plenty of time to do other things as well, instead of needing to be committed to one game for hours on end.
Better played with a gamepad. Otherwise Keyboard WASD to move and your mouse to burn things. They are a little clunky at times.
The sound is relaxing, to the point you don't notice it as you focus on the game, it's perfect background noise. However, it can also be grating when your mission is nearing the end of the ten minute timer as it then becomes more noticeable,  since it makes you feel oh dear time is running out help!
Though its a simple and small game, nothing to get committed to, it can be the perfect game after a long and hard day, and you just want to relax to something by yourself for ten or so minutes at a time not having to worry about anything other than collect treasure with your purple flying dragon.
And tell me... Who doesn’t want to be a dragon!

Tropico is a city building game along the lines of Simcity.  Although a great deal of attention has been paid to creating depth for the game, it suffers from one huge deficit that limits long term playability.  It lacks a way to flatten (or alter) terrain, leaving the most interesting parts of the map unusable.
Really, what's the point of building a huge statue if you can't place it at the top of a cliff, or up on the side of a mountain where everyone can see it?  On one Kalypso forum,  they claimed that this 'feature' was included by design to make the game more challenging.  If so, this was a bad decision.  This same approach to terrain makes road placement difficult and imprecise.
Bottom line : maybe they fixed this in version 5, but I'm not spending the money to find out.

I've recently starter to have serious lag issues with this game. Initially I thought it was just multiplayer, but then quickly realised that it was single player as well. There are a ton of posts about this online but none seem to have offered any solution that worked. Most date from a few years back and therefore the new updates since then claim to have dealt with these issues. I run a Lenovo Z500 and am able to run games like Assassins Creed in high detail with absolutely no difficulty at all.
It's therefore very frustrating that  game more than ten years old stutters and lags every time a command is given or a unit moves or something eventful happens in the game. I've tried turning off details like v-sync and 3d water (which really I shouldn't have to), I've tried the "-nostartup" solution in the command line and I've even set my computer to use the on board graphics when opening this game. None of these solutions have worked.
To top it off there seems to be very little user support. Most of the solutions are several years old now, and the only response I seem to have gotten was a poor English explanation that "it must be something you are doing wrong".
I would advise anyone looking for a souped up modern, fast running version of this classic game to bide their time until the developers really sort this problem out. I have a few friends who play this game and all face the same problem. It isn't the product it should be, and is so laggy and slow that it's basically unplayable.
I purchased the African Kingdoms thinking it would also act as an update to the main game, but really it's just the campaign scenarios and sprite files for the new units/buildings. There does not appear to be any update to the core game mechanics which suffer terribly from the slow down. It's difficult to understand how such an old game runs so slowly and lags so much.
A great shame.

I've played this game for 14 hours, and I'm angry. Hear me roar.
I played for 14 hours, slaughtered COUNTLESS beasties, raiders and robbers. I killed something called a "melonhead" and I've slaughtered so many dogs I could wear their skins and pretend to be the wolf-man.
It was at that time - as I munched down another human steak, made on the desecrated remains of a man who had tried to steal my sled in the middle of the night, that I was assaulted. Well, it was actually while I slept after having eaten the corpse of the aformentioned adversary, seeing as time apparently stops when you eat things.
In any case, let me recount to you, the story of Philip the Doghide boy.
Philip, just as any man, awoke from cryogenic stasis in a secret lab, where he was quickly faced with a hideous creature screaming like the midnight wind 'cross a praire of bones so sharp as knives. And much like that praire of bones, the dogman was soon still and dead. You see, Philip was a total badass, and he vanquished this horrific beast with a few swift uppercuts and rock-hard right-left combos. The beast lay dead, and not satisfied with merely having sent this beast's soul to dogman-heaven, Philip decided that it's skin looked comfortable. He grabbed a shard of glass, cut it open and wore it's pelt - face and all, possibly while dancing to some trance-music and smearing cheap lipstick on himself. Naked. In front of a mirror.
After that psychadellic trip, Philip wandered out into the wilderness, wearing nothing but the skin of his dead adversary. He was messed with. Attacked by rabid dogs and feral.. Dogs. And more dogs. This game has a lot of dogs. If you don't like killing dogs, this is probably not the game for you.
Anyway, needless to say, dogs never really posed a problem for Philip. Philip had two good pairs of hands, and he had a shank made of glass in one of them. Philip was not to be ♥♥♥♥ed with.
Now, Philip was a hulking mass of death, even when armed with nothing but a shard of glass, so I'll assume you understand what happened when Philip found a crowbar and a loaded shotgun in a shed. That's right. Philip turned into a lean, mean, psychopathic killing machine. This brings us to a dark chapter of Philip's life. The killing. The killing never stopped.
Philip was a soulless husk of a man, and that crowbar whispered sweet things in his ears at night. It craved for blood. Lusted for it. Philip was renamed "Philip Mordake".
Philip tried to fight it, of course. Philip was no murderer.. Philip merely loved to kill dogs, but that didn't matter. For each person that crossed Philip's path, the crowbar screamed. It pleaded, begged and demanded of Philip.. Terrible things. Great things. But terrible things.
It drove him to insanity, the whispering. The screams. They all melded together as Philip gave in to the crowbar's crazed yelling. He'd separate flesh from bone, and smash until there was nothing left but something that barely resembeled a human. He'd eat the flesh. Why not? Cut it loose with a shard of glass, and eat chunk by chunk until he was no longer starving.
Philip's path on this strange earth was carved from the blood and bone of any that entered his path. Any that dared touch his sled. Philip was a cruel God on this earth, his fury tempestous and his retribution violent and brutal as it was swift. He cut many a foe from existance, and wore their remains as trophies.
This brings us to the end of Philip's journey. For Philip had been surprised to wake up in the middle of the night, at the sound of somebody stealing his sled! That could not happen - no not at all. And Philip's recourse to this - though predictable - was a thing to behold. He knocked down that poor thief, and whaled with his crowbar until there was naught left of his adversary. Philip hadn't even been injured at this. He was in perfect health, and continued to be so as he smeared himself with the blood of his enemy (note; you can't actually do this in the game. You'll wish you could, though.) and sat himself down again. He dozed off, and once more awoke. This time, to the face of the very first foe that he'd faced.
It was a Dogman, looming above him like a gaunt, shadowy behemoth. The crowbar awoke. It screamed. It begged for blood, and Philip didn't have to be asked twice. He leapt for the creature! He cut it down, and bit it's flesh with that accursed crowbar time and time again! A hailstorm of blows weakened the beast, and it desperately slashed out!
...
Philip was struck in the heart, and died immediately. And the crowbar fell from his hand, going silent.. It was just a normal crowbar.
Now, you might think that's an amusing story. Or maybe you hated that story, but let me tell you what.
I spent 14 HOURS. 14 BLOODY HOURS ON PHILIP.
Philip was a GODDAMNED MONSTER! He was the toughest thing since diamonds armed with shanks in a cuban jail.
He'd survived battles with up to three opponents at once, and though injured, he'd come out on top.
And now he just got killed instantly because of some fantastic stroke of good fortune for some psuedo-werewolf.
This game is interesting, but it's interesting for about 10 minutes. If you've discovered amazing loot in one house, you've basically found all there is in this game. Sure, there are random events and such, but very few of them actually lead anywhere. You're Philip, and you'll always be Philip. Not Philippa, or Sam, or James the Jive♥♥♥♥♥Jukebox Jockey. Philip.
You'll pick your perks, disadvantages and roll out. You die because of silly reasons or because you had a bad start. And then you have to start all over, without any progress having been made.
After a while, it becomes tedious. It's not fun to micro-manage your campfire, clothes, hydration and hunger-levels, as well as spend the ENTIRE GAME TRYING TO FALL ASLEEP, I MEAN♥♥♥♥♥♥ JUST FALL ASLEEP, MAN! YOU JUST MASSACRED AN ENTIRE VILLAGE!
All in all, I'd refund this game if I hadn't hate♥♥♥♥ed 14 hours of gameplay out of it. Do yourself a favour and look at a youtube-clip of somebody playing it without audio first. That will be your life in this game. Like what you see? Go for it.

I watched Indie Game: The Movie and bought this game on sale. After about 4 hours, I did everything except for the speedruns, which I decided weren’t worth my time.
The story just seems all over the place, I know it's supposed to be out of order, but what order is it supposed to be in exactly? Reading through the texts, almost nothing seemed to be part of some cohesive story line and nothing was even enjoyable to read. What a terrible epilogue. Far before the end of the game, I had lost all interest in the story, which comes off as pretentious.
Puzzle difficulty increases almost exponentially, which would be fine if there was more instruction on your new powers than just "The Pit" levels at the beginning of each world, especially with the ring.
The art is also very off-putting to me. The main character, Tim, has this unsettling stare up into the sky, like he’s looking at nothing and his expressions consist of a creepy toothless smile and what looks like a frown maybe? One of the puzzles has the gall to make use of the jigsaw puzzle pieces scattered throughout the game, as if the bland looking platforms are distinct somehow.
Most of the music was good, at least the first time I heard it. In world 4, since your movements change time, each level is really only about 8-20 seconds of real music and you get to hear it all distorted and weird for like 30 minutes as you struggle through the puzzles.
This game was enjoyable for about 45 minutes and I don’t recommend buying it at full price under any circumstance.
Edit: I have since read the Wikipedia article about this game and it just about validates every single problem I had with this game. Blow basically says outright that the story is whatever you thought it was (in my case it was trash). Blow was so pretentious about his game that he didn't think anyone was smart enough to make a soundtrack for it. And again, Tim looks like Chucky.
I have also realized that this game is, in fact, not at all as intelligent as it is made out to be. Just because you can't understand something, doesn't make it smart, it doesn't make it a masterpiece. If you want to ponder and reflect on a story, read a goddamn book, don't play this game.

I've been using Blender for 2 years now, and I have to say that it has really improved from what it began as. It is among the ranks of Maya and Zbrush, and to top it all off, it is absolutely free.
The community surrounding this program is absolutely massive and willing to help a beginner stretch their wings and have a good look around. There are a plethora of tutorials available for a beginner online, especially on youtube, so once you learn keys and basic tips, it's relatively simple to interact with.
Even still, I will say that there is one hell of a learning curve. The user interface is in no way beginner friendly. The organization and explanation of the UI is atrocious. Even after using Blender for so long, I'm still learning about different keystrokes and... oh♥♥♥♥♥♥I pressed a button and now the origin tool won't move. Dammit, this is like the fifth time! Thankfully, a lot of issues like that can be solved by a quick google search, but if you prefer to use software that doesn't require you look up a fix for a problem on google, this software isn't for you.
That being said, if you still choose that you want to tackle this tough program, you get some neat benefits. One such benefit is that Blender can be used commercially. If you build a model, it's yours. That .blend file belongs to you, meaning you can profit off of it if you wish. Game developers, animators, and more can make a profit off of their work, which is great.
And another great benefit (stop me if you've heard this already): BLENDER IS FREE. Like, seriously. It's free. 100%. No subscriptions of any kind, it's open-sourced, and you can, once you understand the interface, sculpt literally anything. There are hundreds if not thousands of mods available on the internet that can do something as simple as giving you a better physics engine to something as complex as scripting the growth of ivy all over a newly-modelled house. You can work with logic bricks to code a game, you can sculpt with a variety of brushes, you can even texture paint (a feature that's been updated since 2.74). With hundreds of tutorials, hundreds of helpful community members, thousands of mods, and tons upon tons of public-domain .blend files, this software is honestly one of the nicest I think I've ever used. Constantly updated and improved, and it is absolutely 100% FREE.
TL;DR: This is a great tool, and valuable asset for anyone who has at least some experience with 3D modelling or feels like they can commit to learning how to interact with such a complex UI. 100% free, can be used commercially, and a powerful resource to add to your toolkit.

Ovecooked is an awesome couch co-op game which will test your friendships at times. Kitchens with new players often devolve into shouting matches quickly, but playing with the right people will result in a well-oiled team which needs only minimal communication.
My only gripe with the game is the difficulty: as far as I can tell, the game does not seem to adjust the difficulty to the number of players. This causes some levels to be quite challenging when there are only 3 players, and near impossible with 2 players. On the other hand, some of the more narrow and restricted kitches become easier when leaving players out. The diffuclty isn't really consistent either. In a few select kitches obtaining even a single star can be very hard at times, while other kitchens can be  aced in a single try. The difference between one and three stars isn't very consistent either, sometimes a single dish can push you from one to the other.
While the later levels will probably require you to create a team of more experienced players, the lower levels can be used quite effectively as a party game. Levels are short (+- 3 minutes), controls can be learned quickly and there isn't any hard thinking involved. It's fun to see which of your friends is able to remain calm and which ones become frustrated raging maniacs when things start to go south.
Overall, this is an excellent game and I strongly recommend it to anyone looking for a fun couch co-op game.

In short: It's good, but there are some level design decisions that are baffling and will make you want to snap your controller in half.
There were multiple points during this game where I said to myself, "This is just. The. Worst." In short, it's a competent jump and shoot with amazing music, occasionally gorgeous visuals and a whole lot of content borrowed liberally from other games. Don't misunderstand, I like references in games like this, but there are level designs and boss fights pulled straight from Castlevania and Megaman games, just with different skins. Liebea's stage's first screen is straight up the Elecman starting room from Megaman 1, for example. Especially late in the game, the boss fights are practically clones of Megaman bosses and it's kind of dispiriting.
There are two things that keep this from being great, though. The first is that while this game brings a lot of the wonderful things from classic Megaman back in a cute new outfit, it also brings the absolute worst aspects of retro platformers with it. Precision jumps. Vanishing/appearing blocks. Knockback. Instant death spikes all over the place. Trial-and-error segments. Limited lives. A grid-based password system.
For example. I feel like the ones who get the most out of this game are the ones who were around at least for Megaman 2. Remember that segment late in the Wily Castle where you have to jump down a long shaft lined with spikes across multiple screens? Remember how infuriating it was never to have enough time to react if you were out of position on the previous screen? This game does it twice, the second time in a level where the visuals are so muddy it's even harder to see the stupid things.
The levels are oddly monochromatic in places, which leads to a lot of problems. There are places where the background blends heavily with the foreground because everything is frickin' green, for example. If the background were darkened significantly this wouldn't be an issue, or if there were contrasting colors.
Also, if you buy this game and find the action and player move entirely too fast, check the display options. I had to set the refresh rate to match my monitor before the game would play at a manageable speed. This is the first time I've ever had to manually set that, and it's a little baffling.

I just finished Metro 2033 Redux a while ago, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. One of the best things is that the game is COMPLETELY in a first person perspective, including the cutscenes. Reminded me of Bioshock Infinite a bit in that respect. You are fully immersed in your world. Except for the ending though..for some reason they chose to do a zoomed out pre-rendered cutscene there.
I played on Survival mode (normal difficulty) and the challenge was decent. At one or two points in the game, it wasn't clear to me what to do (probably wasn't paying attention to the dialogues), but I like the no-hand-holding thing. At the last level as well, I ended up running out of filters (pretty sure I scoured all around for supplies and hit the limit many times) so that kinda took away from the experience a bit.
But otherwise, the story was good. Decent enemy variation. Stealth is possible against humans as well (game doesn't explicitly tell you this IIRC). Just make sure you crouch all the time and turn off your flashlight!
Combat was great as well. The weapon handling felt really good. I found a quad-barrel shotgun and that was massive. Killed all Watchmen in a single shot!
Atmosphere was realistic and well done. Performance was great as well on my humble GTX 750 (with medium settings).
It's hard for me to find fault with the game. I went in with little expectation, but then again I also don't play much FPS games. This is definitely better gameplay wise than Bioshock Infinite and Spec Ops: The Line though.

I promised to review this Redux version to a friend of mine, and that is what I will now finally do! Yay. I actually completely forgot to do it, and I feel pretty bad now. I am a huge fan of the Metro games, enough to have earned all their Achievements (yeah, I know, but it's more for me proving my love for their games - not to show off) and played them all through on Ranger Hardcore of course. So here it is, my opinion on how the Redux compares to its original version, Metro 2033...
Yeah, it's good. Visually changed to look more consistent with the style of Last Light (Redux or no), superior optimization on all accounts, replaced all animations on the main character/weapons, and so on. It's also taking away some of the complexity of 2033's stealth rules, while also adding some Last Light monsters and levels, and there's plenty of 'ironing out the rough edges' thing going on here.
So yeah, I absolutely love the Redux version. It's way superior, to me, over the original. But it's still the same game, so many of the owners of the original has very little incentive to actually get it. Recommend this mostly to new, fresh players out there. Don't forget your air filters!

Quake 3. Quake Live.
In my opinion the best arena style multi player first person shooter at the moment.
This is the the game that I always came back to and will come back to.
It's fast paced, furious and unforgiving. Make a mistake and you pay for it.
It is not very newbie friendly and the learning curve is steep.
Often the so called skill gap between players makes it difficult to survive, but that is the challenge.
Even veterans and ace players face this challenge among each other, it's probably why we keep playing Quake.
There are several different game modes:
-CA, Clan Arena, my favourite, sets two teams of players against each other.
You spawn with all weapons and limited ammo, no power ups, ammo or health on the map.
Your goal is to destroy the opposing team.
-CTF, capture the flag, again two teams, extra ammo, health and power ups.
You goal is to capture the enemy flag and bring it home to your flag to score a point.
-TDM, team death match, two teams, health, ammo and power ups.
Your goal is to score more frags on the other team than they do on your team within a certain time limit.
-Duel, two players face off against each other, health, ammo, power ups and weapons spawning on the map.
Your goal is to score most frags within the time limit.
In my opinion the toughest mode because you can only blame yourself if you lose.
-More game modes......
You might like it !
And if not, no harm done and at least you played a few rounds in the best online shooter on the planet.
Good Luck !

FINAL REVIEW: After playing more, my opinion of this game has come to change. I still recommend it, because it is enjoyable, but buy it on sale. Starts as a 10/10, finishes as a solid 7/10.
The mechanics are fantastic. It has the right "feel" for a game that has Scavenger in its name. The storyline is intriguing, and well presented through random newspaper articles. Combat is a treat, taking a break from standard "X ability does Y damage" combat, instead simply treating combat as any other encounter, and allowing you to determine which skills to use each turn. But there is simply not enough to go around.
The beginning of the game feels like you're dipping your toe into a vast, deep, dark lake. But after a while, when you begin to figure things out, you realize that you aren't stepping into a deep dark lake filled with unknown dangers and treasures. No, you are simply looking at a puzzle, with pieces scattered, a system of parts that just need to be put together in the correct order. Don't get me wrong, puzzles can be fun. But they don't have the replayability that I seek from a roguelike. No matter how many times you dump the pieces out in a random order to start with, the end is always the same.
Oh, and speaking of a lake...why no fishing? You can eat a squirrel. You can eat a dog. You can eat a person. But no fish?

After multiple generations of console-only iterations (excluding DOA online) the latest iteration finally has arrived on the PC platform.
Was it worth the wait?
Ignoring the whole fiasco about the whole "last-gen vs next-gen" version let's just take a look at what the game offers and how it (currently) runs/plays.
For those uninformed, the PC version is actually a port of the Arcade version in Japan. It sits somewhere in between the PS3 and the PS4 version.
The big (console-exclusive for now) additions to the next-gen version was having new particle effects and the newly designed Yarakawa engine (the Soft engine) made by TM themselves.
Meaning, the skin has a softer texture to it, breasts moving more "naturally" and/or "realistically"and having better collision with each other and the clothing.
(*Note: the words "naturally" and "realistically" are in quotes, because those are statements are debatable :P)
Also note that this has no impact on the gameplay aspect in any shape (lol) or form, therefore this did not hinder or diminish my overall experience with the game.
Disappointing?
Sure, but I can live without since the vanilla version (Arcades) does not have this feature as well (may change in the future) but let's just move on to the general aspects:
Having played the console versions and now getting my hands on this version, I have to say that I prefer the PC version over the console version. Not only runs it better but with the added options like SSAA everything just looks a lot sharper over the console counterparts. Unfortunately the console versions were also quite buggy which hindered my experience even further. As for this version I have yet to experience a game breaking bug except the camera glitching out sometimes on a very specific spot on a certain level. So quite stable so far.
More importantly TM did a stellar job on the characters. Gone are the plastic looking anime-like looking dolls. They are now redone to portray a more "realistic" representation of aliens. Because in NO way can they be humans or take place on earth.
Every single character in this game is good looking. The females have perfectly curvy figures and their balloons are so appropriately shaped that Jynx and Jigglypuff from Pokemon would throw a hissyfit over!
The males are no slackers either. They either have muscles on their muscles, are also in peak physical condition while not being overly bulky (sleek look) and have the right bulges in the right places that would make your average male question their own manhood.
Now if only the environment would get the same treatment. Not saying they are bad looking by any means but they pale in comparison if it comes to detail of the characters. Sure, some of the stages are better looking than others but still (some have quite some low-res textures on them). Each stage has multiple transitions (complete with Micheal Bay-esque explosions) to another part of the stage which you can trigger during battle by hitting a specific place in the stage.
Overall, not bad but not great either.
Stages deserve your attention next time TM!!
The following options available are:
TBH, a bit bare (compared to say MK9) but just enough for the average user to tweak. At least it is better than FFXIII (which is not saying much).
Performance wise though, the game runs at 60 fps with little to no slowdown.
So overall, not a bad port but not good either. Just average, so your milage may vary (hopefully TM will continue to support and patch this game (lol) for those that are unable to play this game).
Now the most important aspect of a fighting game, the mechanics and how the gameplay feels (I hope you did not buy this game just to stare at melons, there are better options out there!!!).
The game uses the concept of rock-paper-scissors, meaning strikes counter holds, holds counters blocking, counters counter strikes, etc.
It gives the player a lot freedom on how to play each and every character while being accessible to newer players so they don't feel overwhelmed and being deep enough that veteran player has some room to experiment. Spamming the same move or counter over and over again will get you punished if the player is skilled enough!
The character roster is fairly balanced. Though some characters are a "bit" stronger than others *cough* Bass and Bayman, for example.
Having the biggest roster in the DOA franchise finding the right balance is quite difficult anyway (like every fighting game). So IMO they did a pretty good job.
I hope they continue to take in player feedback and keep on improving all the characters.
Just pick your favorite character, learn his/her ins and outs and just play!

Yes....
The online portion of the game is not available yet and will be patched within 3 months as of now, so unfortunately I can't comment about online portion (netcode, lobby system, match making, etc.)
Disappointing?
Yes, for sure. At least it's coming and free. Here is hoping is not as broken as MK9 was (on launch) or having no online at all like BlazBlue Calamity Trigger (Steam version >.>).
We'll just have to wait and see.
Overall, despite lacking the online portion of the game, there is enough content for you SP guys/girls out there.
Having read all of that and taking all my points into account, did that look like something you want to experience for yourselves?
If yes, then go ahead and buy it. You won't regret it.
If you are in doubt, please wait for a sale OR for the online portion to be patched in (ALA the most important aspect of a fighting game :P)
If nothing I described sounded appealing to you, you can pretty much just ignore it. Or play it at a friend (JOIN THE DARK SIDE).
And most importantly, don't forget to have fun. In the end it's just a game :)

This is my initial thought when I start to play this game. Braid is a platformer like many games, but with a gentle touch on the shift key you reverse the flow of time. This enables some really nifty features which is foundation for some really tough puzzles.  And I mean tough, becuse you can probably fix the tardis if you can solve them straight away. The game is divided into six worlds where each one adds a new mechanic to keep the gameplay refreshing.
Visually, it's like playing an oil painting. It's colorful and clear. Level parts and vackground mix together in a beautiful result.
The soundtrack is brilliant. A calming crossover between folk and classical that sets your brain to a mysterious thinking mode.
Epic and soothing, the music is also intgrated in the gameplay in a really smart way (time goes backwards, music plays backwards).
So the verdict.
Should you buy this?
Well, the game is not perfect. Being somewhat short (playthrough around two to three hours) and having a limited replay value is some major setbacks but the good sides greatly makes up for the less perfect sides. Hey, if you want a great puzzle game that really tests your thinking, get this (or atleast consider buying it).
